docs.title: Flux
docs.text:
Flux searches for better designs and keeps only what it can prove. A script, a model or a coding agent makes each design. Flux checks it against your tests, measures the ones that pass with real tools, and picks by your objectives. Use it for RTL on an open 7 nm flow, Python or C code, cache prefetchers, or any program with settings to tune.

  • First loop

    A complete loop from an empty folder, in Python only. No model, no hardware tools.

    First loop →

  • Create a loop in the Preview

    The web app in your browser, on sample data: a guide makes a loop with you, step by step.

    Create a loop →

  • Write a loop with an agent

    Say what you want, attach your files, and let an agent write and check the loop.

    Write a loop with an agent →

docs.title: How a loop works
docs.text:
A loop is a folder: a document (problem.yaml) and the scripts it names. Each pass, Flux:

  1. picks what to try and makes a design;
  2. runs your checks (a failing design is never measured);
  3. runs the measurements, cheapest first;
  4. keeps the design that best meets your objectives.

Every design, number and refusal goes on the record. A run can stop and resume, and every result traces back to what made it.

docs.title: Preview app
docs.text: The preview runs the Flux web app in your browser: it needs JavaScript.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
Write the document (problem.yaml) and the scripts it names, in the web app: the configurator (Settings › Problem › Configurator, or New loop › Configurator) fills it step by step, and Direct edit shows it as YAML. Start from the first loop, an agent's draft (Write a loop with an agent), or New loop › Create or upload. Defaults and allowed values: Document reference.

Where files go (upload them in Files, or write one with New under the configurator's Files):

Folder Holds beside the document The scripts it names library/ Papers and specs knowledge/ Method notes tests/ The gate's tests (hidden from agents) lib/src/<package>/ A Python package the commands import (lib/src is on the Python path)

Check flags any other file no document names: delete it or name it.

docs.title: Define the goal and interface
docs.text:
• statement: the goal.
  • contract: the interface and restrictions (signature or ports, inputs, accuracy, rules).
  • artifact: the design's file name (design.py, design.sv, kernel.cu). Its extension is every design's. RTL presets imply design.sv; with your own scripts, say it (else .txt).
  • Correctness comes from flow.check, not prose.
statement: Find a fast implementation of count_primes(n).
contract: >-
  Export count_primes(n). Return the number of primes strictly below n for
  nonnegative integer n. Do not change the interface or the benchmark.
artifact: design.py

docs.title: Choose how designs are made
docs.text:
Approach Configuration Use it when Script design: {run: "..."} You can render each parameter into a design FluxAgent design: flux You want generated code or algorithms; the default Coding agent design: claude (also codex, opencode) The design needs edits across files or interactive checks Fixed candidates design: {catalog: [...]} You already have artifacts to compare Tune settings A search space, no generator Commands use the chosen settings directly

A script writes {artifact} (its stdout is ignored):

flow:
  design:
    run: ["{python}", "{home}/render.py", "{artifact}", "{block}"]
  • The search supplies {block}. {point} gives the whole point as a JSON file; {vars} your shared settings. See Search and agents.
  • A command is a string or a list. A string is split into arguments, not run by a shell: for a pipeline use a script or bash -c. Use lists when values contain spaces.
  • A command starting with flux uses the loop's own Flux.

docs.title: Build a gate, cheapest check first
docs.text:
Checks run in order; the first failure refuses the design.

flow:
  check:
    build: "{python} -m py_compile {artifact}"
    correctness:
      run: "{python} {home}/check.py {artifact}"
      timeout_s: 120
Result Meaning Any nonzero exit of a check named build Did not build Exit 3 from any check Did not build N failing in the output N failures Otherwise Exit 0 passes; nonzero is one failure

stderr output alone is never a failure. For another output format:

flow:
  check:
    tests:
      run: "{python} {home}/check.py {artifact}"
      count_re: 'failures=(\d+)'
  • count_re captures a failure count; fail_re counts matching lines.
  • Both scan stdout and stderr, and can fail a design that exits 0. Keep debug text distinct.

For RTL, put the ports and reference function in golden.py:

flow:
  check:
    lint: "fluxpreset rtl lint {artifact}"
    golden: "fluxpreset golden {artifact} --golden {home}/golden.py"
  • Golden model: vectors, clocked designs, float tolerances.
  • The configurator offers the built-in checks under Flux presets (a check's Type, a measurement's Tool).

docs.title: Measure surviving designs
docs.text:
Stages run in document order. Put the cheap screen first, the costly one last. A stage prints the metrics it declares (e.g. time_ms=2.31 bytes=2048, on stdout or stderr):

flow:
  measure:
    screen:
      run: "{python} {home}/bench.py {artifact} --quick"
      metrics: [time_ms, bytes]
      cutoff: {metric: bytes, below: 4096}
    confirm:
      run: "{python} {home}/bench.py {artifact} --full"
      metrics: [time_ms, bytes]
      timeout_s: 1800
  • --quick and --full are your benchmark's own flags.
  • A nonzero exit fails the measurement: no numbers taken, the design refused at that stage (kept on the record; ✗ in Live).
  • metrics_re reads another output format.
  • Every stage declares the metrics its objectives need.

Presets (Presets) and needs for required tools:

flow:
  measure:
    screen:
      run: "fluxpreset rtl measure {artifact} --stage synth --clock-ps 1000"
      metrics: [fmax_mhz, area_um2, power_w, cell_count]
      needs: [yosys, openroad]
    confirm:
      run: "fluxpreset rtl measure {artifact} --stage place --clock-ps 1000"
      metrics: [fmax_mhz, area_um2, power_w, cell_count]
      needs: [yosys, openroad]
      timeout_s: 1800

A stage whose needs tool is missing is skipped: check which stage a number came from.

docs.title: Cutoffs and estimates
docs.text:
cutoff decides whether a design goes on: at (minimum), below (maximum), within (a fraction of the best). A list needs all:

cutoff:
  - {metric: fmax_mhz, at: 1000}
  - {metric: area_um2, below: 80}

estimate screens before paying for the tool:

estimate: {kind: surrogate, margin: 0.05}
  • The surrogate uses earlier measurements at that stage (at least three).
  • A design estimated outside a cutoff or limit by more than margin skips the stage.
  • Estimates are not measurements. Command and model estimators: reference.

docs.title: Define what wins
docs.text:
An objective with goal is a limit; without, a preference:

objectives:
  - {metric: fmax_mhz, direction: maximize, goal: 1000}
  - {metric: area_um2, direction: minimize, goal: 80}
  - {metric: power_w, direction: minimize}
  • Here: at least 1000 MHz, at most 80 µm², then least power.
  • Preferences are compared in written order.
  • A goal uses the deepest stage unless stage names another.
  • If nothing meets every limit, the report shows the closest design and its shortfall; no decision artifact is written.
  • balance: true on several goal-less objectives picks the frontier's knee.
  • A relative limit: {metric: speedup, direction: maximize, keep: 0.9, above: 1.0} keeps 90% of the best gain over the baseline.

docs.title: Control time and concurrency
docs.text:
budget:
  passes: 10
  repairs_per_design: 6
  designs_at_once: 1
  tools_at_once: 1
Key Bounds passes The run (one design per pass; omit or 0 to run until stopped) repairs_per_design Attempts to fix one design designs_at_once Designs made at once (passes: 6, designs_at_once: 3: six designs, three at a time) tools_at_once Tool runs at once across the loop: checks, measurements, agent probes
  • Keep timings isolated with tools_at_once: 1.
  • On a server, the admin must allow parallel work, else the server's cap wins. Configurator: Extra › Running (links to Settings › Preferences › Advanced).
  • Meeting a goal or a stalled search does not end an unlimited run (Run, stop, resume).
  • More: budget reference.

Configurator, Graph step: Runs as Passes | Trunk. Trunk writes trunk: instead of flow: (passes or a trunk).

  • Design gives each agent its own Model, Thinking and effort; + Add an agent adds one (the same agent with another model too: by: [claude, {by: claude, model: opus}]).
  • Under Trunk, Extra › Running's Designs at once counts branches (twice that may wait), and Search becomes a bud every 10 designs when an agent works it.
  • Back to Passes, Design keeps its first agent and model.
  • The switch is disabled, naming why, when trunk mode cannot run the loop (a parameter search, Plan, Design not by a coding agent).

docs.title: Add context and reusable settings
docs.text:
vars: {input_size: 1000000, repetitions: 9}
flow:
  knowledge:
    library: [spec.md, reference.py]
    hidden: [check.py]
  • vars reaches scripts as the {vars} JSON file.
  • knowledge.library joins the library, which agents read on demand.
  • knowledge.hidden hides the gate's files from agents.
  • More: Knowledge, skills, hidden paths.

Then Settings › Problem › Check, and Start with one pass (Run, stop, resume).

docs.title: Recipes
docs.text: Which loop shape fits which problem. Start with New loop in the web app: an empty loop, an agent's draft, or a folder or .zip dropped on Create or upload. The examples' documents are in the public repository's examples/ folder; their scripts come with the source.

docs.title: Tune a program's settings
docs.text:
statement: The fastest block size and thread count for my kernel.
flow:
  search:
    method: sweep
    space:
      block: [16, 32, 64, 128, 256]
      threads: [1, 2, 4, 8]
  check: "{python} {home}/check.py {block} {threads}"
  measure:
    bench:
      run: "{home}/run.sh --block {block} --threads {threads}"
      metrics: [time_ms]
objectives: [{metric: time_ms, direction: minimize}]
budget: {tools_at_once: 1}
  • Time alone: budget.tools_at_once: 1, and pin the program's own threads. Side-by-side runs distort timings. Checks share the same slots.
  • Keep the gate: a setting that crashes or is wrong is refused before it is timed.
  • A knob is a placeholder: {block} works in any command.

docs.title: Choose a search for the space
Trade-offs and limits
docs.text:
• One limit, then the rest: a goal on the first objective; the next decides among those that meet it ("the smallest that makes 1 GHz").
  • A true trade-off: two goal-less objectives and pareto. balance: true picks the knee.
  • A hard cost limit: a check, a stage cutoff, or a search's floor ({metric: storage_bytes, at: 98304}).

docs.title: When a model writes the designs
docs.text:
• Often wrong: give it facts in flow.knowledge (spec, reference code, method note) and skills. The loop's Agents tab shows what it was told and said.
  • Numeric hardware (floating point, transcendentals, fixed point): a golden model and design.prototype: true. The algorithm is proven in Python on every input, then spelled as RTL. A prototype over its cost ceiling (default 2,000) is made cheaper first.
  • A coding agent: flow.design: claude (or codex, opencode). A failed gate goes back to the same session. With a prototype stage it writes the prototype.
  • Let it run: a run goes on until stopped; each start resumes from the record.
  • Steer it: Overview › Note to the loop, or ask about it in the loop's Chat.

docs.title: Read the results
docs.text:
• Overview: the decision, the best designs, the best so far.
  • Results: every design ranked, the front, compare designs side by side (Results).
  • Agents: every model and agent turn.

docs.title: Knowledge, skills, hidden paths
docs.text: What the loop's model and agents can read besides the document, and what they may not. Fields: Document reference › Knowledge.

docs.title: Files, notes and papers
docs.text:
flow:
  knowledge:
    library: [spec.md, reference.py, notes/]
    by: claude
    insights: {by: rules}
Key Does library Files and folders added to the loop's library/ (a folder counts as each of its files) by Who summarises the papers: flux (FluxAgent, default) or an agent; off turns all reading off insights {by: rules}: facts from the results, no AI; {by: <agent>}: conclusions citing designs; unset or {by: off}: none
  • Agents read the library on demand, in pieces. Nothing is pasted into prompts. Hidden paths never appear.
  • Papers are summarised in each pass's Setup, before its design. An unsummarised paper is read whole.
  • You read the library, its digests and outlines in Files › Library. The agents read the insights with it.
  • A linked project adds its library read-only at library/<project>@<group>/, while the loop's owner is a member.

A project's knowledge (web app, the project's Knowledge tab): one insight per entry, each under a topic and proven by designs, added by hand or proposed by the collector.

  • A linked loop's agents read accepted entries with the library (pinned first), as they stood at its start.
  • Each accepted entry becomes an idea in every linked loop's notebook ("from silicon@hw-lab"), scored like any other. A global project's entries need the link's learning on.
  • A retired entry's idea is marked for deletion.
  • More: Groups › Knowledge.

Tip: a model that keeps getting it wrong usually lacks a fact. A method note (the method and the facts, not a design) helps more than more passes.

docs.title: How agents read the library
docs.text:
The library (the loop's and its projects') is read in pieces, never pasted whole: a list of every document (name, pages or lines, what it is) and each linked project's topics; a search returning the nearest files with their digests and best passages; a document's digest, its outline, one section, the passages around a phrase, or a range of lines or pages; one project entry; the insights so far.

  • Names: the path in library/ (booth.md, papers/x.pdf, silicon@hw-lab/x.pdf).
  • Outline: from headings (Markdown #, LaTeX \section, PDF numbered and usual headings); else by page, or 120-line chunks. Files › Library shows the same outline and digest.
  • Formats: text; PDF; Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OpenDocument, HTML and EPUB as Markdown-like text.
  • Title: an HTML <title> or EPUB title, else the file name.
  • Hidden paths are refused.

docs.title: Skills
docs.text:
A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md (front matter name and description, then instructions) and its files. Skills in the loop's skills/ folder are used automatically by the model and every coding agent. The built-in flux-loop-commands skill comes with them.

skills: [skills, ../shared-skills]           # these folders instead of skills/
skills: {"off": [flux-loop-commands]}        # skills/ and the built-in one, this one off
skills: "off"                                # none at all
  • In the web app: the configurator's Knowledge Skills bubble (Settings › Problem › Configurator › Graph) turns skills on or off and lists them.
  • A project's skills (its Skills tab) reach linked loops at skills/<name>@<group>/, read-only, after the loop's own. Turn them off the same way.

docs.title: Hidden from AI
docs.text:
An agent that can read the tests can write a design that passes only them. knowledge.hidden hides paths from the loop's agents:

flow:
  knowledge:
    hidden: [tests/, golden.py, "params/*.json"]
  • Checks, measurements and scripts still read them; a check's failure text still reaches the agent.
  • Paths are relative to the loop folder. An agent's own hidden: adds paths for that agent.
  • Not a security boundary: for secrets, use the sandbox.
  • Chat can read hidden files to answer you; the loop's agents cannot.

Hide a path in the web app:

  • Files: a file's Actions › Hide from AI;
  • configurator Graph: the Knowledge group's Hidden bubble;
  • New loop › Agent: Hide from AI on a file.

A hidden path shows a lock before its name. Point at it to see hidden from AI or the pattern that hides it.

docs.title: Ideas cleanup
docs.text:
The ideas notebook holds each hypothesis and the designs that tested it. knowledge.ideas says who merges duplicates, in a pass's Setup. Default: FluxAgent.

flow:
  knowledge:
    insights: {by: rules}
    ideas: claude                        # an agent; or {by: flux, open: 30, new: 15, timeout_s: 300}; or off
  • When: in a pass's Setup, at most one cleanup each (under trunk:, in a setup bud beside the designs, never before the first one), once there are open open ideas (default 20) and new new or updated ones (default 10) and 5 designs were tried since the last cleanup; also, at open ideas, at the first cleanup after a start and again right after a cleanup that merged or marked at least 3 ideas and a tenth of those it looked at (in the next pass's Setup; under trunk:, at once in the same setup bud) -- at most 5 in a row. The log says what the next waits for (ideas cleanup: merged 2 of 60 -- the next waits for 10 new or changed ideas and 5 designs tried); Live shows Setup · ideas with why it waits; after 5 in a row, a quiet notice under the head says the cleanup is paused until enough is new or changed, or the next start.
  • How much: 60 ideas per cleanup, new ones first, then those looked at longest ago; a growing notebook gets more cleanups, not bigger ones. The log shows progress (ideas cleanup: 60 of 650 not yet reviewed). Under trunk:, Run setup cleans the rest.
  • How long: one cleanup works 5 minutes at most (timeout_s; an agent's own timeout_s is its limit). Then it stops: its merges stay, the rest waits for the next cleanup, which has half as many ideas (ideas cleanup: cut at its time limit ...).
  • What: merges ideas that say the same thing (nothing is deleted; evidence moves to the kept idea); may set a new idea's priority; may mark an unusable idea for deletion, saying which kind: off the problem, self-contradictory, against a constraint, empty or garbled (never a tried, queued or near-duplicate one).
  • Suggestion: with nothing queued, a pass may take the best unmeasured idea (Live: suggested idea). ideas: {suggest: false} turns this off.
  • See merges: Results › Ideas folds merged ideas under the kept one (×N). "idea 7" is an idea; "#7" is a design.
  • Delete: the bin in Results › Ideas; Undo restores it.
  • Marked for deletion: a person accepts or rejects the mark in Results › Ideas.
  • Turn it off: ideas: off (or {by: off}). Web app: the Graph's Knowledge Ideas bubble.

docs.title: Workbench
docs.text:
workbench/ is the agents' own folder: tools and notes, shared by the loop's agents, kept across runs.

  • knowledge.workbench: who summarises it into README.md (off, flux, or an agent; default: the paper summariser).
  • The README is rewritten in a pass's Setup when the workbench changed.
  • Web app: Files › Workbench. The library: Files › Library.

docs.title: Setup steps
docs.text:
Each pass runs three steps in its Setup, before its design:

Step Key Runs Paper summaries knowledge.by While papers are new (8 a pass) Workbench README knowledge.workbench When the workbench changed Ideas cleanup knowledge.ideas Past the thresholds; one at most a pass, 5 minutes at most

A step whose papers or workbench files did not change since it last ran is skipped.

  • Passes at once take each step one at a time; the next finds what the one before wrote.
  • With pipeline, the next pass's Setup runs while the last design is checked and measured.
  • Live's Timeline shows them on the Setup row as the pass's Setup. Under trunk: they are setup buds: the first bud of a start runs the papers, the README and the cleanup beside the first designs, so those read the previous README and summaries (none on a first start).

docs.title: Search and agents
docs.text:
Choose what to try next (flow.search) and who makes the design (flow.design). Checks, measurements and objectives stay the same whichever you pick.

The configurator's Graph draws the loop as a ring. Each box is a key under flow: (or trunk:):

Box Key Does Search search Picks what to try Design design Makes it Check check Tests it; a failure goes back to Design Measure measure Measures it Choose choose Decides

The setup boxes beside the ring run in each pass's Setup, before its design (Setup steps).

docs.title: Search a space of settings
docs.text:
List the choices; commands get them as placeholders.

flow:
  search:
    method: sweep
    space:
      algorithm: [list_sieve, slice_sieve, odd_sieve]
      wheel: [0, 1]
    seeds:
      - {algorithm: list_sieve, wheel: 0}
  design: {run: "{python} {home}/render.py {artifact} {algorithm} {wheel}"}
  • Seeds are measured first. The first seed is the home point.
  • An omitted knob takes its first choice.
  • Order numeric choices: local searches move along that order.
search How it chooses One pass carries Learns from results sweep Every distinct combination Every point (batch_size for fewer) No montecarlo Random distinct points batch_size points (8) No gradient Coordinate descent over nearby choices A wave of moves (all, or wave) After each pass anneal Local moves, sometimes accepting worse One neighbour After each pass genetic Selection and mutation A generation, population (8) After each pass pareto Trade-offs; needs two objectives Up to wave points After each pass by: flux beside the space, no search FluxAgent (or by: claude, an agent) proposes legal points batch_size points (4) After each pass control The home point with some incumbent knobs (keep: [...]) One point phases Several searches in order The current phase's As that phase run Your script: search: {run: "...", timeout_s: 600} (contract) What it prints in one round After each pass
  • Passes (at Start, or budget.passes) count proposals, not points: one sweep pass over 48 points measures 48.
  • budget.designs_at_once: how many of a pass's designs are made and checked at once.
  • With designs at once or pipeline, each design is decided as soon as it is measured; a slow or repaired one holds up no other's decision.
  • A finished search does not stop an unlimited run. Cap the passes for a bounded sweep.
  • Designs climb the stages cheapest first; only cutoffs stop a design early (between stages).
  • A re-check (Measure again, a re-evaluation, Evaluate on a probed draft) is a pass of its own between two passes (R, numbered 1.5 after pass 1). It does not count in budget.passes.
  • With several designs at once, a draft you Evaluate while passes run does not wait for them: it takes the next free lane like a pass (R 2.5, beside the passes), is checked, measured and decided, and that lane's next pass starts after it.

A search's options go under its name (search reference):

flow:
  search:
    method:
      gradient: {steps: 16, patience: 2, reach: adjacent}
    space:
      block: [16, 32, 64, 128]
      order: [ijk, ikj, jki]

Phases: a list, each {search: ..., <its options>}; policy: sets a phase's emphasis.

flow:
  search:
    space: {block: [16, 32, 64, 128], order: [ijk, ikj, jki]}
    method:
      - {search: montecarlo, name: sample, samples: 8, seed: 0}
      - {search: gradient, name: tune, knobs: [block], steps: 8, policy: tune}

docs.title: Conditional choices and components
docs.text:
A knob that only matters for some choices (inactive knobs stay at home and are not measured again):

space:
  algorithm: [list_sieve, slice_sieve, odd_sieve]
  wheel: {values: [0, 1], when: {algorithm: [list_sieve]}}

A component groups knobs; the search sees prefetch.on, prefetch.distance, prefetch.degree, and {point} gives them as nested JSON:

space:
  prefetch:
    optional: true
    distance: [1, 2, 4]
    degree: [1, 2]

from: "out/invented/*.sv" beside values adds the files found when the document loads.

docs.title: Let a model or agent explore designs
docs.text:
No knob space needed. by says who picks the next direction (unset: the rules), policy the emphasis, design who writes the code:

flow:
  search: {by: claude, policy: adaptive}
  design: claude
  • policy: adaptive (default), explore, improve, tune, finetune, variations.
  • search: <algorithm> needs a space and decides alone (by has no effect beside it).
  • In the configurator: the Graph's Search box, with Policy, then Parameters (the knobs and Search by: an algorithm, or AI).
  • Only the budget or a manual stop ends an unlimited run; meeting a goal does not.

docs.title: Put agents in the right steps
docs.text:
Name an agent; use {by: ..., ...} to add options:

flow:
  search: {by: claude, policy: adaptive}
  plan: {by: claude, session: pass}
  design: {by: claude, timeout_s: 1800, probe: {gate: 20, stages: 3}}
  choose: {by: claude}
  knowledge: {by: claude, insights: {by: rules}}
  • Built in: claude, codex, opencode. A server can add more.
  • Agents plan, design and advise. flow.check and flow.measure stay commands.
  • The pick still follows the objectives; an agent's advice is checked and can fall back to the rules.
  • FluxAgent: search: {by: flux, policy: adaptive}, design: flux (model is refused). Setup: Models and agents.

Critics give a second opinion on search, check, measure or choose: critic: flux, an agent, or {by: ..., rounds: N}. A rejection re-picks the direction, fails the design, marks the numbers, or re-makes the pick. Details: critics.

flow:
  check:
    correctness: "{python} {home}/check.py {artifact}"
    critic: claude
  choose: {critic: {by: flux, rounds: 2}}

Sessions, by default:

  • design: one session per design until admitted (repairs included), from a warm start.
  • plan and critics: one per pass (session: pass), each critic its own.
  • session: keep: across passes (below).
  • Paper digests, workbench and ideas: no session.

Probes: an agent can run its current file through the gate and stages during a turn. probe budgets them; allow gives back restricted tools (agent options).

Probed drafts an agent did not hand in are kept as unverified (#p4.1, #p4.2: pass 4, try 1 and 2). They never count. Evaluate (Results) measures one in the next re-check, or, with designs at once, at the next free lane.

docs.title: Several Design agents
docs.text:
List coding agents; passes take turns (pass 1 the first, pass 2 the second, and round again):

flow:
  design:
    by:
      - claude
      - {by: codex, model: gpt-5-codex, effort: high}
      - {by: opencode, model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5}
    timeout_s: 900
  • An entry is a name or {by: <agent>, ...}. model: (or args: [--model, <model>]) sets its model. Design's options apply to all; an entry's own win.
  • With designs_at_once, each starting pass takes the next agent. The order survives a restart.
  • A design stays with its agent: repairs and continued turns too.
  • Each agent has its own warm start and kept sessions.
  • design.prototype is written by the first agent.
  • Refused: an empty list, the same agent with the same options twice, FluxAgent in a list.
  • Live's Timeline and the Agents tab name each turn's agent; Results tags each design's agent once two or more made designs.
  • Configurator: Graph › Design › Add an agent; a tab per agent.

docs.title: Warm starts
docs.text:
By default a Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode design starts warm (session: seeded). Before the first design, one turn studies the loop (document, scripts, checks, stages, baseline, best design) and writes notes. Every design then starts from that session.

flow:
  design: {by: claude}                        # warm starts (the default)
  design: {by: claude, session: fresh}        # every design's session starts from nothing
  design: {by: claude, seed_timeout_s: 1800}     # warm starts, that first turn at most 30 minutes
  design: {by: claude, reseed_after_bests: 3}    # made again after every 3 new best designs (7 unsaid, 0 never)
  • Limit: seed_timeout_s, 300 to 10800 s (default 3600). It ends early when done. Past the limit, designs start from nothing.
  • Runs in the pass's Setup; no design starts before it ends. With several designs at once, the others wait for it.
  • Made again when the document, the loop's files, the agent or its model change; after 24 designs; after 12 hours; after reseed_after_bests new bests (default 7, 0 to 100; 0 never).
  • Reads out/ and the workbench but cannot write them. This needs Linux 5.13+ with Landlock; without it, every design starts from nothing.
  • Fails: that design starts from nothing; the Agents tab says why.
  • Refused with session: fresh or keep, and on other boxes.
  • FluxAgent and run: agents always start fresh.
  • A warm design is told its own task and the loop's record, not the loop's files and tools again: that first turn learned them.
  • Live shows the turn on the Setup row. Each design's turn in Live says how its session began: a warm start, or a new one and why. The Agents tab marks them too.

docs.title: Sessions kept across passes
docs.text:
session: keep keeps an agent's session from pass to pass (any box, or a critic):

flow:
  design: {by: codex, session: keep}            # a new session after 8 turns
  plan: {by: claude, session: keep, turns: 4}
  search: {by: claude, session: keep, turns: forever}        # never renewed for its turns
  • turns: N (default 8) renews after N turns; turns: forever never does.
  • A change to the document, agent, model or Flux starts a new session.
  • One session per design at once.
  • An agent of your own keeps sessions only with a resume command (agent options).
  • The Agents tab says whether each turn resumed.

docs.title: Two ways to run: passes or a trunk
docs.text:
The root key picks the mode. Everything else (checks, stages, objectives, knowledge) is written the same.

Passes (flow:) Trunk (trunk:) Each design Search, Design, Check, Measure, Choose; a failed check is repaired A coding agent hands in one design per turn; branches check, measure and decide it Agent session Per pass or per design One for the whole run Use for A search over a space, scripts, plans, FluxAgent, steering pass by pass A coding agent that keeps going on its own, one or several 
trunk:
  design: {by: [claude], timeout_s: 3600}     # a list: one trunk each (one agent is fine)
  check: {...}                                 # as under flow:
  measure: {...}
budget:
  designs_at_once: 3                          # branches at once (the admin's limit applies); twice that may wait
  passes: 0                                   # designs handed in; 0 = until stopped
  • Trunk: each Design agent keeps one session, resumed at the next start. One turn, one design (at most design.timeout_s). A turn with no design is followed by the next. An agent without resume: starts each design fresh.
  • Branches: up to budget.designs_at_once take designs first in, first out, whoever made each (a design a stop sent back goes first). A branch runs Check, Measure and Choose; no Search, Design or repair.
  • Queue: up to twice the branches wait (or twice the admin's lower limit). Lowering designs_at_once keeps what already waits.
  • Ideas: each turn is told the queued idea, else the best unmeasured one (ideas: {suggest: false} turns that off). A design names the idea it tests.
  • Notes to the loop reach each agent every turn while they stand.
  • Search is off by default. search: flux or an agent adds a bud every 10 decided designs that writes up to 5 new ideas, within its agent's time limit (search: {by: claude, timeout_s: 1800}; unset, the agent's own; FluxAgent 15 minutes). A repeated idea shows proposed again ×N; the count changes nothing. The run's log says at its start whether Search buds run and why not when off (Search buds: off -- Search is the rules; ...), and when the next is due (Search buds: on -- one every 10 decided designs (Search: claude); the next when 30 are decided (24 now, ...)).
  • Ideas cleanup (knowledge.ideas) runs in a setup bud once the notebook grows; the cleanups that follow a productive one run in the same bud, one after the other.
  • Repairs are the agent's own; repairs_per_design does nothing.
  • Setup runs once at start, with no paper summaries, workbench README or ideas cleanup: the start's first setup bud runs those beside the trunks. Run setup on Live or a library change runs a bud again.
  • Start: the baseline if asked, then the re-check, then Setup and the trunks.
  • Refused: a space or search, plan, a Design not by a coding agent, both flow: and trunk:, design: {session: trunk} under flow:.
  • design.prototype does not run; Check warns.
  • Several agents: each is a trunk (t1, t2, ...). The same agent twice with different models is two trunks:
trunk:
  design: {by: [claude, {by: claude, model: opus}, codex], timeout_s: 3600}

docs.title: One loop, one design
docs.text: A loop answers one problem with one design. Several blocks of one IP are one design under one top module (as the bundled nlu). Several problems are several loops; a chart can compare them.

docs.title: Models and agents
docs.text:
Flux uses two kinds of AI, configured separately:

  • FluxAgent (flux in a document; model is an old name for it): Flux's own model on any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. It proposes points, writes designs (design: flux), reviews, and digests papers.
  • Coding agents: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, or one a server adds. Each has its own endpoint, model and login.

A loop with only script designs needs neither. All of it is set in the web app: the server's settings in Admin › Runtime › Agents, a group's in its Agents tab, yours in Account › Agents. They layer field by field: server, then your groups, then yours (A group's agents).

docs.title: FluxAgent
docs.text:
Admin › Runtime › Agents › FluxAgent (or your own tab in Account › Agents): the endpoint (any OpenAI-compatible server: Ollama, LocalAI, vLLM, llama.cpp, a hosted service), the model, the key, seconds per turn and token prices. Keys are encrypted and shown only as "set". Test asks it one short question.

  • With no endpoint set, FluxAgent uses a local Ollama.
  • A service that refuses structured output: turn off Structured answers (Thinking by default).
  • A model on CPU takes minutes per turn: use a GPU or a smaller model, and raise the seconds per turn for long tool turns.
  • Never put keys in a loop's document.

Without any setting in the web app, the server uses the configuration of the machine it runs on (its environment, each agent's own files).

docs.title: Coding agents
docs.text:
An agent's program must be on the server (the Nix shell has Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode). Each user logs in under Account › Agents: a tab per agent with its login (in a small terminal, in the sandbox), Test, model and variables. An agent is used only once its Test passed for whoever starts the loop.

  • Admin › Runtime › Agents shows each agent installed or missing, its version, and its server-wide settings: Program, endpoint, model, key, seconds per turn, turns at once, Enabled, Thinks by default, instructions.
  • + Add agent: another agent of a kind (OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex) with its own program, label and arguments; documents name it as the built-in ones.
  • Model: an agent without an endpoint lists its own models (From the agent); a document's model: ({by: codex, model: gpt-5-codex}) wins over every setting.
  • Without settings of its own, an agent uses its own configuration and login. Its card says "not configured" when it has neither.
  • FluxAgent's settings never apply to an agent.

OpenCode on your own server: in OpenCode's configuration read the key as "apiKey": "{env:FLUX_AGENT_API_KEY}", and set the key on OpenCode's tab. Give the model's real limits and keep reasoning short, or turns can end empty:

"models": {"MODEL": {"limit": {"context": 58112, "output": 16384},
                     "options": {"reasoningEffort": "low"}}}

Also set "timeout": 1800000 in the provider's options.

probe, allow, timeout_s and the rest: Agent options.

docs.title: Which model for which problem
docs.text:
The loop keeps what passes; it does not make a weak model strong. A mid-size model writes a correct Python loop or small adder. Hard numeric hardware (a float function within 1 ULP) needs:

  • a prototype stage (design.prototype: true with a golden model): proven in Python, then spelled as RTL;
  • a method note in flow.knowledge: the method and facts, not a design;
  • a stronger model, or a coding agent, writing the prototype.

docs.title: When something goes wrong
docs.text:
• No answer: a run checks its endpoint first and stops before pass 1 if it is down, refuses the key or lacks the model. Settings › Problem › Check shows the same; an agent's Test says what failed.
  • Read the turns: a loop's Agents tab shows every turn's prompt, reply, tool calls and error (Live › The inspector for one task).
  • Timeouts: raise the seconds per turn (FluxAgent) or timeout_s (an agent's box).
  • Context: an agent past its context window continues in a fresh session; raise the window if you can.

docs.title: Document
docs.text: Every key of a loop's document, problem.yaml. Why to choose each: Configure. Validate with Settings › Problem › Check in the web app.

docs.title: The document at a glance
docs.text:
Only statement is required. A complete document:

statement: Count the primes below n, as fast as possible.  # (1)!
contract: >-  # (2)!
  A Python module defining count_primes(n) that returns
  exactly how many primes are below n.
artifact: design.py

flow:  # (3)!
  search:
    method: sweep
    space: {method: [trial_division, sieve, slice_sieve]}
  design:
    run: "{python} {home}/render.py {artifact} {method}"
  check:  # (4)!
    build: "{python} -m py_compile {artifact}"
    correctness:
      run: "{python} {home}/check.py {artifact}"
      timeout_s: 60
  measure:  # (5)!
    quick:
      run: "{python} {home}/bench.py {artifact} 50000"
      metrics: [time_ms]
      cutoff: {metric: time_ms, below: 20}
    full:
      run: "{python} {home}/bench.py {artifact} 1000000"
      metrics: [time_ms]

objectives:  # (6)!
  - {metric: time_ms, direction: minimize, goal: 20}

budget: {passes: 5, tools_at_once: 1}  # (7)!
vars: {n_max: 1000000}    # (8)!
  1. What to make. The only required field.
  2. Rules every design must follow: names, ports, what is forbidden.
  3. Who does each box of the loop: here a search over three methods, and a script that writes each design (flow settings).
  4. The checks, in order; the first that fails refuses the design (check settings).
  5. The measurements, cheapest first. cutoff decides which designs go on to the next stage (measurement settings).
  6. What decides. A goal makes an objective a limit: here at most 20 ms (objectives).
  7. How much to spend (budget).
  8. Your own settings, handed to every command as the {vars} file.

docs.title: Files and loading
docs.text:
• The folder is the loop. Its name is the id: letters, digits, _, -, and . after the first character; at most 60. An id key is refused.
  • The document: problem.yaml (or problem.yml, problem.json). Alternates: NAME.problem.yaml, each with its own results.
  • Beside it: your scripts, library/ (papers, notes), workbench/ (agents' tools and notes), skills/, out/ (results).
  • Parsing: errors give line and column. Unknown keys are refused with a "did you mean" hint.
  • Normal form: equivalent spellings (plan: flux, plan: {by: flux}) share one record.

docs.title: Document fields
docs.text: Field Values / default Purpose statement Required non-empty string What to build or optimize contract String; empty Interface and rules every design must follow (names, ports, what is forbidden) artifact A file name; from the tools, else design.txt The design's file name: its extension is the designs' (below) flow Map; defaults below Who does each step: search, generation, checks, measurements, and the supporting boxes trunk Map; unset The loop run as a trunk instead of passes, in place of flow with the same contents: Design's by may list agents objectives List; empty Limits and ordered preferences (objectives) budget Map; defaults below Run length, repairs, concurrency, prototypes (budget) vars Map; empty Your own settings, handed to any command as the {vars} JSON file skills off, a folder or list of folders, or {from, off}; skills/ Skills (a folder with SKILL.md) the model and agents can load (skills) needs Map; unset The default resource hint of every check and stage that says none baseline true, false, or a map; absent A reference measured before pass 1 (baseline)

docs.title: The design's file
docs.text:
• artifact: a plain file name with an extension (design.py, design.sv, kernel.cu, top.scala); no folder, not hidden. Every design gets that extension.
  • Unsaid: Flux's RTL presets imply design.sv; otherwise design.txt. Say it with your own scripts.
  • language instead names only the language (language: python is design.py). Not both.

docs.title: Flow settings
docs.text:
flow says who does each box of the loop's drawing. A box takes a word, an agent's name, or {by: <word or agent>, ...settings, ...agent options}:

flow:
  design: claude                                # an agent, no options
  choose: {by: claude, session: pass}           # an agent with options
  plan: flux                                    # FluxAgent
  notes: off                                    # a word
  • flux is FluxAgent (Models and agents); model is refused.
  • claude, codex, opencode are built in; a server adds others (**Admin › Runtime › Agents ›
  • Add agent**).
  • {agent: X} is refused: write {by: X}.
Box Values (first is the default) Purpose flow.search.by unset (the rules, no AI), flux, tools, agent Who decides what to try next (given is the rules, under that name) flow.search.policy adaptive (default), explore, improve, tune, finetune, variations Sets the search's emphasis flow.search.method unset, sweep, montecarlo, anneal, gradient, genetic, pareto, {gradient: {...}}, module:Class, a list of phases How the points of space are picked (search settings) flow.search.run A command, with timeout_s (600) Your own search script proposes the points (search command) flow.search.scope {list: ..., brief: ..., check: ..., timeout_s: 120} The scopes of one whole design a pass may work on (scope) flow.plan off, flux, agent Write the pass's plan, checked before use flow.design flux, agent, a list of agents, {run: ...}, {catalog: [paths]} Write each design flow.check A command, or an ordered map of named checks; never an agent Decide correctness (checks) flow.measure An ordered map of named stages; never an agent Put numbers on passing designs (measurements) flow.choose unset (the objectives choose), agent Make the decision; an agent only breaks ties flow.notes unset (your notes are read), off Read the notes you send from the loop's Overview (Note to the loop) flow.knowledge A map (knowledge): library, by (who digests, or off), insights, ... What the model and agents can look up

Each key is its box in the configurator's Graph (search is Search, knowledge Knowledge, ...).

  • search: {by, policy, method, space}.
    • by: unset (the rules, no AI), flux, tools (FluxAgent with tools: standings, history, decisions, knowledge), or an agent.
    • method picks the points of space and decides alone. A space with by and no method: by proposes the points.
    • A search word under policy: (or a policy under method:) is refused naming the right key.
    • Shorthand: search: explore is {policy: explore}, search: sweep {method: sweep}, search: claude {by: claude}.
  • search.scope (one whole design, no knobs): each pass works on one scope.
    • list: a command printing the scopes, one per line, name first.
    • brief (given {scope}): what the design agent is told.
    • check (given {scope}, {artifact}): checks the scope after the gate (N failing of M, or its exit). While it fails, the design goes back to the agent, within tries_per_pass.
    • The orchestrator picks direction and scope together, seeing recent scopes and results.
    • For a spec in the folder: list: fluxpreset ndf list --spec {home}/spec, brief: fluxpreset ndf clauses {scope} --spec {home}/spec; fluxpreset ndf scope {scope} --spec {home}/spec lists a unit and its dependents.
  • design, one form:
    • {run: ...}: your script (generator contract); no timeout_s of its own (uses the largest check timeout).
    • {catalog: [a.py, b.py]}: the listed files in turn.
    • flux or an agent. by may list coding agents, taking turns ({by: [claude, {by: codex, model: gpt-5-codex}]}; several Design agents).
    • session: seeded (default; warm start), fresh (also pass), or keep.
  • session: seeded (Design only; default for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode): one first turn studies the loop in the pass's Setup; each design starts from it (Warm starts). seeded and fresh are refused on other boxes.
    • seed_timeout_s: that turn's limit (default 3600, 300 to 10800): {by: claude, seed_timeout_s: 1800}.
    • reseed_after_bests: redo it after this many new bests (default 7, 0 to 100, 0 never): {by: claude, reseed_after_bests: 3}.
    • Both are refused without the warm start.
  • session: keep (with turns: K, default 8, or turns: forever) on any agent box or critic: kept across passes. Refused on the papers' digester. {by: codex, session: keep, turns: 4}, {by: claude, session: keep, turns: forever}.
  • check and measure never take by:.
  • choose: {by: claude}: an agent breaks ties the objectives cannot.
  • plan is checked before use; a failing plan falls back to the document's order.
  • Thinking: think: true or false beside whoever works a box.
    • FluxAgent (search, plan, design, critics of check/measure/choose, knowledge and its workbench, ideas): {by: flux, think: true} reasons first (slower, often better).
    • An agent (any box, critic or Knowledge section): {by: claude, think: false} runs at its not-thinking effort, true at its thinking effort (the admin's). Refused for a run agent. An agent's effort (agent options) wins over think.
    • Unsaid: the server's thinking by default.
    • {by: tools, think: true} for Search with tools; Search's AI points: search: {by: flux, think: true, effort: high, space: {...}}.
    • Configurator: Thinking (default, on, off) and effort under each chosen agent.
  • Effort (FluxAgent): effort: low | medium | high | max beside by: flux sets thinking, work time and answer length at once; max also checks its own answer. Comes before think. Unsaid: the admin's default.
flow:
  search: {by: flux, think: true}             # FluxAgent reasons over what to try next
  plan: {by: flux, effort: max}                # works hardest and checks its own plan
  design: {by: codex, think: false}           # the design agent at its effort for not thinking
  choose: {by: claude, effort: high}          # the finer level, as it is
  check: {check: "true", critic: {by: flux, think: true}}         # the critic reasons before it judges
  knowledge: {by: flux, effort: high, ideas: {by: flux, think: false}}   # papers, and the ideas cleanup

docs.title: Critics
docs.text:
A critic is a second opinion on one box, said as critic: inside it. Only four boxes take one:

Box What the critic judges A rejection rounds search The direction picked for a pass, before any design work is spent on it The direction is picked again with the objection yes check A design the checks passed The design fails; the objection is its note on the record no measure A stage's numbers The result is marked rejected and never chosen; it is not measured again no choose The pick The decision is made again without it; the critic says whether it rejects the design or the pick yes 
flow:
  search: {by: claude, critic: flux}
  check:
    correctness: "{python} {home}/check.py {artifact}"
    critic: claude
  choose: {critic: {by: claude, rounds: 2, timeout_s: 600}}
  • A critic is flux, an agent, your own agent ({by: {run: [...]}}), or {by: ..., rounds: N, ...agent options}.
  • rounds (1 to 5, default 1): how many objections the box answers; search and choose only. When they run out, the last pick goes ahead.
  • A search critic needs a picker (by: flux, by: tools, an agent); with the rules, a space, or trunk:, the loader warns. Hand-queued ideas are not judged.
  • A critic that fails or times out has no opinion; it never stops the loop.
  • It runs wherever its box runs: every pass, pass 0, R passes, Re-Evaluate. Numbers already judged are not judged again.
  • The choose critic's rejects: design (final, until Restore in Results) or pick (default; lapses once the numbers change).
  • Its prefers: the design it would choose instead -- only this brings back a design an earlier rejection keeps out (once a decision); designs named in its reasoning do not.
  • Metrics it names in wrong are struck through in Results (values kept).
  • flow.critique is refused (an older key); budget.critique_rounds is ignored with a warning.

docs.title: Check settings
docs.text:
flow.check is one command (a check named test) or an ordered map. Checks run in the order written; the first that reports failures refuses the design and the rest do not run.

check:                                                        # under flow:
  build: "{python} -m py_compile {artifact}"                  # a bare command
  correctness:                                                # or a map
    run: "{python} {home}/check.py {artifact}"
    timeout_s: 60
Field Default Purpose run Required Command string or argument list count_re (\d+) failing One capture group holding the number of failures fail_re Absent One match per failure; used instead of the default count pattern timeout_s 120 Seconds before the check is stopped; a check stopped there refuses the design ("timed out after 120s") and the loop goes on needs The loop's needs, else unlimited A resource hint: the cores and GB of memory it uses at most, and the labels of the machine it runs on
  • Names: a letter, then letters, digits, _, -.
  • build: no pattern; any non-zero exit means it did not build.
  • count_re/fail_re directly under flow.check are refused.
  • Output to verdict: check contract.

docs.title: Measurement settings
docs.text:
flow.measure is an ordered map of stages, cheapest first. A stage is a command or a map:

Field Default Purpose run Required Command string or argument list (as a check's; command: is refused, as everywhere a document runs a command); {metrics} in it is the stage's metrics, comma-separated (fluxpreset rtl measure {artifact} --metrics {metrics} ...) metrics Required unless metrics_re The names printed as name=value -- a number, or a dictionary (below) metrics_re Derived from metrics Map of metric name to a regex with one capture group needs Inferred for fluxpreset prog count/size; else empty Programs required on PATH; a missing one skips the stage ("NOT RUN"). As a map, also a resource hint: {tools: [yosys], cores: 8, memory: 48} timeout_s 600 Seconds before the stage is stopped, with every process it started (a helper it left in the background too) cutoff None A gate before the next stage, or a list of gates that must all pass estimate Off Predict first, and skip designs the estimate already rules out
  • Non-zero exit: a failed measurement. No numbers; the design is refused there (kept on the record until the document changes or Re-Evaluate); ✗ in Live. Exit 0 with no metric is refused too ("no metric matched in the output").
  • Dictionaries: name={"a": 1, "b": 2} (or in a JSON object) gives name.a, name.b (one test each) and name = their mean.
    • _a sets its aggregate: name={"a": 1, "b": 2, "_a": "sum"} (mean, median, min, max, sum; anything else is refused).
    • Missing, null and non-finite values stay unmeasured, never zero.
    • An objective ranks name (by _a, else the mean), by its own aggregate ({metric: name, aggregate: sum, direction: minimize, unit: us}; wins over _a), or one test ({metric: name.a}). type: is refused.
    • Unranked dictionaries are extra measurements, shown folded in Results.
  • Metric names are unique per stage. evaluator: stages are refused.

Cutoffs gate the next stage, one rule each: {metric: M, at: N} (at least N), {metric: M, below: N} (at most N), {metric: M, within: F} (within fraction F, 0 < F <= 1, of this run's best there). M may be carried from an earlier stage.

Estimates: {kind: surrogate|command|model, margin: 0.05}; run only with kind: command (estimate contract). A design estimated past a cutoff or limit by more than the margin is skipped.

Carried numbers: stages may measure different things. At each stage, a metric's number is its deepest measurement so far; Results says where it came from ("fmax_mhz=500 (from timing)").

Shared folder: a design's checks and stages in a pass share FLUX_REUSE_DIR, so tools (the presets do) can continue from earlier work. Never shared across designs (Compiling).

flow:
  measure:
    timing: {run: "{python} {home}/sta.py {artifact}", metrics: [fmax_mhz], cutoff: {metric: fmax_mhz, at: 250}}
    area:   {run: "{python} {home}/area.py {artifact}", metrics: [area_um2]}
objectives:
  - {metric: fmax_mhz, goal: ">= 300"}   # judged on area, with timing's number carried
  - {metric: area_um2, direction: minimize}
  • Every objective needs a stage that measures it. A stage:-pinned limit or a cutoff must name a metric its stage has.
  • task check notes an objective only the last stage measures.
  • Between stages: every design past the cutoffs climbs to the next stage (never measured twice at one stage). Only a cutoff or estimate saves a costly stage; task check says when none does.
  • The decision uses the deepest stage reached. A design that never reached an objective's first stage is not chosen ("stopped at" in Results, or Pending while it may still climb).

docs.title: Knowledge settings
docs.text:
Field Default Purpose library Empty Files and folders (specs, sources, notes, PDFs), relative to the folder, that join library/ as the loop's library; the AI looks it up when it needs it by flux Who summarises the library's papers: flux (FluxAgent) or an agent (its options beside); off turns the library off insights {by: off} Conclusions drawn from the loop's results: {by: rules} (computed, no AI), {by: <agent>}, or {by: off}; the agents read them with the library workbench who digests Who sums up the agents' workbench/ when it changed: off, flux, or an agent ({by: claude, timeout_s: 600} with its options); unsaid, whoever digests the papers ideas flux Who cleans up the ideas notebook before a pass, once it grew: flux (FluxAgent, the default in every loop: no line needed), off, or an agent; {by: flux, open: 20, new: 10} runs it at 20 open ideas with 10 new since the last cleanup (the defaults). It merges repeated ideas (undoable); see Ideas cleanup hidden Empty Files, folders or globs (relative to the folder) the AI agents may not read: tests, checks, a gate's files and their parameters; see Hidden from AI
  • Configurator: a bubble each in the Graph's Knowledge group; By off writes off (Library: by: off), Insights' rules {by: rules}. Skills' off is skills: off, Notes' notes: off.
  • by: off allows insights, ideas, workbench, hidden beside it, not library.
  • digest, lessons, off are older keys, refused; sheet, files, text are ignored with a warning.
  • Linked projects' libraries appear read-only at library/<project>@<group>/ (<project>@_ for a global one), in project order, their hidden paths hidden. @ names at the top of library/ are reserved.

docs.title: Hidden from AI
docs.text:
flow.knowledge.hidden: paths the loop's agents may not read. Checks, stages and scripts still read them; failure text still reaches the agent.

flow:
  knowledge:
    hidden: [tests/, golden.py, "params/*.json"]
  • Relative to the loop folder, inside it, never the document.
  • An agent's own hidden: adds paths for it alone.
  • Left out of the library, knowledge files and skills.
  • Not a sandbox: for secrets use the sandbox.
  • Web app: Files › Actions › Hide from AI, or the configurator's Hidden bubble. Chat can still read them to answer you (Hidden from AI).

docs.title: Skills
docs.text:
A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md (front matter name and description, then instructions). The loop's skills/ and the built-in flux-loop-commands are used by default (Skills). skills: changes that:

skills: off                                  # none, not the built-in one either
skills: [skills, ../shared-skills]           # these folders instead of skills/
skills: {off: [flux-loop-commands, rtl-style]}   # skills/ and the built-in one, these two off
skills: {from: [../shared-skills], off: [old-style]}

docs.title: Objective settings
docs.text:
Each entry is a metric name or a map:

Field Default Purpose metric Required A metric a stage reports (name or name.test for a dictionary metric) direction maximize; a goal written "< 80" or "<= 80" makes it minimize minimize or maximize goal None A limit: at most N when minimizing, at least N when maximizing; also ">= 1000", "< 80" stage The deepest stage for a goal Where the goal is judged (a stage that has the metric: measured there or carried from an earlier one) unit Known for common metrics Display unit aggregate mean How a dictionary's tests make its number: mean, median, min, max, sum tie 0 Relative band within which two designs tie and the next objective decides margin 0 Extra headroom required when a goal is judged on a shallower stage balance false Decide by the best trade-off (the knee) of the goal-less objectives keep None A relative limit: keep this fraction (0..1] of the best gain over above above 0 The reference for keep

How the decision is made:

  1. A design meeting every limit beats one that misses any. An unmeasured limit counts as missed.
  2. Among those, goal-less objectives decide in written order (within tie, the next decides). With balance, the best trade-off decides.
  3. An exact tie goes to the next objective (limits included), then to the earlier design.
  4. If none meets every limit, the closest (fewest misses, then smallest shortfall) is reported, not decided.
  5. While a stage has refused every design, there is no decision ("None has passed every stage yet").

goal cannot combine with keep or balance. A dictionary objective ranks its mean unless aggregate (or its _a) says otherwise, or it names a test (d.test).

docs.title: Resource hints (needs)
docs.text:
needs: {cores: N, memory: G} (GB) says what a check or stage uses at most. A top-level needs: is the default for every check and stage. Unsaid cores: 1 (its builds run -j1); unsaid memory: unlimited (only the sandbox's memory limit applies).

needs: {memory: 8}                 # every step of this loop
flow:
  check:
    lint: {run: "{python} {home}/lint.py {artifact}", needs: {cores: 2}}
  measure:
    place:
      run: fluxpreset rtl measure {artifact} --stage place
      metrics: [area_um2]
      needs: {tools: [openroad], cores: 8, memory: 48}
  • Scheduling: the machine's cores and memory (less 10% of memory, at least 4 GB) are one pool for every loop and user. A step (or an agent's probe) starts when its hint fits what is free; else it waits ("waiting for room (needs 8 cores, 48 GB; free 2 cores, 30 GB)"), in fair turns. After 10 minutes, smaller steps no longer overtake it. A step counts the larger of its hint and its stage's peak over the last 20 runs. No cores said: counts 1 core. No memory said: counts none. A step always starts when nothing else runs.
  • Builds: FLUX_JOBS is its cores (capped by the sandbox), else 1: make -j"$FLUX_JOBS". A compile-heavy step that states no cores builds about 2× slower than with the machine's cores, even on an idle machine. To build with more jobs, state needs: {cores: N} on the step, or loop-wide.
  • Not a limit: a step may use more, up to the sandbox's limits. Its loop then gets one note ("Stage place used 37 GB of memory against a hint of 4 GB.") with Set memory: 48 (peak plus a quarter, rounded to 4 GB, 8 GB above 32 GB), which writes needs: {memory: 48} on that stage. Notes come only for what the step says (or for running out of memory).
  • Out of memory: killed because the machine ran out, it runs once more; a second kill fails it. Killed at its sandbox limit, it fails; raise the loop's sandbox memory.
  • Another machine: any other key (fpga: 1, lab: loopback, board: zcu104) sends the step (and its probes) to a joined machine that has it (Machines). Live says where ("… · on runner-1"). true: has the key; a word: exactly that; a number: that many units (fpga: 1 takes one of fpga=2).
  • Other commands: flow.design: {run: ..., needs: {fpga: true}}, the baseline's run, a search's run (flow.search: {run: ..., needs: ...}) and flow.search.scope.needs take labels too; the top-level needs: does not apply to them. by: boxes always run on the server (needs refused).
  • The whole run: flow: {needs: {bigmem: true, memory: 256}} (or trunk: {needs: ...}) picks the machine for the whole loop. Never a step default. Needs the admin's permission; otherwise the loop runs on the server.
  • Never stale: changing cores, memory or labels changes no measurement. Only a stage's tools is part of how it is measured.
  • Configurator: a check's or measurement's Needs row: cores and GB (empty: "unlimited"), then a pill per machine label (+ Add offers your machines' labels, "fpga · 2 machines · up to 2"). A counted label gets a number; another a word. An unknown label (gpu) is kept, dashed ("no machine has this yet"). Save writes needs: {fpga: 1, lab: loopback}. The Preview app offers examples only.
  • Admin › Activity › Resources shows the pool and waiting steps.

docs.title: Run length, repairs, and concurrency
docs.text:
Field Default Purpose passes 0 A limit on the passes of a start that asks for none; 0 runs until stopped. A pass is one design, so this is how many designs the start makes, however many run at once; under trunk:, the designs its agents hand in. Counted per start, in both: a restart counts from 0 again. Not in the configurator, and a start from the web never reads it: the Start dialog sets each start's passes, and "until I stop it" means just that tries_per_pass 3 What one pass may work through. A loop builds one design a pass, so this caps its tries that give none and a critic's send-backs; for a search, its rounds: a pass carries one proposal, and a round that gives no design takes the next. Leave it out unless a search needs more; only a search's Tries row sets it in the configurator repairs_per_design 3 Repairs of one design before it is given up designs_at_once 1 Designs at once, wherever: passes at once (each its own design, in its own agent session; passes still counts each; a lane takes the next pass as soon as its own is decided -- with pipeline, as soon as its design is handed in -- and each pass decides as soon as it is measured), trunk branches (twice that may wait), a search pass's designs, the start's re-check's designs. A server limit also applies. Passes of a search run one at a time: the designs at once are inside each pass (what a pass carries) tools_at_once auto Tool steps at once across the whole loop: one pool of this many slots. A design's check, its measurements and its decision run as one tool step that holds one slot from its first check to the end of its decision, a wait for other designs' decisions included; on a loop an admin has not allowed parallel work, a design waiting behind a decision that runs an agent turn (a decide by an agent, a select critic) gives its slot back while it waits and takes one again to decide. An agent's probes take slots from the same pool, each probe one slot while it runs (a probe of the gate holds it through all its checks); estimates hold one only while their tool runs. Unsaid: designs_at_once + 1 (a trunk: its branches + 1): a slot per design at once and one spare for an agent's probe; a second probe at once waits for a slot. Use 1 for anything timed, or for a tool that breaks when two of its runs share the machine: no two tools then run at once, checks included. It never holds designs at once, only their tool steps. It is not a share of the cores: each check's and measurement's builds get FLUX_JOBS, its hint's cores, else 1, and the machine's pool keeps every loop's steps within its cores (more slots than cores: the steps past the cores wait for room). A server limit also applies agent_continues 3 Times a design agent's work is continued past its time limit before its design is handed in as it stands agent_grace_s a quarter of the agent's time limit, 300–600 s A final short turn to get the design past the gate; 0 turns it off tools true Whether FluxAgent calls tools inside its turns (compute, check, history, knowledge); false for a server without tool calls. A coding agent's turns are its own pipeline false true: drafting the next design overlaps the tool steps of the designs before it -- each lane starts its next design as soon as its current design is handed in by its agent, while that design's check, measurements and decision finish behind it in its tool step -- however long a decision takes (a decide by an agent), the lane drafts on; at most designs_at_once + tools_at_once designs are in flight at once (started and not yet decided: one drafting in each lane, one in or waiting for each tool slot). It never splits a design's check from its measurements. When a design fails its check (or a measurement sends it back to be fixed), its repair is queued on its lane: at the lane's next hand-in the same agent session repairs it, before the lane starts any new design, oldest first, within repairs_per_design, and the design keeps its number. Live's Timeline draws such a repair as its own dashed box on the lane, with its design's tag; the design's page in Results says "repaired after queueing". Each design is decided as soon as it is measured, whatever order the designs started in, and a design refused at a measurement stays a record later passes can improve on. A stop lets the designs behind finish, their queued repairs too, and be decided; Stop now ends a queued repair before it runs, and Results says "check failed; repair queued, not run before the loop stopped" under the design (the next start does not run it: its number stays spent). The next design's agent sees a design behind as being measured, its numbers once they land. No effect on a re-check (it drafts nothing; beside the passes it measures one design at a time, the start's own re-check designs_at_once at once, each one tool step), a search (its pass measures its designs inside it) or a trunk-mode loop (its agents draft while branches run anyway); on a loop an admin has not allowed parallel work (its Settings › Advanced › Allow parallel work) it still pipelines, with one lane, one agent turn and one tool step at a time: the next design's turn runs while the design before it is checked and measured, and Live says parallel work is off in that run. In the configurator: Extra › Running › Pipelining. Live says what it would save on your loop once it has three passes
  • These nine are the whole budget. designs_at_once, tools_at_once and pipeline are type-checked: a whole number of at least 1, a whole number (0 or unsaid: auto), true or false; a document saying otherwise is refused at its check.
  • prototype as a budget key is refused (it is Design's, below).
  • A removed budget key loads with a warning and does nothing (a configurator save drops it).
  • Prototype limits and FluxAgent's tool turns have no key.

docs.title: Prototypes
docs.text:
A prototype is the algorithm in Python (or SystemC), checked against the golden model before the target design is written. For problems with a golden model.

  • On Design: design: {prototype: false}, design: {by: claude, prototype: systemc}. Values: true (default), false, python, systemc.
  • With run or catalog: ignored, with a warning.
  • It does not create a golden model.

docs.title: Baseline / pass 0
docs.text:
baseline checks and measures a reference before pass 1, so results read relative to it. Off by default. Pass 0 uses no AI, repairs nothing, and does not count toward passes.

baseline: true                                   # the project as it is: your scripts as written
# baseline: {file: baseline.py}                  # an unchanged design file
# baseline: {run: "{python} {home}/baseline.py {artifact}", timeout_s: 600}
# baseline: {metrics: [{metric: area_um2, value: 120}, {metric: fmax_mhz, value: 1000, stage: place}]}
# add only: true to stop after pass 0
Form What pass 0 measures true Your scripts as written; {artifact} is an empty file, so use {home}/... paths {file: F} F (relative to the folder) copied to {artifact}; the original is untouched {run: C, timeout_s: 600} Whatever C writes to {artifact} (contract); if it writes nothing, the project as it is {metrics: [...]} Nothing runs: the values are recorded as the reference
  • metrics entries: {metric, value, stage}, a finite number; stage defaults to the deepest and must report the metric; each pair once. Never a design or the decision.
  • only: true: stop after pass 0.
  • Reuse: a successful baseline stands while the baseline: section is unchanged. To redo it: Settings › Record › Re-Evaluate with Rerun baseline. A failed one retries at the next start.
  • Baselines skip estimates and cutoffs; they are grey lines and the base of relative values, never the decision or a search start.

docs.title: Run, stop, resume
docs.text: Check, start, stop and read a loop in the web app. Everything here is on a loop's page: the Start, Stop and Restart buttons in its header, Settings › Problem › Check, and the Overview, Live and Results tabs (Tour).

docs.title: Check before running
docs.text:
Settings › Problem › Check validates the document and lists its stages, checks, objectives, tools and model. It runs no candidate check or measurement; a one-pass run does that.

  • Every file the document names must be in the loop (a missing one is listed with its key).
  • The golden model must run.
  • A document that does not load, a missing file or a refused setting is listed with where it is set; the configurator marks it on its step (Issues).
  • It runs in the sandbox.
  • Start runs the same check first when the inputs changed; on failure its button reads Start anyway.

A loop has problem.yaml; extra NAME.problem.yaml files are other problems with their own records. Settings › Problem edits one at a time, and Start asks which one runs.

docs.title: Start
docs.text:
Start asks how many passes (one design each) or Until stopped.

  • A start resumes from the record: unchanged measurements are reused.
  • A trunk asks for designs and says what runs ("trunk: 2 agents, 3 branches at once, 6 may wait"); one branch at once while parallel work is off.
  • Settings › Record › Re-Evaluate checks and measures again every design on the record (or only some Results tabs), and with Rerun baseline the baseline (pass 0), before the passes (Results).
  • Who works each box, which model, thinking, budgets: the document (Configure); the run's resources: Settings › Advanced (admins).

docs.title: Stop, resume, and keep experiments separate
docs.text:
An unlimited run goes on until stopped. Meeting an objective or a stalled search does not stop it.

  • Stop and Restart act after the current pass: an amber pill says "Stops after pass 4". Press the same button again to act now; the pass is abandoned.
  • Resume: Start again; unchanged measurements are reused.
  • One run per record: a second start is refused while a run holds the record; so are Delete, Rename, Reset, Archive and Replace.
  • Trunk: Stop ends agent turns, lets running branches finish and keeps the queue. Stop now ends everything; the next start runs the interrupted designs first.
  • Separate experiment: New loop › Clone copies a loop's problem without its runs. Settings › Preferences › Archive, reset or delete › Reset keeps the document and scripts and asks what else to keep.

docs.title: When a measurement still counts
docs.text:
A measurement counts (decision, ranking, best, charts) until its stage changes:

  • the measure command (its words; not spacing, quoting or comments);
  • how numbers are read (metrics / metrics_re, a dictionary's aggregate);
  • its parameters (vars:, when the command takes {vars});
  • its input files (files and scripts the command uses);
  • its tools (the build of each program the stage runs or needs).

Nothing else makes it stale: not prompts, other stages, checks, objectives, cutoffs, agents, budgets, names, comments or unread files.

  • A change is judged at the next start, or at once when saved in the web app while the loop is stopped. Pages show the last judgement and when it was made.
  • Stale measurements stay in Results, muted, marked "measured before a change". The decision and charts leave them out.
  • Overview shows a card ("12 designs were measured before a change to how synth is measured (the measure command and input file a.txt)"). The owner or an editor picks:
    • Accept as current: they count again (audited);
    • Leave as stale: card closed until the next change;
    • Re-measure: checked and measured again, by the running loop at its next free place, beside the designs it is making, one stale design at a time (a loop making one design at a time does it between two passes), or by a new run, designs_at_once of them at once.

docs.title: Read the result
docs.text:
• Overview: the decision against your limits, the best designs, the best so far over time (Tour).
  • Results: every design measured, ranked; charts; compare designs side by side; the ideas notebook (Results).
  • Live: passes, tools and agents, now and for every earlier start; its Start picker opens an older one (Live).
  • Agents: every model and agent turn: prompt, reply, tool calls, time, tokens.
  • Chat: ask an agent about the loop (why it stalls, which design is best); it reads the loop and changes nothing (A loop's Chat).

The decision's artifact is written under out/ only when a design meets every requirement. Estimates and screening numbers are not confirmed measurements.

The run ends with Meaning ✓ accepted A measured design meets every requirement; the decision artifact is written ! closest Correct designs were measured, but none meets every requirement; Overview shows the shortfall ✗ failed No design was measured, or the run could not start; Why it stopped says why

docs.title: Sandbox
docs.text:
Checks, runs, New loop › Agent and Chat's agents run in a container: agents and the loop's own code cannot touch the rest of the server's machine. Engine: rootless Podman, else Docker. Without either: the sandbox needs Podman or Docker.

Sees The host read-only: system, /nix/store, Flux, programs on PATH, the loop's folder Writes Only the loop's out/, workbench/ and cache. Scratch is deleted after the run and capped by Scratch /tmp size (Admin › Runtime › Sandbox, or the loop's Settings › Advanced) Home Flux's agent config and logins, not yours: no ~/.ssh, other repositories or Docker socket Network The host's, or an allowlist of hosts, domains and networks; direct TCP/UDP to them on request; the server's proxy. Admin › Runtime › Sandbox, Proxy; a loop's extra hosts in Settings › Advanced Limits Memory, CPUs, processes and scratch size: the loop's Settings › Advanced, else the server's defaults, never above its maximum (Sandbox limits, The memory guard) Off Settings › Advanced (admins): runs on the server as its account. Trusted code only

docs.title: When the sandbox cannot start
docs.text: Why it stopped on the Overview says what the engine said and what to do (the podman sandbox cannot start: ...). Flux repairs Podman's state itself when no Flux container runs, and logs it. The system service's installer prepares rootless Podman for its account; for anything else, ask the server's admin.

docs.title: When an agent's endpoint fails
docs.text:
• Down or busy (the server answers 5xx or 429, or cannot be reached): the agent's turn waits for the endpoint and then goes on in the same session; no try is spent. All the loops and lanes using that endpoint wait together, and one of them checks it, every 5 s at first and then less often (every 15 s and up for 429). Live's row says waiting for endpoint ... down since 10:02. After 30 minutes the pass ends and the loop waits until the endpoint answers; Stop ends it at once.
  • Refused (its login is refused, its account has no quota left, its model is not offered, or the endpoint is not on the sandbox's network allowlist): retrying cannot help, so the pass ends and the next pass tries once more. Refused again, the loop stops: Why it stopped says what was refused and where to fix it (Account › Agents or Admin › Agents, Admin › Sandbox).

docs.title: Compiling
docs.text:
Flux sets three things for every tool it runs (sandboxed or not):

  • MAKEFLAGS is cleared. An inherited -j would make Verilator build one file at a time. Never put -j in MAKEFLAGS.
  • FLUX_JOBS is the parallelism to use: make -j"$FLUX_JOBS", verilator --build-jobs "$FLUX_JOBS", cmake --build . -j "$FLUX_JOBS", ninja -j "$FLUX_JOBS". It is the step's resource hint cores (needs: {cores: 8} on the check or stage, or loop-wide; capped by the sandbox), else 1 -- so a compile-heavy step that states no cores builds about 2× slower, even on an idle machine. To build with more jobs, state the cores. Every loop's and user's steps on the machine count those cores in one pool, so together they never use more cores than the machine has.
  • ccache is on, one cache per user (ccache/<user> in Flux's cache folder, 10 GB max), never shared between users. Verilator uses it automatically. Other builds: CC="ccache gcc" CXX="ccache g++", or PATH="$FLUX_CCACHE_BIN:$PATH" (wraps gcc, g++, cc, c++, clang, clang++). Live shows hits and misses; Admin › Activity › Resources shows cache sizes.

Built-in presets also reuse one design's work within a pass: rtl measure --stage place after --stage synth at the same clock continues from synthesis; rtl power, energy, path and breakdown read an existing stage; rtl cycles, power and energy reuse the golden test's model. Measure a design's stages at the same --clock-ps to benefit. Nothing is shared across designs, loops or users, and no number changes.
