docs.title: First loop
docs.text:
Build a loop that compares two ways to sum the squares below n: a loop and a formula. Flux makes both, tests them, times them, and keeps the faster passing one.

Needs a Flux server and a browser. No model, no hardware tools.

docs.title: 1. Open the web app
docs.text:
Install and start Flux (Install), open its address and sign in.

The loop runs only your own scripts, so it can run without the sandbox: an admin switches it off for the loop in Settings › Advanced. With Podman or Docker on the server, leave it on.

docs.title: 2. Create the loop and its document
docs.text:
On the Loops list, New loop › Create or upload. Open Paste YAML, name the loop sums, paste this document and press Create from YAML:

statement: Find the fastest correct sum_squares(n) implementation.
contract: >-
  Provide sum_squares(n) for nonnegative integers n. Return the exact integer
  sum of i*i for 0 <= i < n. Keep the function name and signature.
artifact: design.py

flow:
  search:
    method: sweep
    space:
      implementation: [loop, formula]
  design:
    run: ["{python}", "{home}/render.py", "{artifact}", "{implementation}"]
  check:
    correctness: "{python} {home}/check.py {artifact}"
  measure:
    bench:
      run: "{python} {home}/bench.py {artifact}"
      metrics: [time_ms]

objectives:
  - {metric: time_ms, direction: minimize}

budget: {passes: 2, tries_per_pass: 1, tools_at_once: 1}
  • The loop's name, sums, is its id. There is no id field.
  • The sweep proposes both space choices in its first pass.
  • passes: 2 is a cap: the run ends when the sweep has nothing left.
  • tools_at_once: 1 keeps timings from competing.

docs.title: 3. Write the generator
docs.text:
The loop opens on its Overview. Add the three scripts below: write each on your computer and drop it on Files › All files (or use its Files upload button), or write it in the browser with New under the configurator's Files (Settings › Problem › Configurator › Prompt).

render.py:

import sys
from pathlib import Path

implementations = {
    "loop": "sum(i * i for i in range(n))",
    "formula": "n * (n - 1) * (2 * n - 1) // 6",
}
expression = implementations[sys.argv[2]]
Path(sys.argv[1]).write_text(f"def sum_squares(n):\n    return {expression}\n")
  • {implementation}: the chosen value.
  • {artifact}: where the script writes the design.
  • {home}: the loop folder. {python}: the interpreter running Flux.

More in command placeholders.

docs.title: 4. Write the correctness check
docs.text:
check.py:

import importlib.util
import sys

try:
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("candidate", sys.argv[1])
    candidate = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(candidate)
    function = candidate.sum_squares
except Exception as exc:
    print(f"did not load: {exc}")
    sys.exit(3)

failures = 0
for n in [0, 1, 2, 10, 100, 1000]:
    expected = sum(i * i for i in range(n))
    try:
        actual = function(n)
    except Exception as exc:
        actual = repr(exc)
    if actual != expected:
        failures += 1
        print(f"FAIL n={n}: got {actual!r}, expected {expected}")
print(f"{failures} failing")
sys.exit(1 if failures else 0)

This is the gate: a failing design never reaches the benchmark.

  • Exit 3: the design did not build or load.
  • Exit 1: it loaded but failed the tests.

docs.title: 5. Write the measurement
docs.text:
bench.py:

import importlib.util
import sys
import time

spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("candidate", sys.argv[1])
candidate = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(candidate)
candidate.sum_squares(1_000_000)  # warm up

times = []
for _ in range(9):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    candidate.sum_squares(1_000_000)
    times.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
print(f"time_ms={min(times):.6f}")

metrics: [time_ms] tells Flux which name=value to read; the objective minimizes it. The workload, repetitions and statistic are yours to choose.

docs.title: 6. Check, run, and inspect
docs.text:
1. Settings › Problem › Check validates the document and lists what it needs: every file it names, its checks, stages and objectives. It runs no test or benchmark.
  2. Start (▶ in the loop's header) asks how many passes: choose 2 and start. Each pass checks and times one design; the run ends when the sweep has nothing left. The formula should win.
  3. Overview shows the decision and the best design; Results lists both designs with their checks and time_ms; Live shows each pass's steps and their output.

What the run keeps, under Files › All files:

File Contents out/sums.py The chosen passing design out/sums.db The record: every design, check and measurement runs/ The log, the notes and the answer

Start again to go on: unchanged measurements are reused. For a separate experiment, Clone the loop from New loop (its problem, without its runs), or Settings › Preferences › Archive, reset or delete › Reset.

docs.title: Change the loop
docs.text:
• Add an implementation to render.py and space.implementation: the next run measures it.
  • Replace the generator with an agent, add a measurement stage, or add a limit.

Next: Configure, Search and agents, or the web app's pages. Other starting points: an agent writing the loop from your prompt and files (Write a loop with an agent), or a folder or .zip dropped on New loop › Create or upload.

docs.title: Agent options
docs.text: The options a coding agent takes in a document. Boxes an agent may work: Document reference. Model and login: Models and agents.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Written beside by: <agent> on a box or a critic. Beside by: flux or no by: ignored, with a warning.
  • With a list (design: {by: [claude, {by: codex, model: gpt-5-codex}], timeout_s: 1800}), options beside the list apply to all; an entry's own win (several Design agents). Sessions are each agent's own.
Option Default Purpose model The agent's own (or its settings) Its model by name, as the agent takes it: {by: codex, model: gpt-5-codex}, OpenCode's provider/model; it wins over every setting. Refused beside by: flux and for your own run: (give it in your command). The older args: [--model, …] still works, but not both at once timeout_s 1800 (or FLUX_<NAME>_TIMEOUT_S) Most seconds for one turn session pass (design: seeded) pass: one session per pass, on design one until the design is admitted; seeded (design only, its default): each design's session a warm start, begun where a shared turn that read the loop first ended -- Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode, others start from nothing; fresh (design only): each begun from nothing, as pass there; keep: its sessions kept across passes, one per design at once. The papers' digest, the workbench and the ideas have none. turn, an older value, does nothing: a warning, read as pass; remove it turns 8 With session: keep: the turns a session serves before a new one begins, 1 or more; forever: never renewed for its turns (the agent's own context management keeps it running), a new one only when it cannot be resumed or the document, the agent, its model or Flux changes seed_timeout_s 3600 design only, with its warm start (session: seeded, unsaid): the most seconds that shared first turn may take, 300 to 10800, whatever timeout_s says (Warm starts); refused elsewhere reseed_after_bests 7 design only, with its warm start: that shared first turn is made again after this many new best designs, 0 to 100, 0 never (Warm starts); refused elsewhere questions decide Who answers a question the agent asks (your own run: agent asks by writing question.json in its folder): decide (nobody), flux (FluxAgent; model too), operator. It wins over think. docs.title: What an agent may run
docs.text:
• By default an agent runs no compilers, simulators or test runners itself: it probes its file against the loop's gate and stages.
  • allow gives tools back ([yosys], or all). probe: false turns probes off.
  • Probes wait for a budget.tools_at_once slot like the loop's own runs.
  • Your own agent: by: {run: [my-agent, "{prompt_file}", "{artifact}"]} (agent contract).

docs.title: Commands and placeholders
docs.text: How every command a document names runs, the placeholders it gets, and its contract: arguments, output, exit code.

docs.title: How commands run
docs.text:
Checks, stages, estimates, the generator, the search, the baseline and the composition all run the same way, written run: (command: is refused). Your own agent differs: agent command.

  • Form: a list of arguments, or a string split like a shell would, but no shell runs. For pipes: ["sh", "-c", "cat {artifact} | wc -l"].
  • fluxpreset first runs a preset (fluxpreset rtl measure ...).
  • Working directory: {workdir}, the pass's folder, shared by its designs. Use {home}/... for the loop's files.
  • Environment: Flux's, with MAKEFLAGS cleared, FLUX_JOBS set (make -j"$FLUX_JOBS", verilator --build-jobs "$FLUX_JOBS"), ccache's variables, and for one design's checks and stages FLUX_REUSE_DIR (Compiling).
  • stdin: not data; do not read it.
  • Output: stdout and stderr captured separately; checks and stages read both. Live shows the command, folder, output and exit.
  • Timeouts stop the whole process group. A missing program is "not found on PATH"; Check lists them.
  • Placeholders are replaced in every argument, unquoted. An unknown {name} is refused at load (not checked inside arguments with spaces, such as sh -c scripts). A placeholder with no value for that command is left as written.

docs.title: Command placeholders
docs.text:
Placeholder Value Generator Check, stage, estimate Search Baseline Composition {artifact} Path of the design file (<workdir>/<name><ext>) writes it reads it "" writes it writes the whole {home} The document's folder (absolute) ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ {workdir} The pass's working folder ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ the compose folder {python} The interpreter running Flux ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ {name} The design's name (mul8#3, slice_sieve) ✓ ✓ search ✓ the loop's id {vars} Path of a JSON file of vars ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ {knob} One knob's value (True/False for booleans) search mode ✓ first choices {point} Path of a JSON file of every knob search mode ✓ "" ✓ "" {failure} Why the last attempt was refused (text) drafting "" {attempt} 1, 2, ... drafting 1 {history}, {state} Search history and the search's own state file ✓ {metrics} The stage's declared metrics:, comma-separated, in the document's order; Check asks the preset whether its stage can give them stage only {scope} The scope a pass works on, in search.scope's brief and check {prompt}, {prompt_file}, {session}, {answer} Brief and session, for your own agent

{part} is refused (a loop is one design).

File formats:

  • {vars}: vars.json in {workdir}, the document's vars.
  • {point}: <artifact>.point.json, components nested ({"algorithm": "list_sieve", "prefetch": {"distance": 2}}); an optional component that is off is left out.
  • {failure}: text, not a file: the last 4000 characters of the failing check's output (failed at <check>: with several checks), or a send-back reason. Empty at first.

docs.title: Generator command
docs.text:
design: {run: ...} writes one design to {artifact}. Its stdout is not the design.

  • Drafting (no space): a refused draft reruns with {failure} and {attempt}, up to budget.repairs_per_design times. A failing command (non-zero exit, or no file) or the same design twice ends the repairs.
  • Search (a space): once per point, with its {knob}s and {point}. A failure drops the point; no repair. The design is named after its knobs.
# document: design: {run: "{python} {home}/gen.py {artifact} {attempt} {failure}"}
import sys
out, attempt, failure = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3]   # failure is "" at first
design = "def count_primes(n):\n    ...\n" if not failure else "...a design that fixes it..."
open(out, "w").write(design)                                         # exit 0

docs.title: Check command
docs.text:
A check reads {artifact} and reports failures. Flux reads stdout and stderr together:

  1. Exit 3 means the design did not build, whatever was printed. For a check named build, any non-zero exit means that.
  2. Otherwise, with count_re (default (\d+) failing): the first match's number is the failure count. With fail_re only: each match is one failure.

  3. With no match: exit 0 passes, any other exit is one failure.

  4. A printed count wins over the exit: 2 failing with exit 0 fails; 0 failing with exit 1 passes.

  5. The first check with failures refuses the design; its last 4000 characters go to Live and back to the model or agent.
  6. stderr debug output fails nothing unless a pattern matches it.
# document: check: {correctness: "{python} {home}/check.py {artifact}"}
import importlib.util, sys
try:
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("design", sys.argv[1])
    design = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(design)
except Exception as exc:
    print(f"did not load: {exc}"); sys.exit(3)                 # 3: did not build
cases = {10: 4, 100: 25, 1000: 168}
bad = [n for n, want in cases.items() if design.count_primes(n) != want]
for n in bad:
    print(f"FAIL n={n}: got {design.count_primes(n)}, expected {cases[n]}")
print(f"{len(bad)} failing of {len(cases)}")
sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)

docs.title: Measurement command
docs.text:
A stage reads {artifact} and prints its numbers. It must exit 0; on any other exit its numbers are discarded and the design is refused at that stage. Flux reads stdout and stderr:

  • name=value, at the start of a line or after a space: the first occurrence of each metric counts. value is a number (1.5, -2e3); nan and inf are unmeasured.
  • A JSON object on a line of its own (it may span lines): its keys that are declared metrics are read. A name=value line overrides it.
  • A dictionary metric: name={"test": 12, "other": null} (the last occurrence counts), or a dictionary in the JSON object. Each finite entry is name.test; name is the objective's aggregate, else its _a (gate_count={"AND": 41, "OR": 34, "_a": "sum"}: mean, median, min, max or sum), else the mean. If designs disagree on _a, the first one met wins (the journal says so). An unranked dictionary is recorded and shown only.

  • metrics_re, if given, replaces the name=value patterns: one capture group each.

  • Exit 0 with no metric refuses the design ("no metric matched in the output"). Some metrics: recorded with those.

  • For timings set budget.tools_at_once: 1 (one slot pool for checks, measurements, probes).
# document: measure: {bench: {run: "{python} {home}/bench.py {artifact}", metrics: [time_ms]}}
import importlib.util, statistics, sys, time
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("design", sys.argv[1])
design = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(design)
runs = []
for _ in range(5):
    t = time.perf_counter(); design.count_primes(1_000_000); runs.append((time.perf_counter() - t) * 1e3)
print(f"time_ms={statistics.median(runs):.3f} time_spread_ms={max(runs) - min(runs):.3f}")

The measurement cache: a stage does not measure a design again while nothing it depends on changes: the design's text (or knobs), the stage's command, metrics and patterns, vars, the knobs it names, the folder's files (except out/, runs/, workbench/, library/, the documents), the {home}/... files it names, and its programs' and needs' builds. Only successes are reused. The cache is the record: a new record starts empty.

docs.title: Estimate command
docs.text:
estimate: {kind: command, run: ..., margin: 0.1} runs before the stage for each uncached design, with the stage's placeholders and timeout, printing the stage's metrics. A non-zero exit or no numbers: the tool runs. Missing a cutoff or limit by more than margin (a fraction of the limit): skipped, recorded as refused by the estimate.

# document: estimate: {kind: command, run: "{python} {home}/estimate.py {artifact}"}
import sys
print(f"time_ms={len(open(sys.argv[1]).read()) * 0.01:.3f}")

docs.title: Search command
docs.text:
search: {run: ..., timeout_s: 600} is your own search. Each round, Flux writes {history} and runs the command; the command answers with JSON on stdout.

{history} (search-history.json in {workdir}):

{"measured": [{"name": "w4", "knobs": {"w": 4}, "stage": "bench", "metrics": {"time_ms": 3.1}, "by": "mine"}],
 "refused":  [{"name": "w9", "why": "failed at correctness: 2 failing"}],
 "guidance": "operator notes, if any",
 "round": 3}

{state} (out/<record>.search-state.json) is yours: read it if it exists, write it every round; it survives restarts.

The answer is the last line of stdout that is a JSON object (or the whole stdout):

Key Meaning candidates [{name, artifact, knobs, why, by}]: name required; artifact is the design's text (not a path); knobs reach the checks and stages as {knob}/{point} lessons Lines added to the run's lessons not_established Lines added to the report conclusion What the search concluded, recorded when nothing is decided say A line printed with the round done true: this is the last batch

No candidates ends the search, as does a non-zero exit or no JSON (with a note). Candidates go straight to the checks; the generator does not run.

# document: search: {run: "{python} {home}/search.py {history} {state}", timeout_s: 300}
import json, os, sys
history, state_path = json.load(open(sys.argv[1])), sys.argv[2]
state = json.load(open(state_path)) if os.path.exists(state_path) else {"next": 1}
tried = {m["name"] for m in history["measured"]} | {r["name"] for r in history["refused"]}
cands = [{"name": f"w{w}", "artifact": f"WIDTH = {w}\n", "knobs": {"w": w}, "why": "next width"}
         for w in (state["next"], state["next"] + 1) if f"w{w}" not in tried]
state["next"] += 2
os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(state_path), exist_ok=True)
json.dump(state, open(state_path, "w"))
print(json.dumps({"candidates": cands, "done": state["next"] > 8}))

docs.title: Baseline command
docs.text: baseline: {run: ...} runs once before pass 1, with the first point (first choices, overlaid by the first seed). It writes the reference to {artifact}, or prepares the project and writes nothing (checks and stages then use {home}/...). A non-zero exit records "baseline failed"; the loop goes on.

docs.title: Agent command
docs.text:
Your own coding agent: by: {run: [my-agent, "--prompt", "{prompt_file}"], output: text, resume: [...]}. Write run as a list.

  • Placeholders use Python formatting: {prompt} (the brief; very long briefs become an instruction to read the file), {prompt_file}, {artifact}, {workdir} (the session folder), {name}, {python}, {home}, {workbench}, {probe}; a resume command also gets {session} and {answer}. Write a literal brace as {{ or }}; an unknown name refuses the draft.
  • The brief goes to stdin unless the command names {prompt}, {prompt_file} or {answer}.
  • It runs in its session folder with Flux's environment, plus FLUX_<NAME>_ENV and FLUX_PROBE. Default timeout 1800 s.
  • It writes {artifact}. If it does not, its reply is read: a JSON artifact field, else the largest fenced code block.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
The words Flux and its web app use.

Term Meaning Loop A folder holding a document (problem.yaml) and the files it names. The folder name is its id Document problem.yaml: what to make (statement, contract), who does each box (flow), what wins (objectives), how much to spend (budget). Document reference Start One launch of a loop, from Start until it stops. Each start resumes from the record Pass One trip round the loop, one design: choose, make, check, measure, decide. Capped by budget.passes or the Start dialog. budget.designs_at_once runs passes side by side; budget.pipeline: true overlaps the next design with the current one's measuring Trunk The other run mode (trunk: instead of flow:): a coding agent hands in designs from one long session while branches check, measure and decide them. Passes or a trunk Box A step as the configurator's Graph draws it. Setup: Plan (plan), Baseline (baseline). Knowledge: Skills (skills), Library, Workbench, Insights, Ideas (flow.knowledge), Notes (notes), Hidden (flow.knowledge.hidden). Each pass: Search (search), Design (design), Check (check), Measure (measure), Choose (choose) Check, gate A check (flow.check) decides if a design is correct. In order; the first failure refuses it. All checks together are the gate: a design that fails it is never measured Measurement, stage A command putting numbers on a design that passed the gate. Each is a stage of flow.measure, cheapest first; a cutoff decides which go on Design One candidate: a file (the artifact) made by a script, model or agent, with its checks and measurements on record Design name Each pass takes the next number: primes#1, primes#2... Tries inside a pass are primes#3.2, primes#3.3; the one that passes the gate is primes#3. Failed passes spend their number. A repeat of a measured design (spacing and comments aside) is refused ("the same as primes#1"), unless that design's numbers are stale. Search points keep their own names (arch=ripple) Probed draft A draft an agent tested itself but did not hand in: primes#p4.2 (pass 4, second). Unverified, never counted; Evaluate has the loop measure it Standing design The design the next pass builds on: the last decision (or the closest). Kept across restarts Decision The design meeting every limit and best on the objectives, written under out/. If none meets every limit, the closest is reported, not decided. "Then earliest" after Decided by: a tie went to the earlier design Record Every design, check and measurement, with its origin, kept in out/. Reruns reuse it Objective, limit, preference An objective is a metric and a direction. With a goal it is a limit; without, a preference, compared in written order Front, knee The front (Pareto frontier): designs no other beats on every objective. The knee: where improving one starts costing much more of another Knob, space, point A knob is a setting with a list of choices; the space (flow.search.space) is all knobs; a point is one choice per knob Search How the next points are chosen (flow.search.method): sweep, montecarlo, gradient, anneal, genetic, pareto, phases, or FluxAgent or an agent (by: flux). Searches Policy The search's emphasis (flow.search.policy): adaptive (default), explore, improve, tune, finetune, variations FluxAgent Flux's own model on an OpenAI-compatible endpoint: flux in a document (model is refused). Proposes points, writes designs, reviews, digests papers, answers in Chat Agent A coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, or a server's own) that writes files, on its own model settings. Models and agents Critic A second opinion on Search, Check, Measure or Choose. A rejection re-picks the direction, fails the design, marks the numbers, or re-makes the pick. Critics Author In New loop › Agent: who writes the loop from your prompt Knowledge, library What the model and agents can look up: the library (library/, flow.knowledge.library, projects'), read in pieces on demand, and the insights Ideas notebook The hypotheses proposed and the designs that tested them (Results › Ideas). Cleanup merges repeats. Ideas are "idea 3", never "#3" Skill A folder with a SKILL.md (name, description, instructions). The loop's skills/ is read by default Workbench workbench/: the agents' own tools and notes, kept across runs Chat A conversation with an agent or FluxAgent bound to no loop; may read your loops and keep files in your chat workbench. Chat Hidden from AI Paths the loop's agents may not read (flow.knowledge.hidden). The loop's commands, and Chat, still read them Golden model A Python file (usually golden.py) saying what a hardware design computes: PORTS and golden(**inputs). Golden model Prototype The algorithm first written in Python (or SystemC) and checked against the golden model Baseline A reference measured before pass 1 (pass 0). Results read relative to it; never the decision Preset One of Flux's checks or measurements, run as fluxpreset NAME. Presets Archived loop A stopped loop kept read-only, working files deleted; results, document, files, workbench and Chat stay. Unarchive restores editing. Archive Sandbox The container checks, runs and agents run in. Sandbox ULP Unit in the last place: the gap between neighbouring floats. "Within 1 ULP" is at most one step off ASAP7 A free predictive 7 nm process kit (Arizona State University). Flux's area, timing and power are on ASAP7

docs.title: Presets
docs.text:
Flux's own checks and measurements. A document runs one as fluxpreset NAME ... (nothing is copied into the loop).

  • The configurator offers the catalog entries below under Flux presets (a check's Type, a measurement's Tool), with their parameters.
  • Each entry: title, catalog id and role, the command, parameters with defaults. A {name} that is not a loop placeholder is a parameter.

docs.title: golden
docs.text:
The golden test for RTL: the design against a golden model's vectors. It prints the failing vectors and N failing of M, and exits 0 (pass), 1 (fail) or 3 (did not compile). --extra F.sv adds a module the design instantiates; --lib PATH reads shared HDL in place, as rtl's below. The golden model's format is below.

fluxpreset golden DESIGN --golden golden.py [--extra F.sv] [--lib PATH ...] [--module M]
  • Test against a golden model (rtl-golden, a check): fluxpreset golden {artifact} --golden {golden} Verilator runs the module on golden.py's vectors and counts the wrong outputs. Parameters: golden ({home}/golden.py). Reports N failing. Needs verilator.

docs.title: rtl
docs.text:
Hardware checks and measurements on the ASAP7 process: lint with Verilator, measure with OpenROAD-flow-scripts. rtl measure runs the flow to the stage asked and prints one line, fmax_mhz=... area_um2=... power_w=... cell_count=... logic_count=... gate_equivalents=... path_ps=... worst_slack_ps=... (stat only area and counts, adding gate_count; route adds drc_errors and wirelength_um, its timing and power estimated from global routing; final is the same line, signed off on the parasitics extracted from the routed wires).

--metrics a,b,c asks for metrics by name: the line then has exactly those, in that order, and stage=. One flow run serves them all. fluxpreset rtl metrics lists the names, each with where it is read from and the earliest stage that has it:

From Metrics stat area_um2, cell_count, logic_count, gate_equivalents, gate_count; the area classes of rtl breakdown: area_seq_um2, area_arith_um2, area_xor_um2, area_buf_um2, area_logic_um2, flop_count synth fmax_mhz, power_w, path_ps, worst_slack_ps, clock_period_ps; the critical path of rtl path: path_levels, path_cell_ps, path_wire_ps; tns_ps, hold_slack_ps, power_dynamic_w, power_leakage_w, die_area_um2, utilization_pct place wirelength_est_um route drc_errors, wirelength_um final buf_count

Asked for by name only:

  • tns_ps: the total negative slack, 0 when timing closes. Beside worst_slack_ps it says whether one path fails or many.
  • hold_slack_ps: the worst hold slack. The clock is ideal before route.
  • power_dynamic_w and power_leakage_w: power_w split into what switching costs and what the cells leak idle.
  • die_area_um2 and utilization_pct: the die, and how much of the core the cells fill at that stage (area_um2 is the cells alone); the two to read when tuning --utilization.
  • wirelength_est_um: the placer's wire estimate, the routed wirelength_um without paying for routing; the same number at later stages.

  • buf_count: the buffers in the finished design. The flow counts them only at the end, so final alone gives it.

  • Area, cells, power and timing are read at the stage asked; logic_count and area classes come from synthesis.

  • An unknown name, or one the stage cannot give, is refused before anything runs: error: drc_errors needs --stage route (asked: place) -- known at place: .... A requested metric that cannot be read fails the run.
  • Catalog stages run --metrics {metrics} with the document's metrics; Check asks the preset (runs nothing) and refuses a metric the stage cannot give.

Three counts of the logic stand beside cell_count (every mapped cell at that stage):

  • logic_count: the cells of the synthesised netlist less the sequential ones (flops, latches, clock gates) and the buffers, inverters and tie cells, the classes rtl breakdown groups by. Every stage reads it from synthesis, before OpenROAD adds buffers and resizes cells.
  • gate_equivalents: the usual post-synthesis figure: the standard-cell area of the synthesised netlist over the area of the library's reference 2-input NAND, ASAP7's unit-drive NAND2x1 (0.08748 um2, read from the standard-cell LEF). Flops and tie cells count; macros and memories do not. It is the same number at every stage: the buffers and resized cells placement adds, and physical-only cells (tapcells, fillers), are in a later stage's area_um2 but not in gate_equivalents.
  • gate_count: technology-independent. Yosys runs synth -flatten -noabc, then abc -g AND,OR,XOR,MUX, and each combinational gate counts as one: a 2-input AND, OR or XOR, a 2:1 MUX, a NOT. Flops and buffers do not count. It is a dictionary by gate type, gate_count={"AND":41,"OR":34,"XOR":31,"MUX":0,"NOT":0,"_a":"sum"}; its _a makes its one number the total, so an objective needs no aggregate:. stat prints it by default. At the other stages it is printed when asked for, and it costs an extra Yosys pass.

--advanced-gates (off by default) synthesises to complex cells: AOI/OAI, XOR/XNOR, majority, full and half adders, Booth multipliers.

  • Usually smaller area and less power; timing changes too (measure it).
  • Every number of the run comes from that netlist (area_um2, power_w, cell_count, fmax_mhz, the critical path, logic_count, gate_equivalents, rtl breakdown's classes).
  • Taken by rtl measure, breakdown, fmax, power, energy, path; the catalog lists it as advanced_gates under options. Add it to the stage's run line.
  • Examples: adder16's behavioural adder at place (333 ps): 16.6 → 12.2 um2; an 8x8 multiplier (625 ps): 38.0 → 33.9 um2, power down by a third.

With it, gate_count counts complex gates too: Yosys runs synth -flatten -noabc, extract_fa, abc -g AND,NAND,OR,NOR,XOR,XNOR,ANDNOT,ORNOT,MUX,NMUX,AOI3,OAI3,AOI4,OAI4 and opt_clean. One gate each:

Key One gate AND, NAND, OR, NOR, XOR, XNOR a 2-input gate ANDNOT, ORNOT A & ~B, A \| ~B MUX, NMUX a 2:1 mux, inverted or not NOT an inverter AOI3, OAI3, AOI4, OAI4 ~((A&B)\|C), ~((A\|B)&C), ~((A&B)\|(C&D)), ~((A\|B)&(C\|D)) AO3, OA3, AO4, OA4 the same without the inversion: an AOI or OAI whose only reader is a NOT, counted with it as one gate (ABC has no such type) FA a full adder: the sum and the carry of three bits HA a half adder: of two bits, or of three with one constant
  • Adders count one per bit. No MAJ: a lone majority stays AOI/OAI gates. Inverters extract_fa adds count as NOT.
  • Every key is printed (0 when absent), with _a; deterministic.
  • adder16's ripple-carry adder: {"AND":31,"OR":15,"XOR":31,"MUX":0,"NOT":0} (77) without the flag, 15 FA and 1 HA (16) with it.
fluxpreset rtl lint DESIGN
fluxpreset rtl measure DESIGN --stage stat|synth|place|route|final --clock-ps N [--metrics a,b,c] [--advanced-gates] [--utilization P] [--hierarchy] [--seed N] [--check]
fluxpreset rtl metrics [--stage S] [--json]
fluxpreset rtl cycles DESIGN --golden golden.py
fluxpreset rtl equiv DESIGN --reference ref.sv
fluxpreset rtl breakdown DESIGN [--advanced-gates]
fluxpreset rtl fmax DESIGN --stage synth|place|route|final [--steps 6] [--advanced-gates]
fluxpreset rtl power DESIGN --golden golden.py --stage place [--advanced-gates]
fluxpreset rtl energy DESIGN --golden golden.py --stage place [--advanced-gates]
fluxpreset rtl path DESIGN --stage synth|place|route|final [--advanced-gates]

breakdown, fmax, power, energy and path take --utilization, --hierarchy and --seed too.

docs.title: What is passed to the flow
docs.text:
All off by default. Put one in a stage's command when needed; a different command (another seed, say) is measured afresh.

Option What it does --utilization P How full the floorplan's core is, in percent (40 by default). A lower one gives a larger die and easier routing. Nothing changes at stat or in breakdown, which stop at synthesis. --hierarchy Keeps every module instead of flattening: each is synthesised apart and nothing is optimised across a boundary. Placement still works on all the cells at once. Cell counts and areas are the whole design's; gate_count stays that of the flattened design. --seed N Another random start for global placement, global routing and detailed routing, to see how much of a result is luck. It reaches those steps only, so stat and synth do not change. Seed 1 is what global placement does anyway.

docs.title: Other HDL beside the design (--lib)
docs.text:
Keep the design one file of its own modules; pass shared IP and baseline modules beside it, read in place:

fluxpreset rtl measure {artifact} --lib {home}/ip --lib {home}/baseline/fifo.sv --stage synth --metrics {metrics} --clock-ps {clock_ps}

Every rtl command (and golden, and measure --check) takes --lib PATH, repeatable, read in the order given and before the design:

  • a .sv or .v file; a .svh or .vh header adds its folder to the include path;
  • a folder: its .sv and .v files (not its subfolders), sorted by name, the folder on the include path;

  • a .f filelist: one source per line, +incdir+DIR or -I DIR for includes, -f FILE for a nested list, paths relative to the list; // and # start comments, any other option is refused.

  • Verilator, Yosys and OpenROAD-flow-scripts (VERILOG_FILES, VERILOG_INCLUDE_DIRS) read them. --module names the top (lint too; default the design's first module).

  • A design redefining a --lib module (or interface, package) is refused, exit 3: the design redefines module fifo of ip/fifo.sv: instantiate it, don't copy it.
  • equiv reads the libs on both sides; the reference's own definitions win.
  • A missing path: exit 3 (Check names it).

  • The catalog lists lib under options, no default.

  • Lint for hardware defects (rtl-lint, a check): fluxpreset rtl lint {artifact} Verilator's hardware defects only: latches, multiple drivers, combinational loops, blocking/non-blocking mixes, implicit nets; width and style warnings are not defects. It also refuses what does not parse. Reports N failing. Needs verilator.

  • Area and cells (ASAP7) (rtl-stat, a stage): fluxpreset rtl measure {artifact} --metrics {metrics} --stage stat --clock-ps {clock_ps} OpenROAD-flow-scripts' synthesis: the mapped cells' area and count, the logic cells among them, NAND2 gate equivalents, and Yosys's technology-independent gate count (2-input AND/OR/XOR, 2:1 MUX, NOT); nothing timed, the cheapest screen. Parameters: clock_ps (1000). Reports area_um2, cell_count, logic_count, gate_equivalents, gate_count. Needs yosys, openroad, make.
  • Synthesise and time (ASAP7) (rtl-synth, a stage): fluxpreset rtl measure {artifact} --metrics {metrics} --stage synth --clock-ps {clock_ps} OpenROAD-flow-scripts to its floorplan: the netlist timed unplaced, seconds. Parameters: clock_ps (1000). Reports fmax_mhz, area_um2, power_w, cell_count, logic_count, gate_equivalents, path_ps. Needs yosys, openroad, make, sta.
  • Place and time (ASAP7) (rtl-place, a stage): fluxpreset rtl measure {artifact} --metrics {metrics} --stage place --clock-ps {clock_ps} OpenROAD-flow-scripts to detailed placement, timed with wire estimates: tens of seconds. Parameters: clock_ps (1000). Reports fmax_mhz, area_um2, power_w, cell_count, logic_count, gate_equivalents, path_ps. Needs yosys, openroad, make, sta.
  • Route and time (ASAP7) (rtl-route, a stage): fluxpreset rtl measure {artifact} --metrics {metrics} --stage route --clock-ps {clock_ps} OpenROAD-flow-scripts to routing: timing after global routing, minutes. Parameters: clock_ps (1000). Reports fmax_mhz, area_um2, power_w, cell_count, logic_count, gate_equivalents, path_ps. Needs yosys, openroad, make, sta.
  • Sign-off timing and power (ASAP7) (rtl-final, a stage): fluxpreset rtl measure {artifact} --metrics {metrics} --stage final --clock-ps {clock_ps} OpenROAD-flow-scripts through detailed routing and its finish: timing and power with the parasitics extracted from the routed wires (OpenRCX), plus DRC errors and wirelength: the slowest stage and the closest to silicon. Parameters: clock_ps (1000). Reports fmax_mhz, area_um2, power_w, cell_count, logic_count, gate_equivalents, path_ps, drc_errors, wirelength_um. Needs yosys, openroad, make, sta. Give it a generous timeout_s (the crafter suggests 3600): a stage's default is 600 s.
  • Clock cycles (Verilator) (rtl-cycles, a stage): fluxpreset rtl cycles {artifact} --golden {golden} A clocked design run on golden.py's vectors, each started when the last is done: its latency in cycles (the most, the fewest) and the mean cycles per result. Parameters: golden ({home}/golden.py). Reports latency_cycles, latency_min_cycles, cycles_per_result. Needs verilator.
  • Equal to a reference module (rtl-equiv, a check): fluxpreset rtl equiv {artifact} --reference {reference} Formal equivalence with Yosys (a miter of the two, proved by SAT; a clocked pair by induction): passes when they are equal for every input, else prints a counterexample. Parameters: reference ({home}/reference.sv). Reports N failing. Needs yosys.
  • Where the area goes (ASAP7) (rtl-breakdown, a stage): fluxpreset rtl breakdown {artifact} --clock-ps {clock_ps} OpenROAD-flow-scripts' synthesis, its cells grouped: sequential, adders, XORs, buffers and inverters, the rest of the logic; and the flops. Parameters: clock_ps (1000). Reports area_seq_um2, area_arith_um2, area_xor_um2, area_buf_um2, area_logic_um2, flop_count, area_um2. Needs yosys, openroad, make.
  • Fastest clock that closes (ASAP7) (rtl-fmax, a stage): fluxpreset rtl fmax {artifact} --stage {stage} --clock-ps {clock_ps} --steps {steps} A few OpenROAD-flow-scripts runs, each at the period the last one's slack says, until the fastest clock that closes timing at that stage is found: costly, and the honest fmax. Parameters: stage (synth), clock_ps (1000), steps (6). Reports fmax_closed_mhz, closed_period_ps. Needs yosys, openroad, sta, make.
  • Power from the design's own switching (ASAP7) (rtl-power, a stage): fluxpreset rtl power {artifact} --golden {golden} --stage {stage} --clock-ps {clock_ps} Verilator runs golden.py's vectors and records the switching; OpenROAD reads it on the synthesised or placed design and reports power: internal, switching, leakage. Parameters: golden ({home}/golden.py), stage (place), clock_ps (1000). Reports power_w, power_internal_w, power_switching_w, power_leakage_w. Needs verilator, yosys, openroad, sta, make.
  • Energy per result (ASAP7) (rtl-energy, a stage): fluxpreset rtl energy {artifact} --golden {golden} --stage {stage} --clock-ps {clock_ps} The power the golden vectors' own switching draws, times the time one result takes (its measured cycles at the clock): energy per result and energy-delay product. Parameters: golden ({home}/golden.py), stage (place), clock_ps (1000). Reports energy_pj_per_result, edp_pj_ns, power_w, cycles_per_result. Needs verilator, yosys, openroad, sta, make.
  • The critical path's anatomy (ASAP7) (rtl-path, a stage): fluxpreset rtl path {artifact} --stage {stage} --clock-ps {clock_ps} OpenROAD's worst path at the stage: how many cells it crosses, and how much of its delay is in the cells and how much in the wires -- whether to cut logic or wire. Parameters: stage (place), clock_ps (1000). Reports path_ps, path_levels, path_cell_ps, path_wire_ps, slack_ps. Needs yosys, openroad, sta, make.

docs.title: systemc
docs.text:
A SystemC design as SystemVerilog: ICSC translates it, so every RTL preset can judge it. Alone it checks that the module translates; --then "golden --golden g.py" or --then "rtl measure --stage stat" runs that preset on the translation.

fluxpreset systemc DESIGN.h --top M --golden golden.py [--then "golden --golden golden.py"]
  • SystemC translates to RTL (ICSC) (systemc-translate, a check): fluxpreset systemc {artifact} --top {top} --golden {golden} ICSC translates the SystemC module to SystemVerilog: passes when it does, and when the ports are the golden model's. Parameters: top (top), golden ({home}/golden.py). Reports N failing.
  • SystemC against a golden model (systemc-golden, a check): fluxpreset systemc {artifact} --top {top} --golden {golden} --then "golden --golden {golden}" ICSC translates the SystemC module, then Verilator runs the RTL on golden.py's vectors. Parameters: top (top), golden ({home}/golden.py). Reports N failing. Needs verilator.

docs.title: cases
docs.text:
The golden test for Python: the design's function called on cases and compared with the expected value or a reference function's (floats within --tol). Cases come from a JSON table ([args] or {"args", "kwargs", "expected"}), the reference module's CASES, and --random N draws of its inputs(rng).

fluxpreset cases DESIGN.py --call F [--reference ref.py[:F]] [--cases cases.json] [--random N] [--tol R]
  • Compare with a reference function (python-cases, a check): fluxpreset cases {artifact} --call {call} --reference {reference} --random {random} Calls the design's function on cases (a JSON table, the reference's CASES, random inputs from its inputs(rng)) and compares each result with the reference function's or the expected value. Parameters: call (main), reference ({home}/reference.py), random (100). Reports N failing.

docs.title: ccases
docs.text:
cases for a C or C++ function: the design built as a shared library and called through ctypes with a scalar --sig, against a Python reference.

fluxpreset ccases DESIGN.c --call F --sig "long(long,long)" --reference ref.py:F --random N
  • Compare a C function with a reference (c-cases, a check): fluxpreset ccases {artifact} --call {call} --sig {sig} --reference {reference} --random {random} Builds the design as a shared library and calls one function (a scalar signature) on cases, each result compared with a Python reference function's or the expected value. Parameters: call (main), sig (int(int)), reference ({home}/reference.py), random (100). Reports N failing. Needs cc.

docs.title: pytest
docs.text:
Your pytest file against the design: the design is copied as design.py beside your tests, and the failing tests are counted.

fluxpreset pytest DESIGN.py --tests test_design.py

The design is imported as design.

  • Run your pytest file (python-pytest, a check): fluxpreset pytest {artifact} --tests {tests} Runs your pytest file with the design importable as design; counts the failing tests. Parameters: tests ({home}/test_design.py). Reports N failing.

docs.title: accuracy
docs.text:
How far an approximation is from its reference, as a measurement, not pass or fail. max_ulp counts float64 steps.

fluxpreset accuracy DESIGN.py --call F --reference ref.py:F --random N
  • Accuracy against a reference (python-accuracy, a stage): fluxpreset accuracy {artifact} --call {call} --reference {reference} --random {random} Calls the design's function and a reference on the same cases and reports how far apart they are: absolute, relative and ULP error. Parameters: call (main), reference ({home}/reference.py), random (1000). Reports max_abs_error, mean_abs_error, max_rel_error, mean_rel_error, max_ulp.

docs.title: timebound
docs.text:
A time budget as a check: a Python function slower than --max-ms (the fastest of --runs) fails before the costly benchmark runs. A run stuck past the budget is stopped.

fluxpreset timebound DESIGN.py --call F --args "(1000,)" --max-ms 50
  • Within a time budget (python-timebound, a check): fluxpreset timebound {artifact} --call {call} --args {args} --max-ms {max_ms} Times one call of the design's function on a large input and fails a design slower than the budget, before the costly benchmark. Parameters: call (main), args (()), max_ms (1000). Reports N failing.

docs.title: bench
docs.text:
Time a Python function: the design loaded, f(*args) timed over --runs after --warmup. time_ms is the median. Exit 3 when the design does not load, 1 when it raises.

fluxpreset bench DESIGN.py --call F --args "(1000,)" [--runs 5] [--warmup 1]
  • Time a Python function (python-bench, a stage): fluxpreset bench {artifact} --call {call} --args {args} --runs {runs} Loads the design, calls one function with your arguments, times it over several runs. Parameters: call (main), args (()), runs (5). Reports time_ms.

docs.title: prog
docs.text:
Build a program with --build ({out} is the program it builds), then time, count, size or watch it. It prints name=value lines and exits 3 when the build fails.

fluxpreset prog time|count|memory|size --build "c++ -O2 -o {out} {artifact}" [--run CMD]
  • Program size (prog-size, a stage): fluxpreset prog size --build "{build}" Builds the program and reads its sections with size: text, data and bss bytes. Parameters: build (c++ -O2 -o {out} {artifact}). Reports text_bytes, data_bytes, bss_bytes. Needs size.
  • Program run time (prog-time, a stage): fluxpreset prog time --build "{build}" --run "{run}" --runs {runs} --warmup {warmup} Builds the program and times it over several runs (hyperfine when present). Parameters: build (c++ -O2 -o {out} {artifact}), run, runs (10), warmup (1). Reports time_ms, time_ms_stddev, time_ms_min.
  • Instruction count (Valgrind) (prog-count, a stage): fluxpreset prog count --build "{build}" --run "{run}" Builds the program and counts instructions and cache misses with Valgrind's cachegrind: deterministic. Parameters: build (c++ -O2 -o {out} {artifact}), run. Reports instructions, d1_misses, ll_misses, branch_mispredicts. Needs valgrind.
  • Program peak memory (prog-memory, a stage): fluxpreset prog memory --build "{build}" --run "{run}" --runs {runs} Builds the program and runs it: its peak resident memory as the kernel counts it, the most over the runs. Parameters: build (c++ -O2 -o {out} {artifact}), run, runs (3). Reports peak_rss_kb.

docs.title: sanitize
docs.text:
A C or C++ program built with AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer and run: each distinct memory error, leak or undefined behaviour it hits is a failure.

fluxpreset sanitize --build "cc -O1 -o {out} {artifact}" [--run CMD]
  • Memory and undefined-behaviour errors (c-sanitize, a check): fluxpreset sanitize --build "{build}" --run "{run}" Builds the program with AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer and runs it: each memory error, leak or undefined behaviour it hits is a failure. Parameters: build (cc -O1 -o {out} {artifact}), run. Reports N failing. Needs cc.

docs.title: complexity
docs.text:
How complex a design's source is, read and not run, in any common language (lizard). With --max-cyclomatic N it fails each function over N.

fluxpreset complexity DESIGN [--ext .c] [--max-cyclomatic 15]
  • Source complexity (complexity, a stage): fluxpreset complexity {artifact} Reads the design's source (any common language) and counts its lines of code, functions, cyclomatic complexity and tokens; nothing is built or run. Reports loc, functions, cyclomatic_max, cyclomatic_mean, tokens, max_function_loc.
  • No function too complex (complexity-limit, a check): fluxpreset complexity {artifact} --max-cyclomatic {max_cyclomatic} Fails each function whose cyclomatic complexity is over the limit. Parameters: max_cyclomatic (15). Reports N failing.

docs.title: scaling
docs.text:
How a command's time grows with the problem size: timed at doubling sizes ({n}; --input "gen {n}" feeds its stdin, --build makes {out} first), start-up time taken off, fitted as time ~ n^k. scaling_exponent is about 1 for linear, 2 for quadratic. With --max-exponent K it is a check.

fluxpreset scaling [--start 1000|--sizes A,B,C] [--input "gen {n}"] [--build "cc -o {out} {artifact}"] [--max-exponent K] -- CMD {n}
  • How time grows with size (scaling, a stage): fluxpreset scaling --start {start} -- {command} Times the program at doubling problem sizes and fits time ~ n^k: the exponent says how it scales (1 linear, 2 quadratic), the constant factor aside. Parameters: start (1000), command ({artifact} {n}). Reports scaling_exponent, scaling_r2, time_at_max_ms, max_n.
  • Scales no worse than n^k (scaling-limit, a check): fluxpreset scaling --start {start} --max-exponent {max_exponent} -- {command} Times the program at doubling sizes and fails when time grows faster than n to the given power. Parameters: start (1000), command ({artifact} {n}), max_exponent (1.5). Reports N failing.

docs.title: repeat
docs.text:
Any measurement run several times with its noise taken out: each metric's median and NAME_spread_pct.

fluxpreset repeat --n 5 [--warmup 1] -- CMD
  • Median of several runs (repeat, a stage): fluxpreset repeat --n {n} -- {command} Runs any measurement several times and prints each metric's median and its spread, so one noisy run does not decide. Parameters: n (5), command. Reports your name=value lines.

docs.title: derive
docs.text:
Metrics made from other metrics: a command's own numbers plus formulas over them (arithmetic, min, max, abs, sqrt, log, exp).

fluxpreset derive --expr NAME=EXPR [--expr ...] -- CMD
  • Metrics from formulas (derive, a stage): fluxpreset derive --expr {expr} -- {command} Runs any measurement and adds metrics computed from its numbers, such as area times delay or throughput per watt. Parameters: expr (adp=area_um2*path_ps), command. Reports your name=value lines.

docs.title: regress
docs.text:
A performance gate: a measurement run again and compared with a recorded baseline file. --record writes the file, --tol is the allowed percent, --higher names metrics where more is better.

fluxpreset regress --baseline base.json [--tol 5] [--record] -- CMD
  • No worse than a baseline (regress, a check): fluxpreset regress --baseline {baseline} --tol {tol} -- {command} Runs any measurement again and fails when a metric is worse than the recorded baseline by more than the tolerance. Parameters: baseline ({home}/baseline.json), tol (5), command. Reports N failing.

docs.title: extract
docs.text:
Any tool's output as name=value, so a tool that does not speak Flux needs no script: JSON, CSV or text, picked with --pick PATH=name (a dotted path, a column or a regex group).

fluxpreset extract [--format json|csv|regex] --pick PATH=name -- CMD
  • Numbers out of any tool's output (extract, a stage): fluxpreset extract --format {format} --pick {pick} -- {command} Runs your tool and reads its JSON, CSV or text output, printing the numbers you pick as name=value. Parameters: format (json), pick (value=metric), command. Reports your name=value lines.

docs.title: champsim
docs.text:
A cache prefetcher in ChampSim, on your traces. stats runs the prefetcher and the run without it on every trace and says why it wins: coverage (the share of misses removed), accuracy, lateness.

fluxpreset champsim build|check|run|stats ARTIFACT --traces DIR [--warmup N --sim N]
  • Build the prefetcher into ChampSim (champsim-build, a check): fluxpreset champsim build {artifact} Compiles a prefetcher header into ChampSim; reports the first compiler error. Reports N failing. Needs pythia.
  • Smoke-run the prefetcher (champsim-check, a check): fluxpreset champsim check {artifact} --traces {traces} Builds the prefetcher and runs it on one trace; refused when it issues no prefetches. Parameters: traces ({home}/traces). Reports N failing. Needs pythia.
  • Simulate on your traces (ChampSim) (champsim-run, a stage): fluxpreset champsim run {artifact} --traces {traces} --warmup {warmup} --sim {sim} Runs an .ini or a prefetcher header on every trace; the geometric-mean IPC speed-up over no prefetcher. Parameters: traces ({home}/traces), warmup (10000000), sim (15000000). Reports geomean_speedup. Needs pythia.
  • Why the prefetcher wins (ChampSim) (champsim-stats, a stage): fluxpreset champsim stats {artifact} --traces {traces} --warmup {warmup} --sim {sim} Runs it and the run without it on every trace: L2 misses per kilo-instruction with and without it, the share of misses it removed (coverage), and how many of its prefetches were used, late or useless. Parameters: traces ({home}/traces), warmup (10000000), sim (15000000). Reports l2_mpki, l2_mpki_baseline, pf_coverage, pf_accuracy, pf_late, pf_useless, pf_issued_pki, geomean_speedup. Needs pythia.

docs.title: asl
docs.text:
A PTO-style spec's AVS tests, from a spec checkout kept in the loop's folder. tests lists a unit's tests (by id or mnemonic); run runs them with ASLRef as the spec's release suite does, on --jobs threads, each failing test a line then N failing of M. --out FILE writes each result as JSON. Needs aslref on PATH or --aslref.

fluxpreset asl tests|run UNIT... --spec {home}/spec [--jobs N] [--out FILE]
  • The spec's AVS tests pass (asl-avs, a check): fluxpreset asl run {unit} --spec {home}/spec Runs a PTO-style spec unit's AVS tests with ASLRef, through the spec's own runner, from the spec kept in the application's folder. Each failing test a line, then the count. Parameters: unit (TADD). Reports N failing. Needs aslref.

docs.title: ndf
docs.text:
A PTO-style spec's normative clauses, read with the NDF tool. list gives each unit with its clauses by modality and its test count; clauses UNIT prints a unit's clauses; scope UNIT lists the unit and every unit that depends on it; check UNIT --results FILE reads asl run --out and counts each MUST clause failed or uncovered.

fluxpreset ndf list|clauses|scope|check UNIT --spec {home}/spec
  • Every MUST clause covered and passing (ndf-contract, a check): fluxpreset ndf check {unit} --spec {home}/spec --results {results} Reads a PTO-style spec unit's NDF clauses (the NDF tool, from the spec in the application's folder) and the AVS results fluxpreset asl run --out wrote: each MUST clause that failed or has no test is a line, then the count. Parameters: unit (TADD), results (avs.json). Reports N failing. Needs ndf.

docs.title: pto
docs.text:
A pyCircuit design checked against a PTO-style spec's ASL model, unit by unit. The design is one combinational datapath for the spec's elementwise units, with ports op (8 bits, from fluxpreset pto ops), dtype (5), a, b (64), y (64) and fault (1). Each wrong vector is a line, then N failing of M; --build-only only builds, --measure prints vectors_failing, units_passing, units. Needs pycircuit and aslref.

fluxpreset pto ops [--names]
fluxpreset pto ref UNIT...
fluxpreset pto check DESIGN --units UNIT... [--dependents] [--build-only|--measure]

Each takes --spec {home}/spec.

  • The design matches the spec's ASL model (pto-check, a check): fluxpreset pto check {artifact} --units {units} --spec {home}/spec Builds a pyCircuit design (pycircuit, the C++ model) and drives it with each unit's reference vectors -- the spec's own answers from ASLRef, cached per spec -- one wrong vector a line, then the count. The interface: fluxpreset pto ops. Parameters: units (all). Reports N failing. Needs pycircuit, aslref.

docs.title: Without a preset
docs.text:
• Test script (python-test-script, a check): {python} {script} {artifact} A Python script beside the document runs the design on known cases and prints N failing. Parameters: script ({home}/check.py). Reports N failing.
  • Any command (custom-check, a check): {command} Any command; it prints N failing (or say count_re / fail_re), or its exit code decides. Parameters: command. Reports N failing.
  • Timing script (bench-script, a stage): {python} {script} {artifact} A Python script beside the document runs the design and prints time_ms=.... Parameters: script ({home}/bench.py). Reports time_ms.
  • Any command (custom-stage, a stage): {command} Any command; it prints name=value for each metric it measures, listed as the stage's metrics. Parameters: command. Reports your name=value lines.

docs.title: One interface
docs.text:
Every preset keeps the same interface:

Arguments fluxpreset NAME [SUBCOMMAND] ARTIFACT [--option VALUE ...]: the design file first, every other input an option with a default stdin Never read stdout A check: each failure on a line of its own, then N failing (or N failing of M) last. A measurement: name=value for each metric it reports stderr Diagnostics for a person; never the count or the numbers Exit code 0 passed or measured; 1 failed, or the measurement could not be taken; 2 wrong arguments; 3 the design did not build, parse or load Files Only in a temporary folder of its own; never in the loop's folder

docs.title: Golden model
docs.text:
fluxpreset golden, rtl cycles, rtl power, rtl energy and systemc read a golden model: a Python file that defines PORTS and golden(**inputs).

PORTS = [
    {"name": "x", "dir": "in", "bits": 16, "unsigned": True},
    {"name": "y", "dir": "out", "bits": 16, "unsigned": True},
]

def golden(x):
    return {"y": x}
Setting Purpose COUNT Random vectors (default 32), besides generated corner cases SEED Random seed VECTORS Input dictionaries, the whole set when given (no corners, no random vectors); expected outputs still come from golden() EXHAUSTIVE Every input combination (at most 20 input bits) CLOCK The clock port of a clocked design, e.g. "clk" LATENCY Cycles from start to done for a clocked design TOLERANCE_ULP Map of floating-point output port to allowed ULP error; absent means exact

Match the ports and clocking in the contract and the design. Floating-point bit-pattern ports are unsigned; reinterpret their bits in golden() rather than converting the integer to a float. A loop's Python prototype is checked against the same file.

docs.title: Common refusals
docs.text:
Settings › Problem › Check (and Direct edit, and the configurator's Issues) shows one row per issue: file and line, document path, what is wrong, and the nearest known word:

not a task: the document does not load: problem.yaml: flow.plan.by is off | flux | claude | codex | opencode or an agent of your own ({run: [...]}), not 'codx'
  WARNING problem.yaml:25 flow.measure.bench.timout_s -- not a stage setting, ignored; did you mean `timeout_s`?
  ERROR problem.yaml:16 flow.plan.by -- No agent called `codx`. Did you mean `codex`? The loop won't start until this is fixed.
  • Warning: a key nobody reads (a typo, a missing box or setting) or a setting with no effect there (an agent option beside by: flux, questions on a one-turn box, by beside Design's run). Ignored; the loop runs. The run's start log repeats it.
  • Error: a value the loop cannot run with. The document does not load: not a task: and the reason, then the rows.
  • A fix, when safe, is a button beside the row (Use claude, Remove), written to the file; Open line N opens the document there.

Errors (each ends "The loop won't start until this is fixed."):

Message (start) Fix No agent called `codx`. Did you mean `codex`? A by: that names no agent, or a box's word that is its by said short (plan: codx); the row suggests the nearest `swep` is not something `search` takes: it is a search (sweep, ...), a list of phases or `module:Class` A word the key does not take; the row lists the ones it does and suggests the nearest A document does not say its `id`: it is its folder's name Rename the folder instead `statement` must be a non-empty string: what is to be made Say what is to be made REFUSED: `problem.yaml` names 1 path the loop folder does not have (the check's text, with what the folder holds) Add the listed file to the folder, or fix the key that names it 'notes.md' is not a file or folder beside ... (knowledge.library) Add the file, or list what is there `check` is never delegated to an agent: it establishes facts check and measure are commands only `{...}` is not something `design` takes: it is "flux" (FluxAgent), {run: [...]}, {catalog: [...]} or {agent: ...} One form only `flow.design.command` is not a key of a document: a command a document runs is said `run:` (and search's, baseline's, an estimate's, an agent of your own's by: {command: ...}) Say run: flow.design.agent.session is `pass` (one session per design until it is admitted ...) or `keep` Write pass or keep, or remove session from design `dse` is `search` / `extract` is `knowledge: {insights: {by: rules}}` Old names: search and knowledge.insights Who works it is by Write knowledge: {by: claude} or {by: off} `budget.parallel` is a key of an older document, which this Flux no longer reads: open the document with Flux e7a0f9cba, which says what became of it, and export it again (any key) A moved key (budget.parallel, flow.knowledge.digest, flow.measure.<stage>.command, parts:, ...): Flux e7a0f9cba names its replacement. docs.title: Searches
docs.text: What flow.search takes as a search. Search and agents explains when to use which.

docs.title: Space and seeds
docs.text:
flow.search is one form, {by: <who decides>, policy: <name>, method: <how the points are picked>, space: {...}}:

Said What runs nothing, or {by: rules} the rules pick each pass's direction and the kind of work, no AI {by: flux}, {by: tools}, {by: claude} FluxAgent, FluxAgent with its tools, an agent decides ({by: given} is the rules, under that name) {by: ..., policy: explore} (no space) the same, with that policy {method: sweep, space: {...}} that search walks the space; by beside it has no effect (a warning) {policy: explore, method: gradient, space: {...}} the search, with that policy {by: flux, space: {...}}, {by: claude, policy: explore, space: {...}} FluxAgent (or the agent) proposes the points, with that policy {run: ...} your own search (below)
  • Shorthand: search: explore is {policy: explore}, search: sweep {method: sweep}, search: claude {by: claude}; a list is {method: [...]}.
  • Refused: a space with nobody to pick its points; a search under policy: ("sweep is a search, not an intent: method: sweep"); a policy under method:.
  • A search without a space walks nothing.

A search tries points of a space of settings ("knobs"):

search:                                             # under flow:
  method: {gradient: {steps: 16, patience: 2}}     # or: method: gradient
  space:
    algorithm: [list_sieve, slice_sieve, odd_sieve]
    wheel: {values: [0, 1], when: {algorithm: [list_sieve]}}   # only moves for list_sieve
    prefetch:                                       # a component: prefetch.on, .distance, .degree
      optional: true
      distance: [1, 2, 4]
      degree: [1, 2]
    variant: {values: [baseline], from: "variants/*.py"}       # plus file stems found at load
  seeds:
    - {algorithm: list_sieve, wheel: 0}            # measured first; the first seed is home
  • space: each knob is an ordered, non-empty list of scalar choices. Order numeric choices: local searches step to neighbours.
    • A map with values may add when: {knob: choice or [choices]} (moves only then; else its first choice) and from: glob (adds matching file stems, read at every load).
    • A map with neither is a component: knobs component.knob; optional: true adds component.on. They reach commands through {point} only ({component.knob} is not substituted).
  • seeds: measured first; a missing knob takes its first choice.
  • A space must reach a command: a command names a {knob} or {point}, or the generator is a command or catalog. With a model or agent generator, a space only tunes settings.

docs.text:
Option Purpose name A label knobs Move only these (globs such as prefetch.*) hold Keep these fixed (globs too) metric, direction Its own target; default the first objective floor {metric, at} or {metric, keep, above}: designs below it are refused margin Minimum improvement, default 0 policy Its emphasis, as above
  • batch is another name for batch_size: how many designs one pass carries (what a pass carries).
  • An unknown option is refused where written (flow.search.method[1].wavee).
  • budget.designs_at_once: how many of a pass's designs are made and checked at once.
  • A finished walk does not stop an open-ended run: cap passes at Start, or with budget.passes.

docs.title: Write a loop with an agent
docs.text:
Describe the loop, attach your files, and an agent writes it: the document, its checks and measurements, and a golden model where one fits. The author is FluxAgent or a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, or one your server adds). Nothing runs until you start it.

Try it first in the Preview app: create a loop step by step starts with this way.

docs.title: New loop › Agent
docs.text:
On the Loops list, New loop › Agent. The page has four stages:

  1. Ask: name, agent, what the loop should do, and its files (drop them, or a folder or a .zip, on the form).
    • Hide from AI on a file keeps it from every agent (a gate's tests, say).
    • Ask me when unclear (on by default): the agent asks before drafting.
    • Thinking and Effort work as in Chat.
  2. Drafting: the agent's conversation, live, as in Chat.
    • Below it: the files it wrote (written, yours or removed; a lock on hidden ones), the check's last word, its tool calls and checks run.
    • Its questions show as one card.
    • Draft refused? Try again, or type a note in the message box (Enter sends).
  3. Review: its decisions by configurator step, each with its reason. Keep, Change (opens the configurator at that step) or Keep the rest. A change asked in the message box shows as a diff.
  4. Ready: the draft's check (as Settings › Problem › Check). Make loop, or Open in Configurator first. Run one pass first starts one ordinary pass to the deepest stage.

Notes:

  • The draft is a loop from Drafting on. This browser remembers it; you can come back.
  • The agent starts from a new loop's files (a README and library/). It checks its draft and repairs it until the check passes; a coding agent also proves its gate on a sample design before handing over. It never runs the loop itself.
  • When it ends, its changes come back exactly, removals and renames included. Scratch files never come back.
  • Settings › Problem › Agent on an existing loop asks an agent to change it the same way.

docs.title: Ask me when unclear
docs.text:
On, the agent asks before writing anything:

  • what your ask leaves open: objectives and goals, limits (clock, area, latency, budget), measurement stages and tools, which file is the spec or golden model, who designs;
  • up to four questions at once, each with choices and one marked Recommended;
  • the card offers a chip per question, You decide, a free answer, and a timer (10 minutes, then the agent decides);
  • its decisions say which answer decided what;
  • a long question folds behind Show all, never cut.

When revising, it asks only if the change is ambiguous. Off, it asks nothing and records each assumption in its decisions.

docs.title: One session per loop
docs.text:
A coding agent (OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex) keeps one session per loop. Every later job on the loop resumes it: a change in Review, Try again, a note, an edit from Settings › Problem › Agent. Two loops never share a session.

The conversation's first line says which: Session: resumed session (turn 3) or Session: new session (why). A new session starts when:

  • the loop has none yet;
  • you picked another agent, or its model changed;
  • the loop's folder moved;
  • the agent cannot resume (session gone, or context truly full).

A new session starts from the whole brief and the loop's files.

docs.title: When a turn is cut off
docs.text: A job ends when the agent ends its turn. A turn that times out or errors continues in the same session, a few times (three by default). Then the job ends as The agent did not finish: its files are kept, and Try again continues. Stop ends a job the same way.

docs.title: FluxAgent as the author
docs.text:
• Reads and writes the draft's folder only: no path outside it, no hidden name (.x), no path hidden from AI.
  • Checks the draft with Flux's own check and fixes it until it passes. A draft still refused comes back to it, a few times.
  • Runs nothing, so it does not prove the gate on a sample design.
  • Keeps no session between jobs.

docs.title: Check what it wrote
docs.text:
The author's loop is a first draft. Before a long run, check:

  • Checks: do they test what you care about, on enough inputs?
  • Measurements: right workload, right stage, tools_at_once: 1 for timings?
  • Objectives: the limit you meant, in the right direction?
  • Run one pass (Run one pass first on Ready, or Start with one pass) and read its results.

See Configure and Knowledge, skills, hidden paths.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Flux runs as a web server: you install it once, then everything happens in the browser. It is a Python package (Python 3.11 or newer); the hardware tools and the sandbox are optional.

To try the web app first, open the Preview app: create a loop step by step, then a tour of the app, or the tour alone.

docs.title: Install and start the server
docs.text:
The source is not public: ask the maintainer for access. From its folder (here flux-repo):

cd flux-repo
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -e "./flux[web]"
source .venv/bin/activate
flux user add me --admin
flux serve
  • flux user add makes the first account; run it as the user who should own the loops' files.
  • flux serve prints its address (default http://127.0.0.1:8765/). Open it and sign in. Every other account is made in the web app (Admin › People › Users).
  • A server started by hand is for trying Flux. For a team, install the system service.

Next: the Web app tour, then your first loop.

docs.title: Sandbox
docs.text:
Checks, runs and agents run inside a container. Install Podman (rootless, preferred) or Docker on the server's machine. Without either, a start stops with the sandbox needs Podman or Docker.

For code you trust, an admin can turn the sandbox off for one loop (Settings › Advanced). What the sandbox sees and reaches: Run, stop, resume › Sandbox.

docs.title: Hardware tools
docs.text:
Hardware loops need Verilator, Yosys, OpenROAD and other tools. Flux's Nix shell has them all, and the coding agents Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode (Models and agents).

  1. Install Nix.
  2. Add experimental-features = nix-command flakes to ~/.config/nix/nix.conf.
  3. Start the server from the shell (the first entry may build or download tools):
cd flux-repo/flux
nix develop --accept-flake-config
flux serve

The shell puts Flux on PATH: no pip install inside it.

docs.title: System service
docs.text:
A team server runs as a system service, under its own flux account. As root, from flux/:

sudo python3 scripts/install-service.py -- --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8765

The installer is safe to run again: each step already done is skipped. It makes the flux account, lets it use Nix and the binary caches, prepares rootless Podman (sub-ids, linger, cgroup controllers), clones the code, writes /etc/flux/service.env with your proxy settings, installs and enables the service, and makes the first admin (it asks a password). When something it cannot change is missing, it says what and stops. --dry-run reports what is there and what is missing, and writes nothing.

What Where Account flux, a system user Code its own clone, /opt/flux/src Web data /var/lib/flux/web Caches /var/cache/flux Settings /etc/flux/service.env, one NAME=value a line

Afterwards, everything is in the web app: updates in Admin › Server › Version, agents' logins in Account › Agents, backups in Admin › Server › Maintenance.

docs.title: Models and agents
docs.text: A loop whose designs come from a script needs no model. Otherwise set FluxAgent's endpoint and the coding agents in the web app: Models and agents.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• First loop: a complete loop in the web app, Python only.
  • Write a loop with an agent: describe it, an agent writes it.
  • Create a loop step by step in the Preview app.

docs.title: Tour
docs.text:
Flux is a shared server with accounts, used in the browser. Each user has loops; each loop is a document and its files, run sandboxed on the server. Create, check, start, stop, follow and read loops here. Install starts a server.

Try it first in the Preview app: create a loop step by step, then a tour of the app, or the tour alone.

docs.title: Loops
docs.text:
The first page lists your loops. Each row shows:

  • its state, and its design agent (who works its Design box; tinted while running);
  • its designs as "2 / 12 / 30": accepted this start / accepted / all (every design handed in); the tooltip says accepted of measured (accepted and rejected), failed and pending. The Overview's Acceptance rate is accepted ÷ measured;
  • the decision's main measurements (Settings › Measurements' Main, else the first objective), green or red against their limits;
  • Start, Stop and Restart as small icons at the row's end.

Search, filter by state, sort by activity, name or decision. Shared with me lists loops shared with you or your group, with your rights ("ask · edit · run"). Archived loops are under Archived (Archive).

Project tabs: when you see a group's project, tabs above the search filter by project: All, one per project, In no project, each with a count. Under All, a Project column names each loop's first project and "+N" others (Groups). The chosen tab is remembered in this browser.

docs.title: New loop
docs.text: Way What it does Configurator A form in six steps (Create a loop in the Preview walks through it) Create or upload An empty loop, or one from a folder, files, a .zip, or a pasted document (Paste YAML) Direct edit Write the YAML yourself Agent An agent writes it from your prompt and files (Write a loop with an agent) Clone A copy of a loop's problem, without its runs

docs.title: A loop's page
docs.text:
The header has Start (▶) at rest, Stop (■) and Restart (↻) while running.

Tab What it shows Overview State, decision and objectives, best designs, best-so-far chart, notes, the agent's questions Live The run now and every pass, as a graph or timeline (Live) Results Every design measured, charts, ideas, library (Results) Agents Every model and agent turn, newest first: where (pass, box, try), outcome, prompt, reply, tool calls, time, tokens; session info ("resumed (turn k of K)", "new session", "warm start", "shared first session") Files The loop's files and the agents' workbench (Files and settings) Settings Preferences, sharing, maintenance, the problem (Files and settings)

An agent writing or revising the problem shows a strip at the top of the Overview until the loop starts, the document changes, or six hours pass. Hide from Overview hides an ended strip. Its history: Settings › Problem › Agent.

docs.title: Overview cards
docs.text:
• Decision: the decision and its pill (✓ accepted; ! closest when nothing meets every requirement; ✗ failed), "ties with #229", "last pass 17 min ago". Hover the pill for the rule ("Decided by: smallest area_um2 at fmax_mhz >= 1000") and stage. Below: a tile per main measurement with its change from the reference, then Best 3.
    • The reference: the latest baseline at its stage, else the accepted designs' P10 (minimized) or P90 (maximized). Every page compares with the same reference.
  • Best: a chart per main measurement, titled "best cycles (-12.9%)" (or "best cycles 6189" without a baseline).
  • Starred designs (add it yourself): a tile per starred design, latest first.
  • Note to the loop and Agent asks: below.
  • Small cards (top row): State, Designs measured, Passes, Last improvement, Working now by default; up to 10.
Small card Shows Last improvement When the best design last improved ("42 min ago"), which design, which pass, passes since Pass speed Median wall time of the last 20 passes, most at once, passes per hour Working now Agents and models at work, designs per box ("11 design · 3 check · 2 measure"); "idle" at rest Idea queue Ideas queued, evaluated, and proposed but neither Uptime How long this start has run; starts today One metric One metric's best accepted value and change from the baseline ("−12.9%"); the metric you type in the layout editor, else the first objective Stage funnel Designs made → passed checks → measured on the last stage

Customize cards in Account › Profile › Customize (Overview layout); Defaults restores them. Hidden cards cost nothing to load.

docs.title: Start, stop, restart
docs.text:
Start asks how many passes (one design each) or Until stopped.

  • A trunk asks for designs and says what runs ("trunk: 2 agents (claude (opus), codex), 3 branches at once, 6 may wait"); one branch at once while parallel work is off.
  • A folder with several problems asks which; one that does not load is shown with why and a Direct edit link.
  • It checks the document first when inputs changed (as Settings › Problem › Check); on failure the button reads Start anyway.
  • A start resumes from the record. Started from the Loops list, you stay on the list (Started, with Open).
  • A failed loop shows Start again. While an agent writes the problem, Start waits.

Stop and Restart act after the current pass. The asked button turns red with an hourglass, an amber pill shows "Stops after pass 4" or "Restarts after pass 4", and the loop stays running until then. Press the other to switch. Press the same one again (it turns solid red) to act now: it asks, then abandons the pass.

docs.title: A loop's Chat
docs.text:
Chat, on every tab of a loop, opens a panel with one conversation about the loop.

  • The bar: the conversation's name (opens the list, with + New chat and Delete), Open in Chat (opens it in the top bar's Chat), Close.
  • Ask puts a question (why it stalls, which design is best, what to try) to an agent or FluxAgent. It reads the loop and changes nothing.
  • Thinking & commands under an answer shows how it was made.
  • Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line.
  • A dot on Chat means the loop's agent is asking you something.
  • The loop's chats share a Chat workbench (editors only), separate from the loop's own workbench/ (A loop's Chat workbench).
  • Old #/app/NAME/ask and #/app/NAME/talk links open it; #/app/NAME/chat/ID opens one conversation.

Note to the loop (Overview card): a note sent while the loop runs reaches its agents at the next step (a trunk: each agent's next turn), and every step while it stands.

  • Enter sends. A loop at rest has no box.
  • Notes are listed newest first. A filled dot: read ("Read at pass 14"); a ring: waiting.
  • The latest three show; N more shows up to twenty.
  • Editors remove a note with its bin. An unread note then never arrives; a read one leaves the agents' next messages.

Agent asks (Overview card): the agent's question with its choices, You decide and a free answer; your answer goes as a note. Answered questions are listed below. Hidden when there is nothing.

The question's line above the tabs, and the bell, lead there. With the card hidden, Answer opens a dialog.

Chat in the top bar is the same, bound to no loop (Chat); its rail lists your loops' conversations (Loop chats).

docs.title: Everywhere
docs.text:
• Top bar: Chat · Loops · Groups · Admin (admins). New loop is at the end of the Loops list's search bar.
  • Theme: system, light or dark; remembered in this browser.
  • Your name opens Account. While an admin views as a user, it shows that user's name.
  • Bell: a run ends or fails, an agent asks, a loop is shared with you.
  • Browser tab: names what is open ("cpu_tune — Loop", "CPU block diagram — Chat"). Its icon's dot: pink something waits for you, red failed, blue running or answering.
