  • Live updates: pages refresh only what changed, keeping your scroll and selection. An editor you are typing in is never replaced: Changed on the server offers Reload. A background tab pauses and catches up when you return.
  • Long lists load more as you scroll ("N of M").
  • Raw and Fullscreen on files, logs, results and agent turns.
  • Addresses name the view: #/app/NAME/live/timeline, #/app/NAME/settings/problem?step=graph.
  • Phone: account items move to the menu button; lists and tabs stack.

The Preview app runs these pages on sample data.

docs.title: Server and admin
docs.text: Run a Flux server, manage accounts, groups and projects, and set the server's agents, sandbox, chat and maintenance.

docs.title: The server
docs.text:
Installing and starting one: Install; for a team, the system service. Everything else is on these pages.

  • Data: the database, secret.key (encrypts keys and secrets) and every loop. Back up the database and secret.key together (Admin › Server › Maintenance), loop folders separately. Never copy the database alone while the server runs (Backups and restore).
  • Limits: a loop holds up to 100,000 files and 8 GB; one upload 900 files and 256 MB. Runs at once per user: each user's Limits cell (Accounts).
  • Restarts: running loops are found again; their containers keep running meanwhile.
  • TLS proxy: for others to reach the server, put one in front; it must not buffer the live connection (nginx: the server sends X-Accel-Buffering: no).
  • Slow requests (over 0.5 s) are logged; the latest 50 are in Admin › Activity › Resources.
  • Worker processes: heavy pages are made in 2 to 4 worker processes (40-130 MB each).
  • Before login, only the sign-in page is served. Logging in or out in one tab updates the others.
  • After an update, open pages load the new version once.

docs.title: Agents' Tests
docs.text:
A start waits until each agent its problem names passed its Test for the loop's owner, with the current configuration ("Codex not set up for cedric yet (its configuration changed since its Test)"). A new agent version needs new Tests.

  • Each user tests their own in Account › Agents: run in their home with their settings; no credential is seen.
  • Admin › Server › Maintenance › Test agents runs them for every user on a schedule (or Run now): each user's set-up agents ("set up": logged in, own key, endpoint, model or variable, or tested before), in their loops' contexts. Disabled users are skipped.
  • A Test times out after 420 s. A failure is listed in Admin › Loops › Failures.
  • Audited as the user's "agent test". Not counted in usage.

docs.title: Accounts
docs.text:
Admin › People › Users makes an account: a name, a password (empty: an invitation link to send the user) and a group, then Add. Links work once, for a week; there is no mail.

Admin › People › Users: a row per user with Admin, Create, Run, Internals, a Limits cell (loops at once; Active off disables the account), groups (×, +), Last active, Show usage, and ⋯: View as (read-only), a reset or invitation link, Rename, Delete.

Permission Gives Admin Administers the server and every loop. Implies Create, Run, Internals. You cannot clear your own Create loops Makes loops Run loops and agents Runs loops, Ask and agents Internals ("See how Flux works") Agents' prompts, thinking and commands; Flux's skills; diagram source; workbenches; the full log and record; search reasoning. Without it, turns show only replies and counts (Live); a Chat proposal is accepted by someone who has it. No group or project role gives it; audited
  • A new password logs the user out everywhere (from a link or an admin). Changed on their own Account, it keeps the current session.
  • Settings layer field by field: the server's, then each group's (by group name; later wins), then the user's. An empty field inherits. Keys and models never pair with a lower layer's endpoint; token prices are the endpoint's layer's (A group's agents).
  • Groups: a user is in none, one or several. Admin › People › Groups lists each group with members, Open projects level (Asker by default), Rename and Delete. Unrolled: the member grid (Level, a box per word, ×; All members; People adds as Member). The same grid serves projects and loop Sharing.
  • Group membership gives nothing on any loop (the words).
  • A loop is reached only by a share or by a project it is linked into. Your rights are your row, your groups' rows and your projects', together. Ask and Run also need Run loops and agents.
  • Archive, reset, delete, rename and transfer belong to the owner and admins.

docs.title: The words
docs.text:
One vocabulary everywhere.

  • Loop words: view, ask, edit, run (on a shared loop or a project's loops); share (a loop's own: give the loop to others, at most what you hold).
  • Place words: link (link your loops into a project), curate (review knowledge, keep the library), manage (members, levels, access, title; rename, archive, delete), create (groups only: make projects; the maker is Lead).
Place Words Loop share view · ask · edit · run · share Group membership curate · manage · create Project level view · ask · edit · run · link · curate · manage Global project level curate · manage

Levels (a mix is Custom):

Level Words Loop Project Group Global project Member none -- yes yes yes Viewer view yes yes -- -- Asker view · ask yes yes -- -- Contributor view · ask · edit · run · link yes (no link) yes -- -- Maintainer Contributor and curate, create (on a loop: view · ask · edit · run · share) yes yes curate · create curate Lead every word -- yes curate · manage · create curate · manage
  • A loop's levels stop at Maintainer; Owner is shown, never given.
  • Words acting on a loop imply view.
  • Managers give levels up to their own; admins any.
  • Why some boxes are missing: linking needs share on the loop and link on the project; a loop is not curated; managing a loop is the owner's; groups never carry loop words or share; projects do not nest; a global project's visibility gives view and it gives no loop words.

What a group gives on its projects' loops: only the project's group access: invite (default; nothing, hidden), view, or open (the project's open level, Asker by default). Its curate, manage and create reach every project of the group.

Global projects are public (everyone sees them) or private (members and admins only). Members hold only curate or manage. Only admins and managers see others' loops in one. Who links: everyone or admins (a private one: members only).

docs.title: Renames
docs.text:
• User (admins: ⋯ › Rename): everything moves (folder, caches, settings, shares, runs, schedules, chats, usage). Refused while anything of theirs runs. No redirects: people their loops are shared with, and the user, are told the new link. Sessions stay. One "rename user" audit entry.
  • Group (pencil in Admin › People › Groups): members, permissions and shares stay; members are told. Names ignore case; _ reserved, / refused. Refused while a linked loop runs.

docs.title: Deletes
docs.text:
• Active off disables a user: logged out, everything kept.
  • ⋯ › Delete (admins): the dialog lists their loops, sole-managed projects, shares and groups, and asks whether their loops are transferred to a user (a clashing name becomes <loop>-<user>) or deleted. Everything else of theirs goes; the audit and history stay. Refused while anything of theirs runs, for yourself, and for the last admin. Type their name to confirm.
  • Groups › Delete: refused while it has projects (archived too; listed with links). It lists members, shared loops, its agents and settings (loops naming its agents will not start) and its machines (revoked). Type its name. Members keep their accounts and loops.

docs.title: A group's agents
docs.text:
A group's Agents tab (#/groups/<id>/agents, admins and managers) is the layer between the server's settings and each member's.

  • FluxAgent and a tab per agent: endpoint, model, key, seconds per turn, prices (turns at once stay the server's, except for the group's own agents). A set field shows "over server"; an empty one "from server"; ↺ resets. Keys are encrypted and shown only as "set".
  • Per agent: variables, instructions (after the server's, before each member's), thinking by default, and Test (counts for each member who inherits exactly that configuration).
  • All agents: variables for every agent.
  • + Add: a group's own agent (name, kind OpenCode/Claude Code/Codex, label, extra arguments). Documents name it <group>/<name> (group name lower-cased, other characters _: Team A/foo is team_a/foo), or by name alone if unambiguous (by: foo is refused if two groups have one). It shows program not found until its program is found here.
  • Audited (group settings, group agent added, changed, removed), never values. Members see the result in Account › Agents.
  • A renamed group's agents become <new>/<name>; <old>/<name> still works until reused.
  • A member removed from a group loses its layer from their next run.

docs.title: A group's schedule
docs.text:
The Schedule card schedules the group's own agents' turns at once, as Scheduled changes do (+ Schedule, Run now, Edit, Turn off/Turn on, Delete). Never above the admin's limits:

  • the stricter of the group's and the admin's value applies;
  • an agent on the same endpoint as a server agent shares its slots;
  • the server's pause and running limits still apply.

The card says when the admin's limit is stricter ("The admin's limit is stricter: at most 2 at once (shared with OpenCode on box.example:8080)"). Audited (group schedule). Admin › Maintenance › Schedule lists them read-only.

docs.title: Projects
docs.text:
A project belongs to one group (<group>/<name>) or is global (_/<name>, shown "global / …"). Names: letters, digits, -, _, unique per group regardless of case. See Groups and a project's page.

A group's project is made on the group's page (New project: name, title, group access), a global one by admins (New global project in Admin › People › Projects). Members, levels, access, rename, archive and delete are on the project's page (Groups).

  • Levels: the words on a project. The maker is Lead. A Member sees the project and its members only.
  • Group access: invite (default; hidden), view, open (the open level).
  • Rights only add up: group access, group membership's curate/manage, project level, a global project's visibility.
  • A project's contents (files, knowledge, chats) are its own members' and admins' only (Groups).
  • Members with create make a group's projects; only admins make global ones.
  • Archiving hides and freezes a project. Everything is audited.

Admin › People › Projects lists every project: title, address, group, loops, members, library use ("6 B of 2 KB", over when above). Per global project: Visibility, Who links loops. Row tools: open, rename, archive/unarchive, delete. New global project is below.

Library limits: Library limit for every project (GB), or a row's Limit; empty inherits (finally a loop's 8 GB). Audited ("library limit"). An over-limit library cannot grow.

docs.title: Loops in projects
docs.text:
A loop is in none, one or several projects, in an order its owner sets. Only its owner (or an admin) links it: into a group's project where they hold link, or a global one per its join rule. Archived projects take none.

  • In a group's project, members get their loop words on it; the group's members what its access gives. Never takes rights away. Ask and run still need Run loops and agents.
  • A global project gives no rights; users see only their own loops there.
  • Each link has learning (the collector): on by default in a group's project; in a global one off until an admin or manager turns it on.
  • Renamed or transferred loops keep their projects; a deleted project unlinks its loops and tells the owners.

The owner sets them in the loop's Settings › Preferences › Projects (Files and settings): Add to a project…, the order, Learns, ✕. A project's page lists its loops.

docs.title: Your account
docs.text:
Account has four tabs (#/account/agents; #/account opens Profile):

  • Profile: your groups, usage, password (asks the current one; logs out other sessions), desktop notifications, Overview layout.
  • Agents: a tab per agent: login, Test, model, variables, your own instructions; All agents for shared variables. Fields show "from server", "from group", or "over group" with ↺. Your groups' own agents have tabs too.
  • Machines: your machines (Add my machine) and the others your loops may use (Machines).
  • Shared links: every link you made (Share), with opens, Copy, Revoke; stopped when you lost the right.

An agent is used only once its Test passed for whoever starts the loop. Tests run at once, outside any limit (Agents' Tests). Logins run in the sandbox in a small terminal; Claude Code's token is stored encrypted. Without its own settings an agent uses its own configuration (Models and agents).

docs.title: Admin
docs.text:
Five tabs; each opens on the sub-tab last used in this browser. Old addresses (#/admin/users, #/admin/insights) still work.

Tab Sub-tab What it holds Loops All loops Every user's loops; pause new starts; stop or restart all after their pass; execution Failures Failed starts and agent Tests People Users Users and permissions, invitations, View as Groups Every group and its members Projects Every project Runtime Agents FluxAgent and each agent: program, login, model, key, seconds per turn, token prices, turns at once per endpoint, enabled, offered for Ask, thinking by default, instructions; + Add agent Machines Every machine, this server first Sandbox Limits, network, PATH directories mounted, what every user's home starts with Chat What users may use in Chat (Chat) Activity Resources CPU, memory, disks over time; the tool pool (resource hints); sandbox containers; disk per loop Usage Usage and cost by user and agent; disk now Endpoints How each endpoint did; hosts the network refused Commands What the loops' agents ran (Commands) Audit The audit trail, newest first; filter by What, Who and search Server Version The running commit, updates, Update and Roll back (Version) Maintenance Scheduled tasks and setting changes
  • Keys are encrypted and never shown again. With nothing set, runs use the machine's configuration (~/.config/flux/flux.env, each agent's own).
  • Model of an agent without an endpoint: From the agent lists the agent's own models (as each user's login sees them); Default (the agent's own) leaves it to the agent; with the box off, type any name.
  • Which model wins: a document's model:, then the loop's variable, then Account › Agents, then Admin › Runtime › Agents.
  • An agent's panel shows: installed (path on hover) or missing ("claude is not on the runs' PATH"), kind, version, document name; Connection and Verification pills with Test; Program, Name shown; Enabled, Offered for Ask, Thinks by default and efforts.
  • Users are offered only agents whose program is found; a document naming another shows (not available).
  • An added agent runs its own Program (or FLUX_<NAME>_BIN), else its kind's.

docs.title: Enabled
docs.text:
Untick Enabled to switch an agent off. It is offered nowhere (a document naming it shows (disabled by an admin)), and starts, chats, asks and Tests naming it are refused: claude is disabled on this server by an admin. Running loops keep it until they stop. Audited (agent disabled, agent enabled).

Other agents of the same kind are unaffected: an added aide of kind claude still runs its own Program, else the built-in's, else FLUX_CLAUDE_BIN, else claude on PATH. Use Enabled, not a bogus Program, to disable.

docs.title: Thinking by default
docs.text:
Each agent's panel sets whether it Thinks by default (where a loop's box does not say: Thinking; and how Chat's Think starts: Chat), with its effort when thinking and when not (its own leaves it to the agent). FluxAgent's efforts: low, medium, high, max; built in is high thinking, medium not.

Thinks by default Effort when thinking when not Each agent on its own its kind's lowest (low, or minimal) FluxAgent off built in (high) built in (medium)

Precedence: a chat's Think, then the loop's box, then this default. Audited (thinking by default); applies to runs started afterwards.

Structured answers (FluxAgent, on by default): asks the model for answers in a fixed shape; a design answer not in that shape is asked for once more, never read from the text. Turn it off for a model server that cannot: designs are then read from the reply's text, and the run's log says so.

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text: Instructions: text given to the agent with every task (loops, Chat, New loop › Agent, its Test). Not FluxAgent. OpenCode ships with a default (Default restores it). At most 4,000 characters; audited (agent instructions). Groups and users add their own after the server's (Account › Agents); a loop's turns use its owner's.

docs.title: Resources
docs.text:
• Over time: CPU, memory, disks (30 days), beside every loop's tokens per second.
  • Sandbox containers: CPU, memory, processes. Whose: a loop's (Stop after its pass), Chat · user (Stop), Login · user, Agent test · user. left behind containers have Kill (the clean-up removes them too).
  • Compiler caches: each user's ccache size.
  • Disk per loop.
  • Machine picker: this server or a joined machine (its CPU, load, memory, disks, steps; a storage machine's bytes served). Figures arrive with each heartbeat (~15 s), kept 30 days.
  • Orphan caches: sandbox caches no loop owns (a deleted loop's, or not the web's). Each says whether Clean disk removes it next (goes at the next clean) or why not (in use, used in the last 14 days). Clean now runs that part; Delete removes one. A cache owned by another account shows the command to run (podman unshare rm -rf <cache> or sudo -u <owner> rm -rf <cache>).
  • Slow requests: the latest 50 over 0.5 s, and where heavy pages are made (in 4 worker processes, 60 MB each).

docs.title: The memory guard
docs.text:
When the machine runs short of memory (RAM above Stop above, 95%, with swap over the Swap mark, 80%, or filling), the server stops the loop using the most memory, then the next, until RAM is under Until under (90%). A chat sandbox can be stopped too.

  • The loop ends failed; earlier passes are kept. Why it stopped says e.g. Stopped to free memory: the machine was at 96% (30.7 GB of 32.0 GB); this loop used 11.4 GB, the most of any.
  • Logged, audited (memory guard), and the owner is notified. It is not restarted.
  • The Server card shows memory and swap use and the last stop. Edit sets on/off and the marks (50% to 99%); audited (memory guard settings).

docs.title: The sandbox scratch cap
docs.text:
A loop's sandbox scratch (pass working files) is capped by its Scratch /tmp size: the loop's own (Settings › Advanced), else the server's default (Admin › Runtime › Sandbox › Limits), held to the maximum. None set: no cap.

Clean disk trims each scratch every five minutes, oldest first; never recent files, a running loop's current work, or the baseline's and decision's files. Reported in the loop's log, Maintenance history and Disk per loop (trimmed 4.2 GiB today). Trimmed files show no longer kept.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Admin › Activity › Commands summarises what the loops' agents ran over 1, 7 or 30 days (UTC), per loop, agent and mode: commands and flags that do not exist, each flux command's uses and failures, shell programs and tools, commands repeated across turns, turns and failures. No output beyond known error lines. Export saves JSON. Up to a minute behind.

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text:
Task What it does Its setting Clean disk Reaps containers no process runs (every minute); trims scratch (every 5 minutes); warns of low disk (hourly); removes old pass folders (a run's newest stays), a loop's sandbox cache unused 14 days, orphan caches untouched 14 days; optionally old files in FLUX_TMPDIR older than (days), 3; Flux's temporary folder too Condense history Logs over 50 MB and journals over 20 MB keep their recent part (older gzipped); old transcript turns keep only usage. Never results, ideas or decisions older than (days), 14 Compact and check Compacts and checks the database and every record; loads each stopped loop's document; with backups kept over 0, saves the database and secret.key to backups/ backups kept, 0 (no backup) Prune server tables Expired sessions and invitations; old login failures, notifications, refused-host log; old audit lines older than (days), 30; audit (days), 365 (0: all kept) Prune run history Keeps each loop's latest starts in the run list keep, 200 Test agents Off by default: the agents' Tests, below none Clean leftovers Off by default: what updates leave behind, below. Never a record none
  • Default schedules: Clean disk every minute; Compact and check and Clean leftovers weekly; the others daily. Every run is audited.
  • Running loops are touched only where the table says; archived loops only by checks and compaction.
  • Record edits are the loop's own (Settings › Record, never scheduled): Prune stale records, Prune empty starts, Prune failed designs (pick a stage, or Any stage; e.g. Deletes 143 failed designs (stage gate) in bob/x: their rows, their designs' text and the pass files only they have ... Cannot be undone.), Invalidate all, Re-Evaluate (Results).
  • Test agents: each user's set-up agents, in their loops' contexts, and the server's shared configurations as the first admin (Agents' Tests). Two at once; outside limits; audited "(by maintenance)". One failure fails the run; a user whose Test newly fails is told.
  • Clean leftovers (after an update, or weekly), on every loop at rest or one:
Left behind By Removed when problem.yaml.orig, NAME.problem.yaml.orig beside a loop's document an earlier Flux's document migration kept the original the document is there and loads files in the data folder's kept/ the server, to start sooner after a restart, named for its code made by other code than the server runs now (never read again), or half-written by a process gone over an hour ago

It never removes records: out/.NAME.db.before-vN copies and stray -wal, -shm, -journal files are listed as kept for you to delete. It skips running loops. Each removal is audited. Old prepared environments are removed by updates themselves.

Tabs: Tasks (running, queued, failed, done, off), Schedule (scheduled changes), History (every run, the last 1000; chips Failed, Schedule, Run now).

  • Each task has Run now and Edit. One task runs at a time; others queue (queued · 2nd, Cancel). A restart drops the queue.
  • Run now asks first when it deletes or rewrites data (Deletes pass folders older than 3 days in 12 loops (3 running) ... Cannot be undone.), and says nothing when there is nothing to do. Also from Edit › One loop › Run and a loop's own Settings.
  • On one loop: Clean disk trims scratch, removes old pass folders and its sandbox cache; Condense history condenses its log, journal and transcript; Compact and check compacts, checks and loads its document.
  • Schedules: every N minutes, hours or days; daily at a time on picked days; or cron. A time already past waits for the next day.

docs.title: Backups and restore
docs.text:
Back up server database saves the database and secret.key to backups/server-<time>/ while the server runs.

To restore:

  1. Stop the server.
  2. Move flux-web.db and any flux-web.db-wal and flux-web.db-shm aside (keep them).
  3. Put the backup's flux-web.db and secret.key in the data folder.

  4. Start the server.

  5. Never copy a database in while the server runs.

  6. A start that finds mismatched files is refused, naming them; nothing is deleted. Copy all three together before moving any: the -wal holds committed changes.

docs.title: Scheduled changes
docs.text:
+ Schedule: pick a kind, its fields, then when.

Kind What it does Turns at once Sets an agent endpoint's turns at once or FluxAgent's requests at once (whole number; 0 no limit). Group agents are scheduled by the group (A group's schedule) Pause starts Pauses new starts with a reason (up to 200 characters), or resumes. Running loops go on; starts and restarts are refused with the reason Running limit A user's running-loops limit (0–64, or default), or the server's default (0–64, or default). New starts only Stop loops Stops running loops after their pass: all, one user's, or one. Now stops at once Start a loop Starts one loop as its owner, with its last start's options, for 1–1000 passes or until stopped. Refused (a failed run) if gone, archived, owner disabled or at limit, starts paused, or already running
  • When: daily at a time on picked days, or Advanced: cron expression (*/15 9-17 * * 1-5: every 15 minutes, 09:00-17:59, weekdays). Server time zone, shown.
  • Each row: schedule, next and last run, result, Run now, Edit, Turn off/Turn on, Delete.
  • Changes apply at every loop's next turn. Lowering a limit stops no running turn.
  • A missed stop or start is not done later. Settings (pause, limits) take their latest past value when the server starts.
  • Audited, e.g. scheduled: Claude Code turns at once → 4 (was 1).

Example: people by day, loops by night:

Change When Claude Code turns at once → 1 daily at 08:00, Mon–Fri Claude Code turns at once → 4 daily at 20:00, every day

A nightly run: Start a loop at 20:00 until stopped; Pause starts at 20:05 (nightly runs); Stop loops at 07:00 after their pass; Pause starts → Resume starts at 07:30.

docs.title: Parallel work
docs.text:
A loop runs one agent turn and one tool step at a time unless an admin ticks Allow parallel work in its Settings › Preferences › Advanced; then its document says how much.

  • One agent turn at a time counts every agent and model turn of the run (designs, repairs, a trunk's agents, the passes' knowledge steps and buds). Knowledge steps (papers, workbench, ideas cleanup) go after the designs' turns; a FluxAgent cleanup lets a design in between two of its requests.
  • One tool step at a time: one design's check and measurements at a time.
  • pipeline: true still pipelines: the next design's agent turn runs while the previous design is checked and measured. Live says parallel work is off.
  • This holds on the server and on server machines. On its owner's own machine a run may always work in parallel; on a group's machine, per the group's Allow parallel work on our machines (Machines).
  • Running limits, turns at once and pauses still apply.

docs.title: Execution
docs.text: Admin › Loops › Controls › Execution says how loops run from their next start: Shared (the default) or Old loops (fallback), the way loops ran before, kept while the shared way is new. A loop that is running keeps its way until it ends. Each change is in Audit.

docs.title: Sandbox
docs.text: Every run is sandboxed unless a loop's Settings › Preferences › Advanced (admins) says otherwise. Network: open, or an allowlist; HTTP(S) goes through the proxy; raw TCP/UDP is per loop (Sandbox).

docs.title: Allowlists
docs.text:
Every allowlist (sandbox, Chat, a loop's extra hosts, an agent's hosts):

Entry Allows dl.acm.org that host only *.acm.org or .acm.org acm.org and every subdomain (dl.acm.org, www.acm.org, a.b.acm.org) 10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.1.20, ::1 the addresses in the range, or that address localhost this machine (127.0.0.1, ::1)
  • Separate by new lines, commas, semicolons or spaces; # comments.
  • Case, a trailing dot and a port are ignored (DL.ACM.org.:443 is dl.acm.org); a pasted URL keeps its host.
  • * alone is refused: choose open.
  • The page shows how it reads (Understood as: acm.org and its subdomains · arxiv.org only).
  • A redirect to another domain is refused by that host. Recently blocked lists refused hosts; click to add. The agent sees: flux sandbox: refused www.acm.org (not on the network allowlist -- add www.acm.org or *.acm.org).

Limits apply to every sandbox (runs, checks, chats, the author, Tests, logins). For CPUs, memory, processes and scratch /tmp:

  • Default: when the loop sets none.
  • Maximum: higher asks are clamped (memory 8 GB clamped to 1 GB by the server).
  • Empty: no limit (processes: 4096).

CPUs: e.g. 2 or 0.5, up to the machine's count. Memory and scratch in GB (128, 0.5), memory up to the machine's RAM. Scratch also caps disk use (the sandbox scratch cap). Audited (sandbox limits); new sandboxes only. Read-only on a server started without the sandbox.

docs.title: Proxy
docs.text:
The proxy for runs, agents, Chat, logins, the author, and Flux's model calls, sandboxed or not.

  • From the host (default): the server's environment, /etc/environment, /etc/environment.d/*.conf, ~/.config/environment.d/*.conf, then the login shell's exports. Shown as e.g. From /etc/environment: HTTP http://proxy:3128 · not for .corp.example.org.
  • Set here: HTTP and HTTPS proxies (http://host:port, optionally user:password@) and a not through it list (hosts, .domain, *.domain, IPs, CIDRs). Credentials are encrypted and shown as http://***@proxy:3128.
  • Sandboxes get HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, NO_PROXY (localhost always added).
  • In effect shows the result. Audited (sandbox proxy); applies to what starts afterwards.

docs.title: Chat
docs.text:
Admin › Runtime › Chat sets what users may use in Chat; users switch allowed features per chat.

Feature Allowed Default Chat tab The user has Chat in the top bar. Off, every other feature is off too. on Network beyond the base allowlist A chat may also reach the hosts listed under Network beyond the base (These hosts), or any host when it is Open. off Workbench A chat may read and write the user's workbench. on Loop access A chat may read the user's loops, their own and those shared with them, read-only. on
  • Everyone is the server's value; Overrides per group and user (default, on, off). User beats group beats server; among groups, off wins. Add user adds a row.
  • Chats always have the sandbox's base allowlist (Sandbox). With nothing listed and not Open, the network feature stays off.
  • A disabled feature is greyed with why (turned off by the admin on this server, for the group …, for you).
  • Applies from each chat's next message. Audited (chat permissions, chat created, chat deleted).

FluxAgent on the web (web tools; only with the chat's Network on; never private addresses):

Setting Default MB each 50 1 to 500. A larger download is refused. Seconds a fetch 60 5 to 300. Ports beyond 80 and 443 none For example 8080. Other ports are refused. Web search None SearXNG (its address, for example https://searx.example.org), or Brave Search (its subscription token).
  • Paper search needs export.arxiv.org and api.openalex.org allowed.
  • The search provider is reached as set, regardless of the host list.
  • The Brave key is encrypted; replace or Clear it. Fetches are audited (chat web).

Other limits:

Setting Default Range Minutes per coding-agent answer 8 1 to 60 Tool calls per coding-agent answer 40 5 to 400 Diagram tries (Chat) 5 0 to 10 Attached MB each (Attached files) 50 1 to 2048 Attached Files a message 10 1 to 50 Sandbox kept idle (minutes; 0: one sandbox per answer) 30 0 to 240
  • An answer stopped at a limit keeps what was written; with nothing written it fails, naming the limit.
  • How Think starts: thinking by default.
  • Answers run sandboxed under the server's limits with the user's agent settings.
  • A user's chats share one sandbox. It restarts when chat, sandbox, proxy, agent or model settings change, or Flux is updated; an answer in progress is rewritten (restarted: the admin changed the chat settings, restarted: Flux was updated).

docs.title: Sharing
docs.text:
Sharing governs read-only links (Share):

  • Links for anyone (on): off stops making and opening them (signed-in links unaffected).
  • The longest a link for anyone lasts: 1, 7, 30 or 90 days (default 90).
  • Per user: link count and Revoke (all of theirs).

Links are rate-limited and built with the maker's current rights. View as cannot make links. Audited under Shared links.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Applied in order, later wins: the server's (Admin › Runtime › Agents › All agents), the user's (Account), each linked project (the first project wins; Groups › Variables), the loop's (Settings › Preferences). Secrets are encrypted. Sandbox variables, PATH, HOME and model settings cannot be set.

docs.title: Version
docs.text:
Admin › Server › Version shows the running code and updates it, fast-forward on main only.

Tile Shows Running The commit's short hash and subject Update "Up to date" or "3 commits behind origin/main" with Update to; "origin/main · checked 2 min ago"; Check now; queued or building updates (Cancel) Up Uptime ("57 min") Checkout Branch (amber off main), clean or changed files, path Nix The toolchain's locked revisions; the prepared environment (a toolchain change is built before the restart)
  • Checks: opening the tab fetches origin/main when due (daily; hourly after a failure), in the background. A failed check keeps the last good result. Check now checks at once.
  • Update: refused off main, with local changes, or when main diverged. Running loops finish on their version. A loop started on a dirty checkout holds updates until it ends.
  • Toolchain changes build the new environment first, in the background (the tab follows the build); then fast-forward and restart. A failed build changes nothing. Code-only updates go at once.
  • Roll back: to the commit the last update came from, while the checkout is unchanged. Refused with local changes or while a loop runs on the checkout itself.
  • Records: a newer Flux upgrades a loop's record once (next start, or Compact and check), keeping a copy. A running loop's record waits.
  • Old data: this Flux reads records from version 7 and loop files from Nov 12, 2026. Older ones are refused naming Flux 9957e3728 (open, start or import there, export again). A loop file with old box names (generate:, orchestrate:, ...) or params:: convert in Flux fdfd1faf0 (Server › Old data › Migrate). A document with an old key names the Flux that explains it. Nothing is converted here.
  • History: who, when, from, to, result; also audited.

The system service restarts itself after an update. A server started by hand says to restart it.

docs.title: Chat
docs.text: Chat (top bar) is a conversation with an agent or FluxAgent, bound to no loop. Ask about your loops, a paper, an idea; have it write a script or keep notes. Available when an admin enables it (Admin › Runtime › Chat).

docs.title: The page
docs.text:
The rail (left) lists chats; the conversation is in the middle; Settings (the sliders, top right) opens on the right.

Rail tabs: Chats (yours), Loops (Loop chats), Projects (Project chats), then + and Close. Arrow keys, Home and End move between tabs. A tab with a question waiting shows a dot.

  • + starts a chat where you are: your own, or on the open loop or project.
  • Chats: a Search box, then Pinned, Today, This week, Earlier. A spinner marks a chat being answered; a dot marks one asking you (the top bar's Chat too).
  • A chat's more menu (three dots): Pin / Unpin (yours alone), Rename, Delete (removes messages and answers; the workbench stays).
  • Close hides the rail; the menu button brings it back.

Your messages are on the right, answers below. Under each answer: the agent, how long it took, and Thinking & commands (the terminal icon). Files the answer wrote are listed under it (↳ designs/adder8_csel4.sv); click to open.

The message box:

  • Enter sends (also Ctrl+Enter, ⌘+Enter); Shift+Enter adds a line.
  • Pick the agent inside the box (agents offered for Ask, with your settings: Models and agents). A ! means it is not ready: click for Test and Set up.
  • Think: a slower, more considered answer. Each agent starts as the admin set it (thinking by default); your browser remembers your choice per agent.
  • Effort (with Think on, for coding agents): Claude Code low to max, Codex none to xhigh, OpenCode minimal to max; default is its thinking effort. FluxAgent's Effort (low to max) shows always.
  • One answer at a time per chat. The row shows Sending…, Starting…, Starting OpenCode…, then the agent's current command, with Stop.
  • A stopped answer is kept, marked Stopped before it ended. A failed one says why with Retry.
  • Opening a chat picks the agent of its last answer.
  • Answers run in your own sandbox, kept warm between messages (the admin sets how long). An answer interrupted by a settings change or update restarts (restarted: …).
  • Coding agents have time and tool-call limits set by the admin.

docs.title: Attached files
docs.text:
Attach with the paperclip, by dropping on the conversation, or by pasting (a screenshot becomes pasted--.png).

  • Each uploads at once as a chip above the box (Remove takes it off) and goes with your next message.
  • Limits: 50 MB per file, 10 per message, unless the admin changes them.
  • Kept in the workbench's uploads/ (workbench on), else in the answer's attached/. Names never overwrite (notes (2).md).
  • Coding agents open any file with their own tools. FluxAgent reads text, PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OpenDocument, not pictures.
  • In a loop's Chat: editors' files go to the Chat workbench's uploads/; others' stay with the answer. Never in the loop's own folders.

docs.title: Pictures, diagrams and charts
docs.text:
Answers are Markdown. Code blocks have Copy; a block opened with four backticks or ~~~ can hold ``` fences.

  • Pictures: ![caption](/workbench/plots/speed.png), or library/... in a loop or project chat. PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP and SVG. Click to open the viewer (wheel or pinch to zoom, drag to move, Fit or 0, Esc to close). Anything else (web addresses, data:, paths outside the workbench or library) stays as text.
  • **``svg**: drawn in the page's colours. Classes:box,edge,label, tonesink,muted,line,surface,accent,ok,warn,bad, tintsbox tint-1tobox tint-6`.
  • **``figure**: HTML cards and containers for drawings no diagram kind fits. Root; classescard,group,group dashed, tones,tint-1–tint-6,grid cols-3, icons, arrows in. Scripts, handlers, frames, images, forms, links and outsideurl()` are removed.
  • ```diagram: a short YAML that names parts and picks a kind; Flux lays it out.
  • ```chart: JSON; drawn like Results' charts.
  • Save to the workbench writes a drawing as plots/<name>.svg (a diagram's YAML beside it as plots/<name>.diagram.yaml).
  • Nothing an agent wrote runs: drawings are shown as images.
  • Without the Internals permission, svg, figure and diagram blocks arrive as finished pictures (Fullscreen and Save image only, no source). Charts are the same for everyone.
  • ```mermaid is no longer drawn: old answers show it as code to admins, a note to others.

    • Diagram kinds:

    Kind Draws pipeline Stages in columns, pipeline registers between, back edges in lanes below cycle Equal steps in a row, back edges below, an optional band architecture Rows of cards and groups (name, muted line, icon) layers Stacked bands; a bus joins every box beside it blocks Free composition: boxes, stores, states, start/end dots, buses, nested groups; state machines and flow charts (@decision diamonds) timing Waveforms: one word a cycle (0 1 . x A0 z), phases, edge arrows (valid@2 -> ready@4: handshake), skipped cycles (~12), gated clock (c); also week plans memory A memory map, highest address on top, holes shown, nested regions sequence Participants, lifelines, messages, dotted replies, alt and loop frames register A register map: rows by offset, fields by bit network A topology by name and size (topology: mesh 8x8, torus, ring, tree, fat-tree, butterfly, Clos, hypercube, dragonfly), routes, attached blocks (attach: {R00: [MC0 @storage]}) matrix A table of cells (a cache's sets by ways, a reservation table) panels Up to four drawings on one image, a chart among them sankey Flows From -> To: amount; percent: source or percent: total adds shares
    • In blocks, edges place things ("A -> B"); place: lines add the rest ("Registers under Execute"). Ports (Adder.a), bundles (A, B -> X, Y), layout: ring.
    • Ranges name many parts (R00..R33). Edge widths: @wide, @narrow. legend: explains tones.
    • Roles tint parts: @compute, @storage, @interconnect, @io, @control, @external; @accent highlights.
    kind: cycle
title: The loop
steps: [Search: What to try, Design: Make it, Check: Verify it, Measure: Evaluate it, Choose: Select it]
back:
  - Check -> Design: Failed check
legend: {bad: a failed check goes back}
    • Flux sizes and routes everything so nothing overlaps and it fits the column. A label with no room becomes a number with a key. Too wide: it reflows, else is drawn wider and fitted.
    • A block with mistakes shows its errors instead ("edge 3: unknown box 'Excute' (did you mean Execute?)"), and Ask to fix drafts a fix request.
    • Before you see an answer, Flux sends a broken diagram back to the agent, up to 5 times (Diagram tries in Admin › Runtime › Chat; 0 turns it off). The row says Fixing the diagram (2 of 5)…. After the last try: Flux sent this diagram back to be fixed 5 times; it still does not draw. One that reads badly is sent back once more.

    Charts:

    {"type": "scatter", "title": "Area against fmax",
 "x": {"label": "MHz"}, "y": {"label": "um2", "log": false},
 "series": [{"name": "sweep", "points": [[800, 30], [1200, 18]]},
            {"loop": "bob/mul8", "x": "fmax_mhz", "y": "area_um2"}]}
    • type: line (default), scatter, bar (x may be a category).
    • An axis may say "better": "lower" (or "higher"): best-so-far step line, or dashed fronts. "goal": 2 draws a dashed line ("≤ 2").
    • Point tags: ["4 @failed", 2.3] hollow, @decision orange ring, @accent, @ok, @warn, @bad ring it.
    • A loop series: loop (owner/loop), y a metric, x design (default) or a metric; optional stage, part. Read live with your rights, drawn as Results draws it. Click a point for Open in Results. An unreadable loop says "owner/loop: not available".
    • Limits: 8 series, 500 points per written series, a loop's newest 5000 designs.
    • Show the source, Copy, Fullscreen, Zoom to an area.
    • An invalid block stays as code with why ("Not a chart: colour is no field of a chart.").

docs.title: Loop chats
docs.text:
The Loops tab lists each loop you can read that has conversations, latest first (loops you may ask about with none yet come after, greyed). Find a loop or a chat filters.

  • Click a loop: ‹ goes back; its conversations are listed like Chats; + starts one.
  • A conversation opens with the loop's name as a tag. It works like a chat, answered by the loop's own Chat: one answer at a time per loop (One answer at a time per loop), reads the loop, changes nothing.
  • Only people with Ask on the loop can ask; others can read. A private conversation (asked by someone without edit) is shown only to its asker.
  • Settings shows the loop (read-only) and, for editors, its Chat workbench.
  • Open in NAME opens the loop's page on that conversation.
  • more: Pin; Delete for editors and for a private conversation's asker. No Rename (the title is the first question).

docs.title: Project chats
docs.text:
A project's own members read its conversations; those who may edit, curate or manage it ask. Someone who sees it only through its group sees none (Groups). The project's Chat button opens one.

  • The Projects tab works like Loops. Inside a project a line shows 12 entries · To review: 3 · 4 loops.
  • The agent reads the project read-only: library, accepted knowledge, topics, and its loops you may ask about. Hidden paths stay hidden. Your own model settings, base network, no web tools; one answer at a time per project.
  • Proposals (Actions): Knowledge (an entry to To review, never straight in), Topic, Library (files from the project's Chat workbench).
  • The project's Chat workbench works like a loop's. An archived project's chats are read-only.

docs.title: Questions
docs.text:
An agent asks only when it cannot go on without you. The question ends the answer as a card.

  • Up to four questions; chips at the top move between them (✓ Type · Widths · Target, 2 of 3).
  • Each has options (one marked Recommended), value fields, and Other for free text.
  • 1–8 pick, Enter moves on, Next › and Back too. Send once something is answered; blank questions are the agent's to decide.
  • You decide lets the agent choose all.
  • Typing a normal message also answers.

The answer goes as one message to the agent that asked:

Answer to: Which adder families should adder16's generator try?
- choice: carry-select
- choice: Kogge-Stone

Answer to: Which cell library?
- choice: sky130
keep it small

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
Agents never change your loops themselves; they propose. Each proposal is a card: what, where, why, a preview. Accept makes it as you (same checks and audit as by hand); Reject drops it. The card then says Done, Rejected or Refused with why.

Kind What it does Its preview Library copies files from your workbench into the loop's library/ (papers, notes its agents read) each file, its size and where it goes; replaces when it overwrites one Document writes a text file (.md, .txt, .rst) under the loop's library/, where its agents read it; a lesson (what a run taught) goes under library/lessons/ the text, or the change to the file it replaces Note sends a note to the running loop, as the Overview's Note to the loop does the note Hidden from AI hides paths from the loop's agents, or shows them again (Hidden from AI) the hidden paths before and after: each still hidden with its lock, one shown again struck through Idea adds an idea to the loop's notebook its title, hypothesis and test Queue queues an idea for testing, or takes it off the queue the idea and its place in line Merge merges ideas that say the same thing, as the notebook's cleanup does (it can be undone) the idea kept and those merged into it Design note pins a note on a design, shown in Results' design detail and in Live's inspector the design, its numbers, the note Reference marks a design as a reference for comparison the design and its numbers Settings changes settings of the loop's problem document -- its budget, who works a box, its model, anything the Configure page sets -- saved as the Configure page saves each setting now and proposed; when it takes effect Problem document replaces the text of the loop's problem document (its flow, checks, measurements), saved as Direct edit saves the change, line by line; when it takes effect Measure again measures a design again (a flaky timeout, a tool that failed), as Results' Reject with Measure again does the design, its numbers, the stages, and when it is measured
  • Design notes and references are for reading only.
  • Settings and Problem document reach a running loop at its next start (Restart). They must still load; a document changed since is refused on Accept. Saving settings drops comments.
  • A design to measure again counts as rejected until measured.
  • Files the agent brings (a downloaded paper) go to your workbench first.
  • A proposal copying a file the loop hides from its agents is refused, naming the file.
  • Checked when the answer ends and again on Accept: you must own the loop or have Edit; not archived. At most 10 proposals per answer.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
The panel's Uses:

Switch On Loops The agent may read your loops: your own, and those shared with you with Ask. The line says how many. Workbench The agent may read and write your workbench. Network The agent may reach the hosts the admin allows for chat, or any host when the admin opens it. Off, it has the sandbox's base allowlist only, which agents need to work. The line says which. On, FluxAgent also has its web tools.
  • A new chat: Workbench on, Loops and Network off. Make these my defaults changes that. A switch the admin keeps off is greyed with why.
  • Each answer uses the switches as they were when sent.
  • Workbench is shown only with the Internals permission; for others it is on, unseen.
  • In focus (with Loops): one loop the answers look at closely.
  • A loop's chat has no switches: its loop read-only, base network, no web tools.
  • The panel remembers open or closed. Under ~1360 px it opens over the conversation.

docs.title: On the web
docs.text:
With Network on, FluxAgent has web tools:

Tool What it does Fetch Gets a page or a document over HTTP or HTTPS and reads its text: HTML, PDF, EPUB, Office files, plain text. A PDF or other document is saved whole. Paper search Searches arXiv and OpenAlex. Each paper comes with its title, authors, year, venue, the start of its abstract, its DOI and an open-access PDF's address when known. Web search Searches the web, only when the admin set a search provider (Admin › Runtime › Chat).
  • Only hosts the admin allows (or any public host); never private addresses. Paper search needs export.arxiv.org and api.openalex.org.
  • Saved files go to the workbench's uploads/ (never overwritten: paper-2.pdf). To add one to a loop's library, the agent proposes it.
  • Only search words go out, never your data. The answer cites addresses.
  • Thinking & commands shows each fetch; the audit records hosts.
  • Coding agents use their own web tools within the chat's network.

docs.title: The workbench
docs.text:
One folder for all your chats: tools/, notes/, drafts/, uploads/. Chat does not create or run loops; drafts for one wait in drafts/ (start a loop from New loop).

  • Settings › Workbench shows a tree. Files open read-only with Download, Delete, Fullscreen. Refresh reloads (also after each answer).
  • Each answer lists the files it wrote. One another chat may have written meanwhile is dimmed, changed meanwhile.
  • A path an answer names (/workbench/notes/speed.md, notes/speed.md) becomes a link if the file exists.

docs.title: A loop's Chat workbench
docs.text:
A loop's chats share one Chat workbench, separate from the loop's own workbench/ (the loop's runs never see it).

  • For editors only (owner, Edit, admins) with the admin's Workbench allowed. Others' answers get none, and their attached files stay with the answer.
  • Without the Internals permission there is no tree to browse, but answers still use it.
  • It moves, is renamed and is deleted with the loop; deleting a conversation or resetting the loop keeps it.
  • A project's Chat workbench is the same, kept apart from its library and knowledge.

docs.title: Share
docs.text:
Share (first tool of a conversation's head) makes a read-only link.

  • What it shows: the whole conversation, or one answer.
  • Who can open it: signed in to this Flux, or anyone with the link.
  • Expires: 1, 7 (default), 30 or 90 days; never only for signed-in links. Anyone-links last at most the admin's limit (90 days unless Admin › Runtime › Chat › Sharing says less).
  • Make link, Copy, Revoke. Account › Shared links lists all.

The page is live: it shows answers written after the link was made. Workbench pictures in answers are shown; other workbench and attached files appear by name, not shared. Never shared: workbench, attachments, Thinking & commands, proposals, the loop, library, settings.

  • A loop's conversation needs the Share right; the link shows only your questions ("1 question of another person is not shared").
  • A conversation quoting a file hidden from the loop's agents is not shared.
  • A broken link (revoked, expired, deleted, right lost) shows This link does not open. A signed-in link without a session goes through sign-in.
  • Search engines are asked not to index it.

docs.title: Files and settings
docs.text: A loop's Files tab browses its folder; Settings holds its preferences and its problem.

docs.title: Files
docs.text: Four views, each with a count: Workbench, Library, Inputs, All files. On a phone a file opens on its own, with ‹ Back.

docs.title: Workbench
docs.text:
The agents' own folder, workbench/. Only for people with the Internals permission (Admin › People › Users); for others it is hidden and left out of a Full export.

  • A search over names and first lines.
  • Overview: workbench/README.md, opened first.
  • Tools: five shown, "+N" for more.
  • Notes by age: Today, Yesterday, This week, Earlier (folded).
  • Numbered notes: three or more files of one name and a number (draft1297-…) folded into one row.
  • Other: the rest.

Files open in the same viewer as All files.

docs.title: Library
docs.text:
What the agents can read: the loop's library/, one row per document (kind, title, size), ✓ digested, or not relevant when its digest says so.

  • N of M digested, a search, ↻ (read again), {} (show digests).
  • + Add a document: files go to library/, a folder to library/<folder>/, a single .zip is unpacked.
  • Each linked project's library follows, read-only (a lock), at library/<project>@<group>/.
  • Also digested: digests of other files (notes, knowledge files) and of files now gone.
  • Delete digest (the bin; needs Edit; audited). The group head deletes digests of missing files (Delete N digests). A digest of a file still there is made again at the next read.
  • Opening a document shows Download, Raw, Actions, its Digest and Outline (as the agents read it).

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Everything else the loop was given:

  • In the problem: files and folders the document names (golden model, command files, library entries);
  • Skills: skills/ or the document's skills folder;
  • Other.

A lock marks hidden files. The foot links to Settings › Problem.

docs.title: Large folders
docs.text:
• A big workbench folder is one row (data/, 12345 files, newest change).
  • Lists show the newest and count the rest ("102 more · All files").
  • Not walked: links, other mounted file systems, dot folders, __pycache__, .gitignored paths.
  • All files loads a big folder as you scroll ("100 of 12345 entries").
  • The configurator's Files and Library folds big folders too; library/, skills/ and skill folders are never folded.

docs.title: All files
docs.text:
The folder as it is: the document, scripts, library/, workbench, out/, runs/.

  • Open a file to view, edit, save or download; Raw and Fullscreen show it whole.
  • Upload: drop files or folders, or use Files (upload arrow) and Folder (folder with a plus).
  • Actions: Rename, Move, Delete, Hide from AI / Show to AI (edits knowledge.hidden; Hidden from AI). Hidden items show a lock; hover says hidden from AI or what hides it.
  • A name with @ at the top of library/ is refused (reserved for project libraries).
  • Linked projects' libraries appear under library/, marked project · read-only. Change them on the project's page.
  • .gitignored files are hidden; .gitignore'd and dot files lists them greyed.
  • Images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP) are shown; SVG stays text. PDFs open in the browser's viewer (Firefox inline; Chrome, Edge and phones get Open and Download).

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Two parts: Preferences and Problem.

docs.title: Preferences
docs.text:
• Measurements: per metric: shown, main (in lists and summaries), shown as change from the baseline. Charts and the decision always use every measurement.
  • Environment variables: the loop's own, over its projects' (Groups › Variables), your account's and the server's. Applied at the next start.
  • Sharing: a grid of who has which words (the words).
    • Rows: Owner (fixed), then each user or group shared with.
    • Level: Viewer, Asker, Contributor, Maintainer, or Custom.
    • Words: view (always on), ask (chat about it), edit (files, document, settings, notes, accept Chat proposals), run (start, stop, restart, re-measure), share.
    • People adds a user or group as Viewer. Ticking a box saves.
    • A sharer who is not the owner can give at most what they hold.
    • Linked projects show read-only rows (via project); ▸ lists their people; Change on the project › edits them.
    • Your rights are your row, your groups' rows and your projects', together. Being in a group with the owner gives nothing.
    • A run started by anyone runs as the owner, on the owner's settings and limits.
  • Projects: the projects the loop is linked into, in order (drag, or the chevrons). The order sets the libraries' order. Per row: Learns (may the project learn from runs) and ✕.
    • Add to a project… lists projects where you hold link, and global ones that take loops.
    • Linking gives the project's members their loop words (never share). A global project gives no rights; its learning starts off.
  • Name & ownership: rename (1 to 60 letters, digits, _, -) or transfer. The loop must be stopped with nothing reading it. Everything moves with it; the old address stops working. A transfer drops the admin's overrides, shares and agent tests.
  • Advanced (admins): sandbox on/off; memory, CPU, process and scratch limits (clamped to the server's maximum, Sandbox limits); parallel work; extra hosts; raw TCP/UDP; host folders mounted; extra Nixpkgs or Nixchip packages. Others see a summary line.
  • Maintenance (folded): Clean disk (scratch, old pass folders, sandbox cache), Condense history (log, journal, transcript), Compact and check (records, document).
  • Record (folded): Prune stale records, Prune empty starts, Prune failed designs, Invalidate all, Re-Evaluate (Results). Pending requests show here and on the Overview with Cancel.
  • Archive, reset or delete (loop stopped; cannot be undone):
    • Archive: read-only, disk freed (Archive).
    • Reset: clears what runs generated; you choose what to keep (workbench, results and history, caches). Document, files and settings stay.
    • Delete: removes the loop.

docs.title: Archive
docs.text:
Archive (owner or admin) asks for the loop's name and lists what goes and stays, with sizes.

Kept Deleted The results, out/: designs, measurements, decisions (Results and its exports) The passes' working files The document, your files and the library The tools' whole outputs (Live keeps each one's end) The workbench's notes and tools The sandbox's tool caches and scratch The last start's log, the answer, notes and Chat Work in progress and build folders What Live shows of the past starts The log of the starts before the last
  • Overview, Live, Results, Files and Chat still read it. Edits, starts and resets are refused until Unarchive.
  • Archived loops show under the Archived chip; search and links still find them.
  • Clean-ups skip them. A start after Unarchive rebuilds scratch.

docs.title: Export and import
docs.text:
Export (owner, editors, admin) writes one .zip, for this or another Flux:

Loop only Full The problem document, your files, lib/, skills/, the library yes yes Hidden files (listed in the file's manifest) yes yes The results, out/: designs, measurements, decisions, ideas yes The workbench's notes and tools (no build folders), the answer, the notes yes
  • Never exported: variables and secrets, credentials, agent instructions, shares, rights, project libraries, Chat conversations, Live history, agent working files, tool outputs, caches, logs, links, repositories.
  • The file starts with a manifest: kind, maker, server, date, documents, hidden paths, command count, sizes. Audited ("loop exported").

Import replaces this loop's contents (loop stopped).

  1. Pick the file. Its manifest shows, with what will be replaced ("This replaces x's document, files and library, and its results: 12 designs are replaced by 40 designs.").
  2. Replace. A Full file also brings its record, workbench, answer and notes.

  3. A Loop only file clears existing results unless you tick Keep the current results.

  4. The loop keeps its name, id, owner, shares, projects, variables, settings, Chat and run history.

  5. The Overview says "Replaced from x.full.zip, made by ada@host, date, Full"; an editor can clear it (×). Audited ("loop replaced").
  6. Nothing runs on import.
  7. Refused, changing nothing: files before Nov 12, 2026 (names the Flux to convert it with), a document with old box names (generate:, orchestrate:, ...) or params: (convert in Flux fdfd1faf0, Server › Old data), files from a newer Flux ("update this server first").
  8. Limits (admin settings): loop_import_max (2 GB file), loop_import_unpacked_max (16 GB unpacked).

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
Viewers without edit see the configurator's steps beside the document, read-only.

  • Configurator: the document in six steps (try it in the Preview's Create a loop guide). See below.
  • Direct edit: the YAML, saved with its diff. A document that does not load is flagged before saving.
  • Agent: describe a change; an agent revises a copy and shows the diff (not while running).
  • Check: checks the document (ready or not, refusals, missing files, checks, stages, objectives, tools, model), as Start does; it runs no design. Full output under Details.
  • Several problems (problem.yaml and each top-level NAME.problem.yaml; foo.yaml is an input): a menu picks which one to edit (settings/problem/edit?doc=fast.problem.yaml). One that does not load is red and opens in Direct edit. Which problem runs is picked in Start.

docs.title: The configurator
docs.text:
• Save shows a diff. What the form cannot express is kept as written, greyed at the end of the document, and listed on Save. Keys the loader ignores (a misspelled timout_s) are kept for you to fix.
  • Save counts the document as checked once Check passed on these files, or a start ran.
  • Steps are cards of rows: label, then box or menu; a greyed value is the default. The line at the step's foot explains the focused setting.
  • Prompt: name, design file, what to make, rules, Files.
  • Check & Measure: Checks and Measurements cards.
  • Objective: how designs are compared, then the numbers.
  • Extra: Parameters, Running, Resources (folded cards; one off its default opens).
  • Graph: the loop's boxes. Left of the ring, Setup (Plan, Baseline) and Knowledge (Skills, Library, Workbench, Insights, Ideas, Notes, Hidden). Solid outline: on; dashed: off. An AI pill marks FluxAgent or an agent at work.

A box's panel starts with By: off (where allowed), agent, or the box's own kind (rules, script, files, goals).

  • With agent: an Agent menu (FluxAgent, then the server's agents), Thinking and effort. An agent the server does not offer shows (not available), and the loop will not start until fixed.
  • A coding agent's options fold under <agent> · options: Questions, Wait, Time limit and last turn, May time out, Session.
  • Session: one per pass (default) or one per loop (with turns, or Until stopped: turns: forever). Design's: one per design, warm start (default; Study time in minutes, seed_timeout_s), one per design, cold start (session: fresh), or one per loop.
  • Design's Probe card: on/off, which gate checks, gate and measure runs.
  • Search's Policy card: Policy, then Search (an algorithm or AI) and its settings.
  • Limits (folded): prototype limits, FluxAgent's tool turns.
  • Check and Measure link to where their commands are set. Choose's By is goals or agent (breaks ties).
  • Knowledge bubbles: Skills on/off and list; Library off or who sums up papers; Workbench off or who sums it up; Insights off, agent or rules; Ideas off or who cleans up; Notes on/off; Hidden paths.
  • A dot marks a value the document sets.

Issues (what Check and Direct edit report: an error stops the loop, a warning is an ignored key) show where they are set:

  • the rail counts them ("● 1 error · 1 warning"; Save: "1 to fix · 2 warnings");
  • the Graph box wears the mark and shows the value as written (codx);
  • the panel outlines the setting with plain words, "Did you mean X?", a fix (Use codex, Remove) and Open line N. A fix is written to the file (refused if it changed meanwhile).

docs.title: Groups
docs.text:
Groups (top bar) shows your teams: members, what membership gives, whose settings runs use, and each group's projects. Admins create groups in Admin › People › Groups (Server and admin).

A group is like an organisation; a project is like one of its repositories, with its own members. Loops are linked into projects.

docs.title: A group's page
docs.text:
The head: the group's name with ▾ (switch group, or Global), its facts ("12 members · 5 projects · open projects give Asker"), and You: level. The address keeps the group (#/groups/<id>, #/groups/global).

Tab Address What it shows Overview #/groups/<id> Projects (title, address <group>/<name>, invite only or open · level, your level, e.g. "Asker + curate"); New project for members who may create; People; Your access (your level and what it gives); Agents summary for admins and managers Members #/groups/<id>/members Names and levels; the member grid for managers Agents #/groups/<id>/agents Admins and managers: the group's agent settings and own agents (A group's agents), and its Schedule (A group's schedule) Machines #/groups/<id>/machines Admins and managers: the group's machines; + Add machine, labels, Rename, Drain/Resume, Rotate keys, Revoke; Allow parallel work on our machines (on by default; Machines)

members, agents and machines cannot be project names. An older project with one of those names keeps it; that tab is then at #/groups/<id>?tab=members.

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
Level Gives Member Nothing extra Maintainer curate, create Lead curate, manage, create
  • Group membership gives nothing on any loop. A loop is reached when its owner shares it, or links it into a project you are in (or one open to the group).
  • A Lead adds people (People; they join as Member), removes anyone but themselves (×), and gives levels and words up to their own. Admins give any.
  • Others see names and levels, read-only. Nobody leaves a group here.

docs.title: New project
docs.text: New project: a Title and a Name (letters, digits, -, _, at most 60; not members or agents; unique in the group regardless of case). Create project makes <group>/<name>, blank and invite only, with you as Lead.

docs.title: A project's page
docs.text:
Address: #/groups/<group id>/<name> (global: #/groups/global/<name>). Old #/projects/<group>/<name> links still open it.

Head: group ▾ / title ▾ (switch group or project; + New project), its access (Invite only, Group views, Open; global: Public or Private), Chat (Project chats), You: level, and Leave for members.

Tabs: Overview, Files (Library, Skills), Knowledge, Variables, Settings (only for those who may change something). Files, Knowledge, Variables and Chat are for its own members and admins (below).

Overview What it shows Loops · N Linked loops you may see: owner / name, state, design agent, last active; for your own, its place in the loop's project order ("1st of its 3"). + Link one of my loops with the link role; the cross unlinks (the loop stays). A global project lists only your loops (all for admins and managers), with whether each learns People · N Members and levels; Manage › opens Settings Library File count and size; Open › Your access Your words and how you have them

Words on a project: view, ask, edit, run (on every linked loop), then link (link your loops), curate (review knowledge, keep the library), manage (title, members, access; rename, archive, delete). Each implies view. Words only add up. A global project's members hold only curate or manage; its visibility gives view.

Access for the group's members (set by the project's managers, the group's managers, admins):

  • Invite only (default): hidden until you are added.
  • Group views: members view it and its loops.
  • Open to the group: every member gets its Level for open (Viewer, Asker, Contributor or Maintainer).

There is no joining; anyone may leave.

docs.title: Its contents are its members'
docs.text:
A project's files (Library, Skills), knowledge, variables and chats are for its own members and admins only. A group member who is not on the project's list (via Group views, Open to the group, or curate/manage on the group) sees the project, its people and its loops, but not those tabs: "You see that this project exists. Ask its managers to add people." Group managers can add themselves.

A linked loop reads the project's library, skills and knowledge only while its owner is a member who views it.

docs.title: Library
docs.text:
Files › Library: papers, specs and notes for the project's loops. Same browser as a loop's Files: upload (Files, Folder, drop; a .zip is unpacked), Rename, Move, Delete.

  • Limit: the project's own, else the server's (both in Admin › People › Projects), else 8 GB and 100,000 files. Shown as "1.2 GB of 5 GB". Over-limit changes are refused.
  • Every linked loop reads it read-only at library/<name>@<group>/ (library/<name>@_/ for a global project). Archived projects are read by no loop.
Who May Its members who view it (any word; everyone for a public global project) and admins -- never through its group browse and download edit, curate or manage on it as its member (a global project's members with curate or manage) upload, rename, move, delete, edit a text file manage as its member (its managers, admins) Hide from AI / Show to AI: the paths the agents of its loops will not see (under its place, library/<name>@<group>/drafts/)

Archived: read-only. Every change is audited.

docs.title: Skills
docs.text: Files › Skills: the project's skills/ folder, a folder per skill with a SKILL.md (Skills). Same people and browser as the library. Linked loops get them read-only at skills/<name>@<group>/.

docs.title: Knowledge
docs.text:
Short entries, each one insight, filed under topics and proven by designs of the project's loops.

  • Accepted entries reach linked loops at their next start, read with the library (Knowledge). Proposals, rejected and retired entries never do.
  • Entries come from people (+ Add), the collector, and project chats (Project chats); the last two go to To review.
  • A line shows use: "Read by 2 of 3 linked loops this week, 14 times".
  • Chips: All, one per topic, To review (curators), + Add.
  • A row: headline, two lines of analysis, topic, backing ("✓ maria · 2 designs", "+1" reinforced today).
  • Opened: the analysis (#142 links to the design), Designs (rank "top 1 of 61", day, source), Ideas ("in 3 loops' ideas · tried 2 · won 1"; each accepted entry is an idea in every linked loop), who accepted it, and the toolbar: Reinforce, Pin, Merge, Edit, Retire.
Who May Its members who view it (and admins; never through its group) read the list; their own proposals, marked in review edit, curate or manage + Add an entry (topic, one-line insight, analysis citing #142, at least one design); Reinforce with another design; write the Topics curate as its member To review: edit, ✓ accept, ✕ reject, Merge into; Edit, Retire, Pin, Merge listed entries
  • Proof is enough with designs from 2 different loops (backed by N loops). A curator's ✓ on less proof ticks it ("✓ maria").
  • A curator's own entry goes straight in (on a global project another curator accepts it).
  • A proposal may say contradicts: headline.
  • Merge keeps one entry and folds others into it; Unmerge restores them.
  • Pin puts an entry first (also in what the agents read).
  • Stale: Flux marks entries whose evidence faded; ✓ retires, ✕ keeps. Nothing retires by itself.
  • Everything is kept and audited. Archived: read-only.

docs.title: The collector
docs.text:
With a link's learning on (default in a group's project; in a global one a manager or admin turns it on, and the loop's owner may turn it off), Flux reads linked loops' best designs once they change and writes proposals. Nothing in the loop changes. Billed to the loop owner's FluxAgent as knowledge collector (Admin › Activity › Usage).

It finds What happens The new designs work by an accepted entry's mechanism They reinforce it at once, no review: "+ … collected from nlu-gelu, reinforced" They work by the mechanism of a proposal in review They join its designs: the proposal stays in To review, now backed by that loop too A new insight A proposal in To review, "collected from nlu-gelu" They contradict an entry A proposal marked contradicts: its headline, and on the entry a mark like 1 of 4 loops disagrees until a curator rejects that proposal; opened, the entry lists those designs under Against An entry is superseded or shown wrong A proposal retire: its headline, with the reason: ✓ retires the entry, ✕ keeps it. Nothing is retired by itself

Collect now (managers, admins) lists the linked loops with their state (top designs unread, nothing new, learning off, no measured designs, not linked, ...).

  • Untick loops to skip. Archived loops are listed unticked; their records are only read.
  • Read designs again, even those already read: reads the top 5 regardless.
  • One model call per loop, in the background (Collecting 2 of 7…); audited.
  • A loop whose owner is not a project member is listed its owner is not a member: on your model: read only on Collect now, on your model, if you can view the loop.
  • Compare loops: finds what ticked loops share; one call per topic (~10-20k tokens), on your model, billed as knowledge compare. Needs two loops.
  • Last collected: nlu-gelu · Oct 23 · 2 proposed, 1 reinforced; Runs lists every run.

docs.title: Suggestions
docs.text: Off until a curator turns them on (Settings › Suggestions). Suggest on a proposal asks a model for one move (accept, reject, merge, a better headline) with why; Apply does it. Never automatic. Runs on the pressing curator's FluxAgent. Also as each proposal arrives, on my model suggests automatically on that curator's model. Audited ("knowledge suggest"); usage as knowledge suggestions.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
The project's environment variables: name, value, secret (stored encrypted, shown as secret · set), bin, Add. Names: letters, digits, _; Flux's and the sandbox's own (FLUX_SANDBOX…, PATH, HOME, model settings) are refused.

Each linked loop reads them at its next start, in every process. Later wins:

  1. the server's (Admin › Runtime › Agents › All agents),
  2. the loop owner's (Account),
  3. each project, in the loop's order (the first project wins over later ones),

  4. the loop's own (Settings › Variables).

  5. Only while the project is unarchived and the owner is a member who views it.

  6. The loop's settings list them as from project / </em>, <strong>overridden</strong> when beaten.</li> <li>A secret reaches every linked loop's processes.</li> </ol> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Who</th> <th>May</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td>Its members who <strong>view</strong> it (any word; everyone for a public global project) and admins -- never through its group</td> <td>the names and the plain values</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>edit</strong> or <strong>manage</strong> on it as its member (a global project's managers), admins</td> <td>add, change and remove them -- not while it is archived</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>Audited by name, never value. Kept across a rename; deleted with the project.</p> <h3 id="settings">Settings<a class="headerlink" href="#settings" title="Permanent link">¶</a></h3> <p>For managers and admins:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Members & access</strong>: the member grid (<a href="../admin/#the-words">the words</a>), <strong>All members</strong>, <strong>People</strong>, the group's access and <strong>Level for open</strong>.</li> <li><strong>About</strong>: title and description.</li> <li><strong>Name</strong> / <strong>Rename</strong>: no redirect; members and linked loops' owners are told. Refused while a linked loop runs.</li> <li><strong>Archive</strong> / <strong>Unarchive</strong>, <strong>Delete</strong> (type its name; loops stay, unlinked).</li> <li>Global projects (admins): <strong>Visibility</strong> (<strong>Public</strong> or <strong>Private</strong>) and who may link loops.</li> <li><strong>Topics</strong> (editors too): id (lower-case letters, digits, <code>-</code>, <code>_</code>) and question; <strong>{ }</strong> shows <code>knowledge.yaml</code> (<code>pipelining: Where do pipeline stages pay off, and what do they cost?</code>). A topic with entries cannot be removed.</li> </ul> <h2 id="global">Global<a class="headerlink" href="#global" title="Permanent link">¶</a></h2> <p><strong>Global</strong> lists public global projects and private ones you belong to.</p> <ul> <li>Only admins create them: <strong>New global project</strong> in <strong>Admin › People › Projects</strong> (public, or private).</li> <li>Anyone may link a loop into a public one; a private one's members into it.</li> <li>Linking gives nobody rights on the loop; you see only your own loops in it.</li> <li>Learning is off until an admin or manager turns it on.</li> </ul> <h2 id="in-no-group">In no group<a class="headerlink" href="#in-no-group" title="Permanent link">¶</a></h2> <p>You see an explanation, <strong>Global</strong>, and your loops under <strong>Loops</strong>.</p> <h2 id="admins">Admins<a class="headerlink" href="#admins" title="Permanent link">¶</a></h2> <p>An admin's <strong>▾</strong> lists every group ("not a member" where so). Admins set any level, add and remove members, make projects, and see every group's <strong>Agents</strong> and <strong>Machines</strong> tabs. <strong>Every group in Admin › People › Groups</strong> opens the admin page.</p>

docs.title: Live
docs.text: A loop's Live tab shows its run task by task as it happens, and replays earlier starts. Two views: Graph (default) and Timeline (live/timeline). Old live/tree and live/log addresses open the Graph; the start's log is in Files, and on the Overview's Log when a run stopped on an error.

docs.title: The toolbar
docs.text:
• Start: which start to show: the running one or an older one (latest 50; Earlier for more).
  • Follow: keep the latest work in view. Scrolling, zooming or selecting stops it; press again to resume.
  • The head: All passes and its counts (tasks, done, failed, retried).
  • With pipelining off and three passes or more, a hint may say "Pipelining could make passes about 24% shorter: Settings › Problem › Extra › Pipelining." (shown at 10% or more).

docs.title: Graph
docs.text:
One pass as the loop's boxes: Search, Design, Check, Measure, Choose, and any critic.

  • Each box says its setting, ✓ or ✗, and ×N when it ran again. Skipped boxes are dashed.
  • A design of several tries has a bar per try: ✓, ! (not built) or ✗.
  • Pass chain above: a bubble per pass, coloured by outcome (Pass 4 shown). Click one to draw it. … expands every pass; Less folds them.
  • Ideas: a pass testing a queued idea skips search; Search says queued idea, and the inspector links to Results › Ideas. A design that takes a suggested idea says suggested idea.
  • Check and Measure have a bar per step (check or stage), not per run. The tooltip sums its runs (check unit: 9 of 11 passed, 1 failed, 1 running); a click opens the latest. A stage not reached yet is grey (measurement perf: waiting), hollow once the pass is over (not reached).
  • Design opens the agent's draft and conversation. Its Rationale lists the key changes and why.
  • Many designs at once (a re-check, several per pass): one row per design, a dot per check or stage (✓ #214 ●●●●, ✓ #246 ●● 24m 07s). Dots: green done, red failed, blue running, grey waiting, hollow never reached. The latest five show ("34 earlier designs" folded). Click a row for its checks or stages, then each for its command, exit and output.
  • A stage that exits non-zero is a failed measurement (red dot, ✗).
  • Standing design measured again: after a pass, the standing design is measured on the same stage to compare fairly.
